📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Last night, The Game Awards 2026 nominations were officially announced, and fans immediately noticed the prestigious Game of the Year category - previously won by the likes of Astro Bot, Clair Obscur, and Elden Ring - does not feature a PlayStation-published game this year. It's a rare sight for PlayStation Studios, which has secured a Game of the Year nomination every year since 2015.

PlayStation has published several games this year that might usually be shoe-ins for a Game of the Year nomination. Marvel's Wolverine is the company's highest profile first-party release in 2026, but it's also responsible for this year's Saros, as well as the externally-developed but PlayStation-published Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls.

According to recent reports, despite missing out on the Game of the Year slot, however, PlayStation still features in other categories. All three of the aforementioned games are up for various, non-GOTY awards, while Marathon is nominated for Best Multiplayer, and the upcoming God of War Laufey for Most Anticipated. Here's all of PlayStation's 2026 nominations:.

And if you're wondering, here are the 13 Game of the Year nominations PlayStation has secured over the last 11 years:.

2027's PlayStation slate of games might fare better at next year's The Game Awards, what with a new entry in the often-nominated God of War series in Laufey, and potentially Naughty Dog's Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Heartopia has kicked off a latest event to celebrate passing 30 million downloads. Just a couple of weeks after delivering the vintage Hollywood-themed Dreamlight Cinematics event, developer XD Games has revealed The Whimsical Tea Party, a limited-time Gilded Acorn Exhibition.

The event kicked off on Saturday, bringing some latest themed content to the game.

Recent findings suggest that whimsical Tea Party’s biggest addition are the upcoming outfits, including the Wandering Traveler, and the Duke Bunny outfits. Each outfit is available in three different colours. Another thing Heartopia events bring are building materials sets.

This one adds the Labyrinth furniture building materials set, the Hedgehog & Flamingo mallet, and the Cheshire Cat pet costume. Speaking of outfits, XD Games is dropping the in-game prices for a number of items permanently.

All original pet outfits now cost 66.7% less. Those of the Common variety will now cost 10 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, instead of the previous 30. Rare pet outfits will cost 5 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, down from 15.

Keeping with the theme of freebies, Heartopia is also celebrating surpassing 30 million downloads worldwide by giving all players a small gift package in-game. This freebie is available until May 29, so you should have enough time to claim it.

For comprehensive guidance on where to find birds, bugs, and fish, check out our Heartopia bird locations, Heartopia bug locations, and Heartopia fish locations guides. If you’re instead looking to find some wild vegetables for those cooking recipes, hit those links. And, as ever, it doesn’t hurt to see if you missed out on any Heartopia codes.

Sony defeat $2.6 billion UK class action lawsuit which argued PlayStation's dominant market position fuels "excessive and unfair" game prices

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (463 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, it's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony.
  • As reported by Reuters and The Game Business, the body ruled that the lawsuit - brought by Alex Neill on behalf of folks who bought digital games on PlayStation between August 2016 and February 2026 - failed to establish that Sony had infringed competition law.
  • The lawsuit claimed that PlayStation's dominant position when it comes to selling digital games on its platforms via the PlayStation Store subjected consumers to "excessive and unfair prices", as a result of terms and a 30% commission fee levied against developers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, it's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony. A UK class action lawsuit which accused the company of using the PlayStation Store's dominant market position to fuel "excessive and unfair" prices for digital games has been dismissed in its entirety by the Competition Appeal Tribunal in London.

As reported by Reuters and The Game Business, the body ruled that the lawsuit - brought by Alex Neill on behalf of folks who bought digital games on PlayStation between August 2016 and February 2026 - failed to establish that Sony had infringed competition law.

The lawsuit claimed that PlayStation's dominant position when it comes to selling digital games on its platforms via the PlayStation Store subjected consumers to "excessive and unfair prices", as a result of terms and a 30% commission fee levied against developers. Neill and co argued owning a PlayStation traps game buyers within a competitionless ecosystem, thereby impacting their ability to seek out a better deal.

It's quite similar to the arguments which have been made against Valve in similar lawsuits concerning the Steam overlords' dominance over the PC game buying space, though a key distinction is that there is some competition on PC via the likes of the Epic store and GOG. How effective some of that competition can be in practice is a different kettle of fish, but the options are there.

Recent findings suggest that in a judgement that could potentially factor into the responses to any similar lawsuits against Valve or other PC storefronts going forwards, the tribunal ruled that Sony compete in a wider ‘systems market’ against Xbox, Nintendo and PC, with PlayStation having no legal duty under competition law to allow third-party stores onto their platform as competition closer to home. The latter the tribunal noted would be expensive, complex and come with potential security ramifications.

As if that wasn't enough, the body ruled that as far as the pricing being unfair went, Neill hadn't proven that Sony’s profit margins were excessive and declared there was no evidence the presence of rival storefronts on PlayStation would've seen prices come down. That's essentially the word NO written in the largest font possible on a sheet of paper the size of a table, then.

Every lawsuit's different, especially when filed in different countries, but if I was one of the other class action suits against Sony or another major game seller on the go at the moment, I'd maybe not be feeling so hot right now. On the other hand, perhaps seeing what the tribunal judged Neill not to have provided suffiencient evidence for might aid those other efforts in formulating their arguments ready to face the scrutiny of government bodies and corporate law-talkers.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • HoYoverse just wrapped up a stacked Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, delivering the one-two punch of revealing the game’s next major enhancement, and detailing what you can expect from its third anniversary celebrations.
  • First off, Version 4.2, dubbed So Laughed the Masses, arrives April 22, making two characters playable, and bringing back a host of beloved characters for re-runs.
  • The major inciting incident of this new chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse just wrapped up a stacked Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, delivering the one-two punch of revealing the game’s next major enhancement, and detailing what you can expect from its third anniversary celebrations.

First off, Version 4.2, dubbed So Laughed the Masses, arrives April 22, making two characters playable, and bringing back a host of beloved characters for re-runs. The latest revision continues the Phantasmoon Games arc, as the story takes an especially suspect new development.

The major inciting incident of this new chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Meanwhile, Fulwish has invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV HQ to announce their intention to host a TV debate about the ultimate goal of the Phantasmoon Games.

Naturally, you’re invited, and you’ll have to overcome the challenges that await to gather more Wishpower.

Industry observers note that our first fresh arrival is Silver Wolf LV.999, with whom you should already be familiar from her Version 1 form. The difference now, of course, is that she’s getting a brand-new alternate kit, since — true to her new name — she's evolved into a Godmode Player upon reaching Level 999. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-Star Imaginary character on the Path of Elation.

Her main combat trick is the ability to rack up Hidden MMR, which is what allows her to eventually activate her Cartridge and settle into the aforementioned Godmode state. While in that form, she shifts the entire battle into the virtual world, pulling in both teams into her gaming domain.

This is essentially a world under her control, which is why she can unlock a Reward Stage at the start of her turn, which lets her spawn in-game items. When picked up, these items can turn the tide of battle.

In a recent development, keeping up with the ultra-gamer persona, Silver Wolf's Aha Instant strike blasts all enemies with a laser cannon, dealing massive damage. Perhaps her most interesting ability is being able to hack into the battlefield when she’s not actively on the team, something she can do when a teammate falls under enemy control.

It has been revealed that evanescia is the other newly-playable character, who has thus far only been an observer of the Phantasmoon Games, as well as one of the most prominent upcoming characters we've met so far on Planarcadia. V4.2 sees the girl join the roster as a 5-Star Physical character who’s likewise on the Path of Elation. As she fights, she always accumulates Certified Banger, when she earns the title she’s able to simultaneously regenerate Energy and maintain her damage.

Industry observers note that evanescia’s damage continues to increase the more Certified Banger she accumulates, triggering an attack from Master Fox upon reaching a certain threshold, which deals damage to all enemies and regenerates Energy for herself. Her Elation Skill adds a bit of a performance to her kit, and is capable of hitting all enemies.

You may have noticed the Path of Elation theme in this one, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the Elation Trailblazer variant on the main playable character is also joining the team in 4.2. There’s a latest weapon that starts off as a glow stick but can transform into a lightblade as you deal damage, and, yes, gain Certified Banger.

It can also turn into nunchucks, which delivers a unique flurry of attacks on all enemies surrounding the character, dealing multiple instances of damage. You can also use it to cheer for a teammate, hyping them up.

Industry observers note that version 4.2 Warp Events will bring back six characters. The first half will see reruns of The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly. The second half will give you another shot at unlocking Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao. What’s more, four of the game’s characters will be buffed in this patch, so you may want to reconsider putting them them back on your team. They are Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt.

As part of the same update, you can expect the debut of the Cosmic Data Roaming event, which goes live alongside the anniversary celebrations. The event lets you live the life of a streamer.

Currency Wars is getting a big expansion, too. Likewise, the Cosmicon Collective is getting its version 2.0 upgrade, adding upcoming decks, dice as well as a new team challenge game mode.

In a recent development, elsewhere, you’ll find fresh items in the Gift of Stardust Store, including a new outfit for Castorice. Between the time 4.2 launches and when the celebrations begin, you’ll be able to try your luck in Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere, an online event where you can leave a message for a chance to win various prizes.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that upsettingly, it is that time of the week again, as Take-Two are laying off staff at Firaxis, the developer behind Civilization and XCOM, only a little over a year the last time the studio suffered from layoffs.
  • Word of the layoffs came from Bloomberg, who report that about 60 people are losing their jobs, apparently roughly a third of its staff.
  • It has been revealed that "As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis.

Industry observers note that upsettingly, it is that time of the week again, as Take-Two are laying off staff at Firaxis, the developer behind Civilization and XCOM, only a little over a year the last time the studio suffered from layoffs. Firaxis are, notably, owned by Take-Two, the publisher of GTA 6 which comes out in, oh, two days time? Interesting timing, 'ey.

Word of the layoffs came from Bloomberg, who report that about 60 people are losing their jobs, apparently roughly a third of its staff. The studio's head, Heather Hazen, is also leaving. A spokesperson for 2K Games (the Take-Two label that manages Firaxis) shared a statement on the layoffs: "Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength - designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years.

It has been revealed that "As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis." I don't feel personally confident in the idea that the only way to make a firm succeed is by laying a bunch of people off thereby making it much harder to make anything in the first place, especially in the lead-up to what will likely be the best selling game of the decade, but what do I know!

Bloomberg also report Firaxis have been working on a new XCOM, which is yet to be announced, but the project has apparently had to contend with numerous development concerns, missing a "significant milestone over the summer." This new XCOM game hasn't been cancelled at the very least, but anonymous sources that spoke with Bloomberg remarked it may have to deal with a shakeup due to the cuts. As always, solidarity with all those affected by this situation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hours before it's even playable in most of the world, Grand Theft Auto 6 has already broken the record for the most viewers across livestreaming platforms like Twitch.

It has been revealed that according to streaming data and analytics website Streams Charts, GTA 6 had amassed 6.38m live viewers across Twitch, YouTube, and Kick at 12:30 UTC today. At that time, the game had been officially available for a few hours in Latest Zealand, and elsewhere by using a region-switch trick.

In a recent development, the previous record for most live viewers was set by Valorant, Riot Game's popular tactical shooter, during its closed beta in xx. That game brought in 1.74m live viewers, but it's worth noting there was a promotion offering players a chance to access the beta if they watched a stream. Despite having no such incentive, GTA 6 has more than tripled Valorant's record.

Twitch is the largest platform for GTA 6 streams according to Streams Charts, and already the game is the 6th biggest category in Twitch history. It's also expected the figure will increase as GTA 6 introduces officially in more regions of the world.

If you'd like to find out when exactly Grand Theft Auto 6 releases for you, check out Eurogamer's GTA 6 launch time guide for an accurate list by country. You can also read the Everything We Know about Grand Theft Auto 6 guide for a full breakdown on all the details ahead of its launch in your region.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Okay, you'll have to stick with me for this one because it's going to take some explaining...

So, all the way back in 2023, a supposed leak on the GTAForums (please beware of potential GTA 6 spoilers if you click this link) attracted relatively little attention. At the time, there was no way to prove that any of it was legit.

The "leak" in question revealed Rockstar's schedule, with the original poster claiming that a sequel to LA Noire would be the developer's next game, after GTA 6, and it was targeting a 2030 release.

The reason it's being brought again almost three years later — chiefly via Reddit — is because as it turns out, the leaker did get a number of details about GTA 6 correct. Most notably, they managed to provide surprisingly solid info on the game's multiple endings — and they'd obviously be quite difficult to predict without some kind of insider knowledge.

To be clear, not everything in the "leak" has ended up being correct. It's a little hit and miss, but then things can change in the space of two and a half years or so; it's possible that these inaccurate details were legit at or before the time of posting.

I think the deciding factor for the believers here is that Rockstar moving on to a latest LA Noire would make some sense.

Assuming it's in line with the first game, you would think that it would be a much smaller production than something like Red Dead Redemption 3 — even with the tech and engine refinements the company has made with GTA 6.

Plus, there is some LA Noire DNA in both Red Dead Redemption 2 and GTA 6; environmental and NPC interactions are key parts of Rockstar's most recent releases, and they arguably stem from LA Noire's investigative gameplay loop.

It's also worth remembering that after LA Noire's original developer Team Bondi was closed in 2011 (with Rockstar retaining the rights to LA Noire itself), its founder Brendan McNamara would go on to establish a new outfit called Video Games Deluxe.

The Australian studio crafted LA Noire: The VR Case Files years later, and even took over post-launch support for GTA: The Trilogy following its incredibly shoddy launch. Video Games Deluxe was then acquired by Rockstar in 2025, and it was renamed Rockstar Australia. Hmmm.

Recent findings suggest that so some of this stuff seems to line up — but I don't think there's quite enough evidence here to nail the suspect. I mean, er, put your full trust in that original leak. Still, I wouldn't say no to another LA Noire.

Would you love to see an LA Noire sequel? Feel free to doubt all of this in the comments section below.

[source gtaforums.com, via reddit.com].

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

James Marsden says his Cyclops isn't there for a quick nostalgia hit in Avengers: Doomsday, but something much more substantial.

According to recent reports, "I didn’t want Cyclops to simply appear for a nostalgic cameo and then disappear," Marsden told Sharp Magazine of his belated return as the X-Men icon. "I wanted there to be a genuine purpose behind his presence.".

In a recent development, marsden added, "Without giving anything away, I feel very good about what we were able to do with the character. I haven’t seen the finished film yet, but I think fans will be excited not only to see familiar faces return but also to see that their appearances genuinely matter to the story. There’s real purpose behind Cyclops being there, and that’s what excites me most.".

Marsden also hints that Cyclops will finally step into a more prominent role in the X-Men dynamic after, in the actor's own words, the character "took a back seat to Wolverine" in prior entries. Marsden appeared as Cyclops in only the first trilogy of X-Men movies, meaning it's been over two decades since he fired off a laser blast in angle.

The new Avengers: Doomsday trailer highlights Cyclops' role perfectly – even uttering his iconic catchphrase, "To me, my X-Men" as he's surrounded by various heroes from Marvel's past and present against a backdrop of Sentinels and Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom.

Elsewhere, fresh off the Doomsday trailer, are two substantial fan theories doing the rounds. One notes Steve Rogers is actually Loki in disguise, while the other says Thor loses another body part in the fight against Doom.

Watch Cyclops lead from the front in Avengers: Doomsday, in UK cinemas on December 16 and in the US on December 18.

Industry observers note that animal Crossing: New Horizons has received a surprise patch today to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the life sim series. The enhancement, version 3.0.2, is available across the Switch and Switch 2 versions of the game.

In a recent development, the patch brings a single upcoming addition to New Horizons - a leaf item. Everyone gets it, too, so you don’t have to do anything special to acquire it.

Recent findings suggest that after installing the patch, simply head to your in-house mailbox to claim it. The mail includes a hearty message to fans who supported the series for years, featuring an appropriate Nintendo N64 stamp.

The Leaf Statue, as it’s referred to in-game, lights up when placed.

April 14, 2011 marks the release of the original, lesser-known version of Animal Crossing in Japan. The game was initially released as Animal Forest (Dobutsu no Mori) on the Nintendo N64, before later making its way to the Nintendo GameCube in December of the same year as Dobutsu no Mori+ with some extra features.

Sources indicate that that same, original design of the package is also available for display in your game. The rest of the patch notes are entirely about various bug fixes, so not much more there. You can see the full change log on Nintendo’s support website.

Grand Theft Auto 6 isn't even out yet, and it's already causing some technical problems over at the game's official Reddit page.

Industry observers note that in a post verified by r/GTA6 moderators and pinned to the page, user and moderator PapaXah wrote "GTA 6 broke Reddit", and explained that "many things" were presently busted at the time of the post. Looking through Reddit, many flairs (little labels attached to posts) aren't loading properly and appear as a string of code rather than proper images. Ahead of the game's full launch across the world, the Grand Theft Auto 6 has already broken viewership records across streaming platforms like Twitch and YouTube. Interesting details about the game are also trickling out, including the fact that different refrigerators have their own unique sounds. Video games, ladies and gentlemen.

It has been revealed that with Grand Theft Auto 6 releasing today, our review has been released to the wild with it. It is overwhelmingly positive, with Chris Tapsell dubbing GTA 6 as "the most believable and unbelievable video game world ever made" and rated it a full five stars.

#189277. What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1674 w)

What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1674 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that it's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto.
  • Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption.
  • During the noughties especially, when the most expensive games took considerably less time to make, Rockstar tried their hand at a number of projects besides GTA.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto. Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't GTA 6, which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making, with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial production shadowed by labour disputes, that appears to have given Rockstar's various teams little time or space to think about anything else.

It wasn't ever thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption. Once upon a time, they had a reputation for slightly dodgy experiments. I recently interviewed former Rockstar North tech director Obbe Vermeij about a few of them, including Agent, the unofficial James Bond game Rockstar toyed with before putting all chips on Grand Theft Auto 5.

During the noughties especially, when the most expensive games took considerably less time to make, Rockstar tried their hand at a number of projects besides GTA. There was 2002's Manhunt, a rancid parody of snuff films – not much loved, but sufficiently admired to spawn a sequel in the hands of Rockstar London. There was 2005's adaptation of Walter Hill flick The Warriors - a mouthy Homeric beat 'em up in which you cross New York on foot over the course of a single night - and 2006's Rockstar Presents Table Tennis - an inexplicable pivot towards realistic sports simulation from Rockstar San Diego. Later in 2006 came Bully, aka Canis Canem Edit, a boarding school life sim from Rockstar Vancouver (née Barking Dog Studios). I didn't warm to Bully, myself, but I've never been able to get its sardonic OST out of my head.

In amongst all these, Rockstar weighed up several game projects that never made it out of the building. The aforesaid Agent is perhaps the best-known, but my conversation with Vermeij (who worked at Rockstar from 1995 to 2009) began with "Z", a fleeting attempt to expand into the world of zombie action games, which Rockstar spent a few weeks mulling over in the wake of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. It was set in the islands of Scotland, which would have made it the only Rockstar North project to unfold in the studio's backyard. "I think it was meant to be smaller than GTA, map-wise, and there weren't going to be any deserted cities - it was really just islands and some villages," Vermeij told me. "But it really didn't get that far.".

The pitch for Z couldn't be further from the sweat and glitter of GTA 6's Miami, but the two projects would have shared a taste for 'simulation' elements. "It actually was going to have cars running out of fuel," Vermeij told me. "That was going to be one of the things, and the whole idea was that you'd find cars and they'd only have a little bit of fuel in them." As for why Z never entered full development, turns out desolate North Atlantic archipelagos full of corpses can be a bit of a downer. "Everybody was super excited to do something newly introduced," Vermeij went on. "And then pretty rapidly, we kind of realised that it's really just a depressing version of GTA, and it sort of died.".

Sources indicate that the increasing success of Grand Theft Auto during these years was something of a "curse", Vermeij went on. It meant that a lot of Rockstar's ventures beyond GTA were eventually folded back into the series. "It's very difficult to have a studio and have one mega game, and then do something on the side," he explained. "It's almost impossible, because at any time during the development of the smaller project, management's going to say 'oh! The big project's in trouble. We need more people.' And they're just going to pull everybody from that small team onto the big team, so even if we had progressed with [Z], what would have happened is we would have had to start GTA 4 at the same time, and eventually the small team would just be merged with the big team again.".

Rockstar's Bondalike game Agent got a lot further down the road to release than Z. It was in development for several years following GTA 4's launch, and was touted by co-founder Sam Houser as Rockstar's next megagame. "A lot of work had been done on that," Vermeij recalled. "And then we ended up just cutting and cutting it, because the same thing happened – at some point you kind of go OK, well, we better get on with the next GTA.".

Agent sounds like it could have been a hoot, at least going by Vermeij's description of his own time with the project. It was a relatively linear, level-based action game with a touch of camp. "There was a French ski resort, and there was going to be a Mediterranean town like San Tropez, somewhere like that," Vermeij explained. "There was going to be a North African place, like Morocco or Egypt. The last level was going to be on the moon, with lasers – like Moonraker. There was another one, London or something, I can't remember. But then we just ended up cutting everything down, because what we could see happening was that at some point, we would have to go back to work on GTA. It wasn't close to being finished.".

While never a spoof in the vein of Austin Powers, Agent would have been a sillier production than the grimy and downbeat GTA 4. "It was meant to lean into all the cliches," Vermeij said. "It was like James Bond from the 1970s - there was a girl with white boots. It wasn't a comedy, it was just completely over-the-top cliched.".

As for the choice of a level-based format, this came from a desire for variety the studio couldn't realistically achieve in a GTA-style open world. "If you had to have them all on one map, you would basically have had to model a mini version of Europe," Vermeij said, "So you couldn't do that." Players might have been able to revisit locations containing several missions, which calls to mind Io Interactive's later Hitman: World of Assassination games, to say nothing of their own bash at the Flemingverse, 007 First Light. "I don't how whether it was going to be completely linear, or whether you were always going to be able to visit all those locations." Vermeij said.

Needless to say, Rockstar's Bondalike would have featured chase scenes. Vermeij himself worked on the moving parts. "I remember doing some work on what we called the car recording stuff for GTA," he went on. "So if a level designer wanted to set up a chase scene, they would drive one car, record it, and then play back the recording, drive a second car and record that... and so driving one by one, you could set up a whole chase scene. I did a version of that for [human] characters as well, because for one of the Agent missions in the French ski resort, there was like a chase where the bad guys were on skiis and using their machine guns. So I set up a thing where you'd play them one by one, and then play the whole thing back. There was maybe like five or six bad guys and they'd ski after you, and then it was just up to the player to avoid them.".

Industry observers note that according to Vermeij, Agent never had a defined story during his time with it. It was more of a mix of scenario concepts, "kind of how we used to do games with GTA 3 and Vice City". Mind you, the absence of a nailed-down plot isn't necessarily a sign that Agent was lightyears from being finished. Even at their most byzantine, Bond movie plotlines often feel like an afterthought. "It's like oh yeah, there's a bad guy and there's a thingally-dingally that needs to be captured before the world comes to an end," summarised Vermeij. Still, Agent would spend a long time in limbo after Vermeij left. It's still unclear how much it was in active development before Rockstar's trademark finally evaporated in November 2018.

Industry observers note that one thing I learned while reading up on Rockstar's checkered history was that GTA 3, the game that made GTA a Thing on PlayStation, wasn't deemed an immediate hit at launch. According to Vermeij himself, it was months before Rockstar realised what they'd built. This inspired an obvious closing question: what might Rockstar have done, if GTA 3 hadn't blown up the way it did? Which of those other projects might have become the focus?

"I really have never thought about it," Vermeij pondered. "When Rockstar San Diego joined, it was 2002, and they already had a bunch of games and a bunch of franchises, like Midnight Club and Smuggler's Run. They were already into driving games and city games in that way, so it wouldn't have surprised me if we'd gone in that direction anyway. But then they were more about car modding and decals and stuff like that.

In a recent development, "At Rockstar North, we only had Manhunt and GTA," he went on. "With Manhunt, that team was in development hell for a while, they had a couple of rough years where they got stuck and in the end, they pulled through, and they got a pretty decent game. But I don't think that would have been the future. I don't think [Rockstar North] would have done a Manhunt 2. So yeah, it would be Table Tennis, I think! Everything on Table Tennis!".

Unofficial GTA 6 PC port scrapped as Rockstar allegedly takes down Discord server

💡 Key Takeaways
  • One unofficial GTA 6 PC port has been scrapped, hours after major progress in getting the game up and running was shown, as its lead quits and alleges that Rockstar Games has taken down the project's Discord server.
  • In a recent development, project Leonida was one of the main GTA 6 recompilation efforts, and yesterday, as notorious leaker Cyberleek dropped an executable file for the Xbox build of the game they'd shared last week, it seemed like it wouldn't be long before the fan-made PC port was functional.
  • In the hours that followed, it'd seem even more progress was made.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One unofficial GTA 6 PC port has been scrapped, hours after major progress in getting the game up and running was shown, as its lead quits and alleges that Rockstar Games has taken down the project's Discord server.

In a recent development, project Leonida was one of the main GTA 6 recompilation efforts, and yesterday, as notorious leaker Cyberleek dropped an executable file for the Xbox build of the game they'd shared last week, it seemed like it wouldn't be long before the fan-made PC port was functional. The devs behind Leonida never expected things to work immediately, but mere hours after the EXE file was dropped, an enhancement in the Discord server claimed: "The game almost boots. Black screen, audio cuts off.".

In the hours that followed, it'd seem even more progress was made. One video shared on Reddit, apparently posted on the Leonida Discord server, appears to show the full opening sequence and the first-time game setup running on PC. However, don't expect any further updates from the project – or at least, not from its original creator – as the Discord server has now completely disappeared, and the project's lead says they're "stepping away" from it entirely.

In a recent development, "I quit guys. I'm sorry," NotRexed writes on Twitter. "I really want to make cool stuff but every single time shit happens that I can't control so I'm stepping away. Thank you everybody, especially in the discord that allowed me to have this opportunity.".

Recent findings suggest that in a follow-up post, they claim that Rockstar was behind the Discord server's takedown, saying: "Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I've said before, I'm a 15-year-old kid. Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle-aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye." Their original GitHub repository has also vanished, though others' clones of Leonida still appear to be live.

In a recent development, even with the original version of Leonida scrapped, though, there are still other projects racing to be the first to actually work. In fact, there's a whole tracker dedicated to monitoring the progress of various projects and how close they are to being ready to work. One such project recently said: "The title boots, runs its menus at its own 30 fps and loads the world, where rendering fails.".

While none are working yet, I still expect takedowns aplenty in the coming days and weeks, even if it's exceedingly difficult to completely wipe something from the internet once it's been posted.

Latest Update: DOOM: The Dark Ages Was Originally Planned As Xbox Exclusive

💡 Key Takeaways
  • DOOM: The Dark Ages was originally designed as an Xbox exclusive, but late decisions led it to being ported to PS5.
  • The news comes from a Kiwi Talkz podcast, where host Reece Reilly was joined by three former id Software devs to discuss all things DOOM, Xbox Game Pass, id Software work culture, layoffs, and more.
  • Interestingly, quite far into the conversation, ex-id software employee Jordan Turner claims that "originally [DOOM: The Dark Ages] was going to be Xbox exclusive" up until "fairly late in the process".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

DOOM: The Dark Ages was originally designed as an Xbox exclusive, but late decisions led it to being ported to PS5.

The news comes from a Kiwi Talkz podcast, where host Reece Reilly was joined by three former id Software devs to discuss all things DOOM, Xbox Game Pass, id Software work culture, layoffs, and more.

Interestingly, quite far into the conversation, ex-id software employee Jordan Turner claims that "originally [DOOM: The Dark Ages] was going to be Xbox exclusive" up until "fairly late in the process".

Sources indicate that "And in Dark Ages' case too, originally the game was going to be Xbox exclusive, and then fairly late in the process, we were porting to PS5. And at that point, we were still like, is our goal premium sales? In certain studio meetings, Marty [Stratton] would say stuff like, when we got it on Battle.net - 'it's another premium platform to put the game on'".

Reacting to Turner, Reilly goes on to critic the Xbox Game Pass model, saying he doesn't "understand it" and that it "devalues games". The conversation continues with a discussion about a lack of clarity and protection from Microsoft when developing games for Xbox Game Pass, and how id Software exec Marty Stratton felt porting to PS5 was "another premium platform to put The Dark Ages on" (as seen above).

Speaking to IGN in 2024, former Xbox CEO Phil Spencer described DOOM as a franchise that "everyone deserves to play", recalling a meeting between Stratton and himself in which the id Software exec mentioned "he wanted to sell it on all platforms. Simple as that".

Back in July, the DOOM developer was dealt a massive blow as part of Xbox's planned 'Reset', which saw id Software lay off a significant portion of its team.

id Software still remains an Xbox first-party developer, and is "already working on its next game", according to Xbox boss Asha Sharma's recent post on social media.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the Metro series is finally, officially back with a upcoming installment.
  • 2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however.
  • What won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Metro series is finally, officially back with a upcoming installment. 4A Games has just unveiled Metro 2039 to the world, the follow-up to the outstanding Metro Exodus, released all the way back in 2019.

2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however. Rather than build on the semi-open-world structure of Exodus, the upcoming sequel instead brings the focus back to where it all began: the Metro.

What won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is. Metro 2039 remains, like its predecessors, a story-driven, single-player game. Returning to the confined spaces of the Moscow Metro brings the focus back to the claustrophobic, uneasy atmosphere of the original games.

In a recent development, the game’s protagonist is, for the first time, going to be voiced throughout. From what we’ve been able to see, the psychological horror in this installment will be driven more by the very real effects the apocalypse has had, and continues to have, on denizens of the Metro.

According to recent reports, 2039 has been in development for years, but 4A Games has been rocked by two considerable events: the 2020 Covid pandemic, and Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, where the developer is based. The game’s darker story has changed in response to that.

The team’s Ukrainian perspective is molded into the narrative, and more prominently represents the toll the events of the last several years has taken on members of the team, their families and communities.

According to the developer, you can expect a bigger emphasis on choice and consequence, with Russian author Dmitry Glukhovsky returning to co-write a narrative that explores the compromised morality of a post-war society.

According to recent reports, the new protagonist’s return to the Metro comes with the reveal that the different underground factions are now united under one banner, the not-so-subtly named Novoreich. Lead by a former Spartan, the Novoreich is an authoritarian regime which offers what it believes to be the only path to salvation.

In a recent development, 4A Games remains majority Ukrainian, with teams based in Kyiv, and Malta. Unlike most AAA projects today, the studio continues to rely on its own engine tech. The 4A Engine is given a major upgrade for 2039: ray tracing is now a core component of the rendering pipeline, but the tech has been rebuilt to run better on modern hardware.

It has been revealed that today’s reveal sadly didn’t feature much gameplay - only a brief first-look with a mix of gameplay and cinematics. The developer, however, emphasised that creating cluttered, believable and lived-in environments remains a key focus.

Metro 2039 is set for release sometime this winter on PC, Xbox Series X/S, and PS5.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Avengers: Doomsday is fast approaching, and everyone seems pretty convinced Bucky Barnes isn't making it out alive.

Sebastian Stan has a role in The Batman 2, which set off alarm bells for Marvel fans that the Winter Soldier might not be returning for more in the MCU – and now an revision from Stan himself only seems to seal the deal.

Recent findings suggest that "I'm always happy to keep playing him. I don't know if the decision's up to me, ultimately," Stan said on the Next Best Picture podcast.

Sources indicate that when prompted by the interviewer that he must have some sway, Stan said: "Well, I don't know, to be honest with you. I'm ready to take the character in all kinds of different ways, but I can't make that decision, it's the powers that be. And I think they have a lot going on, they have a lot on their plate. Do I feel we've explored that character, there's nowhere else to go, I think we did our best? I do think we've done our best so far.

Industry observers note that "I don't think that that character totally got to fully live out his arc in the way that he has in the comics for instance, or that I've wanted," he continued. "I've been a massive fan of the whole Black Widow of it all. But that's not the only way, you could take him in all kinds of ways. I've spoken about this Sicario-esque paranoid thriller where he just recognizes this person on the street and thinks it's a torturer from Hydra, like back in the day, and he becomes obsessed and starts following the person and realizes the person has a family. And then he's like, 'Am I crazy or is this the guy…?' and confronts the person, the guy denies it.

"Kevin just sort of went, "Sounds good, uh, we'll see,'" he added with a laugh. "So, I'm always ready, but we're at that point now where I can feel it, he needs to either evolve somewhere, or maybe it's time. It's one of those.".

According to recent reports, now, while it sounds like Stan still has tons of ideas when it comes to Bucky Barnes, it also certainly sounds like he's made peace with leaving the character behind. We'll find out when Avengers: Doomsday finally arrives on December 18.

In the meantime, check out our guide to all the upcoming Marvel movies and TV indicates for everything else the MCU has in store.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that UPGRADE 19TH NOVEMBER: All of the 34 fired Rockstar employees appear in the credits for GTA 6.
  • It has been revealed that also, we couldn't identify six names in the "former employees" section of the credits before because they don't appear there, we now know.
  • ORIGINAL STORY 18TH NOVEMBER: Eurogamer can confirm that at least 28 of the 34 employees fired by Rockstar roughly a year ago - in an action that directly led to the employment tribunal Rockstar is currently facing in Scotland - are named in the credits of Grand Theft Auto 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that UPGRADE 19TH NOVEMBER: All of the 34 fired Rockstar employees appear in the credits for GTA 6. We were able to confirm the final few names' existence there after Rockstar posted the full credits online - in searchable form. Before this, the process of cross-checking was intensely laborious: it required watching a scrolling list of names for an hour-and-a-half to see if they appeared.

It has been revealed that also, we couldn't identify six names in the "former employees" section of the credits before because they don't appear there, we now know. These names appear listed under the departments the people worked for, as if they still worked at Rockstar. Why this is, we don't know - perhaps it's something to do with being involved in the employment tribunal or not. We're asking Rockstar for clarification.

ORIGINAL STORY 18TH NOVEMBER: Eurogamer can confirm that at least 28 of the 34 employees fired by Rockstar roughly a year ago - in an action that directly led to the employment tribunal Rockstar is currently facing in Scotland - are named in the credits of Grand Theft Auto 6.

We cross-checked a list of 34 names supplied to us by the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain - the same organisation taking action against Rockstar on behalf of the fired employees. And of those names, we found 28 direct matches in the credits, along with a couple of discrepancies we've since verified, and some close-sounding names we're attempting to clarify. Some names may simply be missing. We won't publish the list for privacy reasons.

It has been revealed that A number of those fired employees are seeking compensation for unfair dismissal amid allegations of "union busting", in an employment tribunal that comes to an end today. The delayed climax of the case couldn't be more fateful, aligned as it is with tomorrow's release of GTA 6, and the outcome will be historic either way.

Sources indicate that rockstar recently revealed that more than 4,711 people worked at the tech giant making GTA 6, employed across 12 offices around the world - a staff-count that has more than doubled since Red Dead Redemption 2. It's a game that's wowed critics - Eurogamer awarded GTA 6 five stars in our review this afternoon - and which observers expect to generate $2bn in revenue in its opening weekend alone.

But perhaps Christian Donlan put it best when digesting the opulence on display in the Netflix 'extended look' GTA 6 trailer. "To spend all this money making something so beautifully rich and detailed, to pay billions for this game and sweat every little animation, to float it out to us on Netflix, amongst genuine discussion around whether Netflix can handle it? That's commitment," he wrote. "And if you're willing to do that, and willing to do that to tell an underdog story, you should let your workers who made everything form a union.".

In a recent development, I know it, you know it, hell, I'm sure developer Archetype Entertainment know it: Exodus is kind of just Mass Effect again. That's in part because the DNA of the game has been built by series vets like Drew Karpyshyn, Chad Robertson and James Ohlen. But it's also because, well, they're putting FemShep in the game. Yes, I'm being a tad facetious here, but when the latest trailer for your game is literally titled "Female Jun Reveal," well, comparisons will be made!

Industry observers note that to top it all off, a blog post from the devs literally refers to the alternate gender for the protag as FemJun. They know what they're doing. In any case, first up, her voice actor! She's being played by Carina Conti, an up and comer last digitally heard in Mafia: The Old Country as Isabella Torrisi. Male Jun (who hasn't been given a nickname, which couldn't possibly serve to other female Jun (and MascJun is right there!)) has also had his voice actor confirmed as Stephen Oyoung, who you'll have heard as Mister Negative in Insomniac's Spider-Man games and Red Hood in Gotham Knights.

It has been revealed that it's been previously confirmed that no matter which gender you pick for Jun, you'll be able to romance whoever you like, so, happy smoochin'! The story will stay the same too, as will dialogue options, though I'm imagine some pronoun switcheroos will take place somewhere along the line.

Recent findings suggest that I'm mostly just left feeling that this doesn't really seem like it'll fix the game's boring hero problem. Edwin made note of Jun's quite lacklustre vibe earlier this year, aptly tearing down MascJun's Instagram visage, though this was prior to the face model and voice actor change the character has undergone. Personally, I'm not sure that'll be enough, and FemJun kind of matches that Instagram look; the perfect bun and bangs that pop out when she takes her helmet off is quite silly too. Ah well! A game isn't done until it's done (which, in theory, will be April 7th next year).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As GTA 6 continues to celebrate its unparalleled launch, other games are falling behind Rockstar's behemoth in popularity, analysts report – including generally high-population online titles, such as Call of Duty… and even Fortnite.

Rhys Elliott, head of market analysis at Alinea Analytics, reveals as much in a fresh post over on X, writing that "GTA 6's launch hit Call of Duty HARD, Alinea Analytics estimates." So, how hard are we talking?"CoD HQ's daily active customers across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam are down 42% from an average of 7.5 million DAUs to 4.4 million." That's nearly 50% – and when you narrow things down to PlayStation, Call of Duty's "main platform," it's worse.

On Sony's consoles, "Call of Duty took a 44% hit," as Elliott writes. "Sadly, CoD has barely bounced back after four days. It's still down 41% from its baseline." We're now on day five, and something tells me it's not much better. It isn't just Call of Duty, which recently released Modern Warfare 4, either. "Fortnite also took a hit, with its DAUs on PlayStation and Xbox paragliding down 28% from 17.8 million to 12.8 million.".

In a recent development, unlike Call of Duty, though, Fortnite has seen a bit of a recovery. As Elliott puts it, "Fortnite very much has its hooks in its player base, so it already managed to claw back some folks (back to 19% below its baseline) by the end of the weekend." Not to mention that "Fortnite is holding one of its major live events to tie up the current season on Dec 5," which the analyst says "Epic hopes will pull players back after they've polished off GTA 6's story.".

What really stands out here is that GTA 6 currently only has a story mode. There's no online counterpart like the one many know and love Grand Theft Auto 5 for – and it's tough to imagine what the future of other online games (like, you know, Call of Duty and Fornite) will look like then. "When the online component and PC port of GTA 6 land," as Elliott himself speculates, "it's going to be rough times for these live-service titles.".

Indeed, it will be – or so I believe, anyway. Only time will tell for certain, and there's no knowing when the online mode will even drop as it stands now… that and the PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6, which we've heard zilch about.

PSA: Some GTA 6 Ultimate Edition content is only available for the first chapter, and you'll have to put in hard graft to unlock more

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, GTA 6's Ultimate Edition has proven enormously popular, despite its hefty $100 price tag.
  • As previously confirmed, the $100/£90 Ultimate Edition provides access to exclusive vehicles, weapons, shops, and more, with the full list as follows:.
  • Rockstar also previously revealed that "Ultimate Edition bonuses become available to Jason and Lucia across their story, with fresh items uncovered behind each chapter".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, GTA 6's Ultimate Edition has proven enormously popular, despite its hefty $100 price tag. So much so that Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar parent company Take-Two, recently confirmed it's the edition most people are buying - and that's despite a lack of specific information about how its unlockable content works. With GTA 6 just hours away from release, however - and out now in certain parts of the work - details are beginning to emerge, and the answer is perhaps a little surprising.

As previously confirmed, the $100/£90 Ultimate Edition provides access to exclusive vehicles, weapons, shops, and more, with the full list as follows:.

Rockstar also previously revealed that "Ultimate Edition bonuses become available to Jason and Lucia across their story, with fresh items uncovered behind each chapter". The specifics of how - and when - all this stuff unlocks, though, remained unclear. So if you've opted for the Ultimate Edition, you might be wondering where your stuff is when you finally fire up the game. As reported by IGN, which has full unlock details, it turns out virtually all of GTA 6's Ultimate Edition content, as per details in the in-game shop, requires progressing through the main story - in some cases dozens and dozens of hours into the story - before it'll become available.

Sources indicate that ultimate Edition-exclusive shops, for instance, unlock during Chapter 1, and many of the other additions become available by the end of Chapter 2. That doesn't sound too difficult, but as Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell notes, reaching that point could take upward of 25 hours. As for some of the late-game unlocks, such as the Shitzu Squalo and the Vice City Style outfits and tattoos (available in Chapter 4) and Chapter 5's 95 Grotti Cheetah, you could be looking at closing in on 60 hours of playtime before they unlock.

"It'll vary depending how hard people focus on the main story," Chris explains, "but if you were mostly focused on the main story plus the optional character-based missions in largely chronological order, that's about how long it'd take.".

Sources indicate that it's also worth noting - perhaps surprisingly - that some Ultimate Edition content is only a temporary unlock, usable only during specific chapters. Jason's Dinka Enduro motorcycle and Crest Kayak, for instance, can only be accessed and enjoyed during Chapter 1. That's also true for his retro Vapid Ganado, available from the Coastal Auto Care mod shop in Key Lento. So basically, you'll want to make the most of these while you can!

All this might be a little disappointing for players who were expecting to be showered with Ultimate Edition spoils from the off (and that they'd be permanent unlocks), but the good news is 60 hours in GTA 6 is far from a chore. As Chris explained in his five star GTA 6 review, Rockstar's latest is an "irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action" that "pushes back the horizon of video games once again".

According to recent reports, everything's a bit grim these days, so let's just go all in on the misery shall we? Let's start with this line from the game's Steam page we'll be talking about today: "Mondrayn is a grim JRPG with survival elements where dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering." Crikey! You're telling me the sweet release of death won't be so saccharine after all? Sounds rough, so it's a good thing Mondrayn looks so darn compelling.

According to recent reports, the world of Mondrayn is a dead one. You start out waking up in a city, it's in a gnarly state, of course, overrun by a disease of unknown origin. Horrible monsters are roaming about the place, cults are performing nasty rituals, and you've got no memories, so all you can do is try and make any friends you can, kill the undead and get out of, all places, limbo.

Mondrayn is an RPG in the sense that it utilises turn-based combat, "intertwined with shootouts." I'm not entirely sure how that manifests, you do seem to be able to do both regular attacks and special moves, the state of characters seems to have an impact, but truthfully I don't mind not understanding because what I'm here for are the utterly, delectably rancid vibes on display.

In a recent development, every single pixel in this game looks like it was dipped in a vat of grime, puss, blood and vomit, and I revel in it! The enemy portraits are crunchy and violet, they look ripped straight out of some obscure art book for a Warhammer-esque tabletop game no one has ever heard of. It looks a bit fantasy, a bit steampunk, and incredibly, incredibly grimdark. It's the kind of world I'd rather instantly top myself than spend a second longer in, so, kudos to the fictional characters in it that have no choice in the matter for managing better than me. As it stands, Mondrayn has no release date, but you can wishlist it on Steam in the meantime.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that lego Jeff the Land Shark has been officially revealed, and the kit will be hitting shelves on January 1. You can check it out for yourself at the Lego store, though it's not up for pre-order quite yet.

The most precious boy from Marvel Rivals is apparently getting a Lego set if leaks are to be believed, but fans are seriously divided on how Lego Jeff the Land Shark looks.

Sources indicate that popping up via reliable source Unibricks on Instagram, Lego Jeff the Land Shark looks to be a mid-size figure that's roughly on par with Lego Eevee. Much like his inspiration from Marvel Rivals and the comics, he's all toothy grins, substantial cartoon eyes, and stubby little legs… but the result has received mixed reactions from fans who aren't entirely sold on the idea. The comments on Unibrick's post trend toward the negative, while responses on a Reddit post sharing a video of the set from Newly introduced Elementary are split down the middle – they basically veer from "aw, so cute!" to "oh man, that's hideous.".

Recent findings suggest that want more Jeff in your life? There's plenty of merch based on his appearance in Marvel Rivals, from tees to action figures. You can find it all at Amazon, where a lot is getting a discount ahead of Black Friday.

Industry observers note that I understand this mixed reception. While the alleged model does capture that signature smile and happy-go-lucky vibe, it doesn't quite replicate Jeff's squishy, rotund look. The tail on this leaked set feels a little sparse too, as if it's missing pieces. (I assume this is so the fin can 'wag' thanks to a ball joint, but it looks odd at a glance.).

Still, I think the team's done the best they can with the scale they're working at – and I'm not sure I'd call it 'bad' by any means. Soft and rounded characters are really hard to recreate in Lego brick form at this size due to the toy's angular nature. While a few of the best Lego sets manage it through some eldritch sorcery (Munchlax or Wallace & Gromit come to mind), I can only imagine how tricky it is with a shark that is basically a spongy football with legs.

There's no word on when this kit would launch, but if it's January, that month is looking very busy - a host of Marvel kits are also hitting the Lego store then.

Either way, this leaked kit is just one of many Jeff-themed pieces of merch coming out; although the recent Hasbro Marvel Rivals action figures are cool, I only have eyes for the Jeff the Land Shark action figure.

It has been revealed that if you want to know more about the character, here's why Marvel's Jeff the Land Shark is so popular. Want to build up your collection, on the other hand? Don't miss the best Lego Black Friday deals.

I've been writing about games in one form or another since 2012, but these days you'll find me managing GamesRadar+'s tabletop gaming and toy coverage (I spend my time here handling everything from board game reviews to the latest Lego news). I've also been obsessed with Warhammer since the 1990s, and love nothing more than running tabletop RPGs like D&D as a Dungeon Master.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Sims 4 players on PlayStation and Xbox have now caught up to their friends on PC, at least when it comes to the game’s Marketplace. This newly introduced feature is essentially a hub for paid mods and other user-created content.

As often happens when long-established games introduce paid mods, The Sims 4’s wasn’t especially well-received, in part because of the introduction of a fresh premium currency - Moola - that is the only way to purchase any of that content.

The Moola denominations and prices are similar to many other in-game currencies, and the criticism around them is the same: they obfuscate the true value of items, and because of the way those denominations are structured, you’ll never be able to buy exactly what you need.

According to recent reports, for most games, the subject of paid mods has always been fraught, and that's certainly true for The Sims 4. In the announcement blog post, Maxis said that the launch on consoles will work similarly to what PC players have seen, in that Kits will no longer be available to buy directly with real money on the PlayStation and Microsoft Stores. While Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs will remain, you’ll need to buy Moola if you want to acquire Kits going forward.

According to recent reports, interestingly, however, EA seems to have changed its mind somewhat on the Kits situation. A recently leaked memo (via SimsCommunity), appears to show that the publisher intends on making Kits available for purchase directly again, without the need for Moola.

According to recent reports, unfortunately, this only appears to affect the PC version, with the reversion reportedly forthcoming on both the EA App as well as Steam. Indeed, according to the same report, the change has already taken place on the former, with the latter following on April 20.

Considering the Marketplace only just introduced on consoles, the company may wait to see if the decision to remove Kits from console platform marketplaces will be as poorly received as it has been on PC.

If you’re looking to jump back into The Sims 4 to check out all the upcoming paid content, make sure you’re well-equipped with our list of Sims 4 cheats and debug options, or this one specifically for the Royalty & Legacy expansion cheats.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Koei Tecmo has declared the second and final DLC for Nioh 3 will be released next month, with an Xbox version of the game to follow in 2027.

Industry observers note that koei Tecmo and Team Ninja are a pretty busy bunch. Nioh 3 released earlier this year and has remained one of the best action games of 2026, which was only around four months after Ninja Gaiden 4 was released. On top of that, Fatal Frame 2: Crimson Butterfly Remake released a month after Nioh, and Wo Long 2: Wings of Ember is set to release next March – and that's not even mentioning the new Dead or Alive game that's on the way. And yet, somehow, the developer is still able to get the DLC for Nioh 3 out months ahead of schedule.

It has been revealed that nioh 3's first DLC pack, Hell Rising, arrived in August ahead of its October release date, and now Koei Tecmo has confirmed that Nioh 3's second DLC, Bloody Insurrection, is releasing on December 17, 2026, which is a little bit ahead of its previously stated February release date. The DLC is set to have a new stage – Shimbara in 1638 – and The Battlefield of Carnage which seems to be the game's equivalent of something like Devil May Cry's Bloody Palace.

On top of all of that, the developer has unveiled that Nioh 3 will be the first game to release on Xbox consoles after a disclaimer teased this back in February. The Nioh 3 Complete Edition, which naturally includes the game and its DLC, will be released on January 28, 2027 for PS5, PC, and Xbox Series X|S.

Nioh 3 was already the first game in the series to launch simultaneously on PC and PlayStation after the first two games had exclusivity windows on PS4, so hopefully this means Nioh 4 will be multiplatform from day one, should it arrive.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the promise of user-generated content, this idea that you could host a platform that grows infinitely because the people that interact with it make things for it and you don't even have to pay anyone, is an alluring one. And its siren call has come for Dead by Daylight, as developer Behaviour Interactive have outlined the future of the game, which includes a way to make your own bits for the multiplayer horror game.

"What if you could create your own Dead by Daylight experiences?" explains a blog post recapping the intends for how the game is going to change. "As one of the most exciting updates coming in 2027, the Dead by Daylight Workshop will open the doors to user-created content in some incredible ways. From designing your own Maps and importing custom assets, to modifying game rules, objectives, and even creating entirely newly introduced modes, the possibilities are vast.".

Recent findings suggest that the post goes on to note that anything created in the workshop will "exist separately from all our classic modes, with dedicated creation tools and moderation provided to ensure experienced modders have everything they need to do their best work, and all submissions meet our official guidelines." I am always hesitant when it comes to UGC faff, because the ability to make your own custom Debbie Daylight maps might sound promising, but people do actually have to engage with them for the whole thing to work. It's just putting a hat on a hat!

Sources indicate that anyway, the workshop isn't the only thing Behaviour have in the works. For one, the game is getting a big visual overhaul. You can expect lighting improvements, more detailed assets and "tons of atmospheric touches," alongside revamps of particular maps like the Temple of Purgation and Backwater Swamp. Killers and survivors will be getting some TLC too by "improving character textures, proportions, hair, and animations to make them look and feel more lifelike. That includes updated character rigs, newly introduced motion capture, and new facial animation technology designed to better express a character’s fear, pain, and struggles over the course of a Trial.".

In a recent development, beyond all of that, a dynamic weather system is coming to the game, meaning you'll now have to deal with the likes of rain, thunderstorms, snow and heavy wind, all of which can impact matches. Onboarding for newer folks should be getting some improvements too, with the addition of a "more cinematic introduction, clearer explanations and tutorials of game mechanics, and a more gradual introduction," to the game. All of this will be coming in one big update sometime in 2027, so, keep your eyes peeled for whenever that drops.

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Don't expect GTA 6 to get an patch supporting higher framerate modes, at least, not on current-generation consoles.
  • According to recent reports, last week, some players weren't too happy with the news that GTA 6 is targeting 30FPS on all platforms it's presently launching on - PS5 Pro, PS5, Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S.
  • Rockstar's now seemingly confirmed that its crime epic won't run at 60FPS or 40FPS anytime soon, simply because it can't on the currently available hardware.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Don't expect GTA 6 to get an patch supporting higher framerate modes, at least, not on current-generation consoles. Rockstar has explained that even the most powerful console of the bunch, the PS5 Pro, isn't powerful enough to run the lavish game at 40FPS or 60FPS.

According to recent reports, last week, some players weren't too happy with the news that GTA 6 is targeting 30FPS on all platforms it's presently launching on - PS5 Pro, PS5, Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S. Like countless other massive productions this generation, the hope was that Rockstar Games would offer both quality and performance modes for its lush open-world monster.

Rockstar's now seemingly confirmed that its crime epic won't run at 60FPS or 40FPS anytime soon, simply because it can't on the currently available hardware.

"While the PS5 Pro's central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game's complex simulation at higher frame rates," the studio's technology production director, Marc Chambers, stated in a statement to Kotaku. There you have it, then - even the beefiest console around can't handle Leonida at higher framerates.

Chambers did note some of the souped up console's other technical improvements, however: "Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR). The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game's visual fidelity.".

According to recent reports, the tech gurus over at Digital Foundry gave some more insight into how GTA 6 runs on current-gen machines, calling it a "technical tour de force," though one that can still dip below 30FPS on PS5 and Xbox Series X during busier chase scenes and explosive shootouts. It's perhaps unsurprising, then, that higher framerates are off the table for now.

A 30FPS launch is by no means a departure for Rockstar Games, either. GTA 5 also ran at an unsteady 30FPS when it first dropped onto the Xbox 360 and PS3, with 60FPS support only coming alongside the game's PC port more than a year later. I'm not too fussed about the game's 30FPS target, personally. I'd much rather have a game that consistently hits 30FPS than one that continuously chugs trying to reach 60FPS, especially when it's as frequently drop dead gorgeous as GTA 6.

According to recent reports, the slightly lower framerates haven't affected the game's critical response so far, either. In Eurogamer's GTA 6 review, our Chris Tapsell called it a "game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale" as "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again.".

If you're planning to jump into the game at midnight - or if you're virtually travelling to Fresh Zealand for early entry - there's a few things to be aware of. First is that you won't be able to replay GTA 6's missions without multiple save files, so be sure to soak it all up. Second, some Ultimate Edition content is only available in the first chapter.

You can see what exactly the ESRB had to say about this title in its official rating summary:.

It has been revealed that "This is an action role-playing game in which players follow the story of a mercenary on a quest to save the planet from evil. From a third-person perspective, players traverse locations across the planet, interact with characters, and battle human enemies and fantasy creatures (e.g., robots, monsters, mutants). Players use swords, pistols, and magic attacks to defeat enemies; battles are accompanied by realistic gunfire, light effects, and large explosions. A handful of sequences depict additional acts of violence and blood: a character impaled by a sword; a character shot at close range; a character detonating a bomb to kill soldiers. Some female characters are designed with low-cut outfits and deep cleavage; the dialogue also references suggestive material (e.g., “Bad little girls like you two deserve a good spanking”; “My, what sharp teeth you have…All the better to eat me with, perhaps?”). Final Fantasy VII Revelation will be launching for the Switch 2 on the same day as other versions of the game.

Nintendo also recently featured Revelation as one of the major games on the way to the Switch 2 in 2027, alongside titles such as The Duskbloods and Resident Evil: Veronica.

Will you be checking out Revelation when it rolls out for Switch 2 next year? What do you think about the ESRB rating and description? Let us know in the comments.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The developer unveiled a grand 2026 roadmap, covering three more seasons currently in the works, and a wealth of new additions across the entire game, including new maps and the introduction of a new theatre of combat.
  • In a wide-ranging new video dubbed The Year Ahead, members of the Battlefield 6 development team have revealed a lot of new information about the future of the multiplayer shooter, going over plenty of the features and new content coming over the course of this year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It took Battlefield Studios over four months to tell Battlefield 6 players what they can actually expect from the game over the course of this year, in terms of content - but we’re glad to see a plan laid out nonetheless.

The developer unveiled a grand 2026 roadmap, covering three more seasons currently in the works, and a wealth of new additions across the entire game, including new maps and the introduction of a new theatre of combat.

In a wide-ranging new video dubbed The Year Ahead, members of the Battlefield 6 development team have revealed a lot of new information about the future of the multiplayer shooter, going over plenty of the features and new content coming over the course of this year.

According to recent reports, the video confirmed that BF6 has at least three other seasons in the works. Season 3, which begins in May, will be followed by Season 4, and Season 5 later in the year. Season 5 is the most mysterious, which is understandable.

Sources indicate that we’ve known about some of what’s coming in Season 3, such as the remake of Golmud Railway (now called Railway to Golmud), but the video also revealed that a remake of Battlefield 3’s Grand Bazaar - now Cairo Bazaar - will also arrive later in the same season. Other exciting additions, such as battle royale solos and ranked play for Redsec are also on the agenda for Season 3.

Sources indicate that season 4, set for July, looks to be the biggest so far, with the introduction of naval combat, which will be available across two maps. Tsuru Reef, which is mentioned to be even larger than Golmud, the largest map in BF6. The Pacific-set map won’t be the only one, as later in the season, another remake will arrive, this time of the iconic Wake Island.

According to recent reports, the introduction of naval combat will bring with it a fresh dynamic wave system, aircraft carriers with operational flight decks, and new naval vehicles. Custom lobbies and Spectator Mode are also planned for Season 4.

Season 5 will bring three maps to BF6, rather than two, but all of its content remains under wraps.

Sources indicate that perhaps a sour note is that almost all of the maps referenced and shown in the video are remakes of maps from other Battlefield games, or reimagined at the very least. The Battlefield series is no stranger to remaking its own maps, but Battlefield 6 appears to be leaning on it much more than past entries.

If it’s any consolation, however, the map remakes we’ve played so far in Battlefield 6 have gone through major changes that have contributed to giving them a different flow and feel from their classic versions, or even remakes in other BF games.

Sources indicate that over the course of 2026, you can also expect the return of persistent servers, as well as a server browser to find them all - just like the good ol’ days. This includes the ability to host your own, though it’s unclear quite how this is going to work.

Season 3 is set to revealed in the coming days, so you’ll be hearing back from BF Studios in the near future.

Back in September, Xbox officially announced its reorganisation looks for legendary studio Rare, moving it under Activision alongside Halo, Age of Empires, Sea Of Thieves, and Banjo-Kazooie.

According to recent reports, at the time, Rare was reportedly working on "other projects" beyond Sea of Thieves, but decisions about their future were now in Activision's hands. The two companies have collaborated pretty well in the past, considering how well Activision handled Crash Bandicoot and Spyro.

It has been revealed that however, a newly introduced job posting on Activision's LinkedIn page suggests that another Rare IP, Banjo-Kazooie, has found a home amongst its new overseers. The job is for 'Product Manager, Emerging Franchises' with responsibilities to lead market planning, publishing strategies, drive business performance, and a whole bunch of other corporate fluff. What we found interesting is the accompanying mission statement.

Here's a look at the 'Your Mission' segment:.

"Activision is home to iconic gaming franchises including Call of Duty®, Crash Bandicoot™, Spyro the Dragon™, and now… Halo®, Age of Empires®, Sea of Thieves™, and Banjo Kazooie®. Become part of the team working on building, growing, and shaping many of these franchises.".

In a recent development, it's been a good 18 years since Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts & Bolts, already longer than GTA VI's 13-year wait, so you've gotta feel for Banjo fans. According to the job posting, both Sea of Thieves and Banjo-Kazooie now fall under Activision, with a team working on "building, growing, and shaping many of these franchises".

What happens next for Banjo-Kazooie has been a hot topic of conversation for donkeys now, and if this job listing is to be taken at face value, could we finally be looking at a newly introduced game in the near future? According to former Rare employee Grant Kirkhope, at least three studios have already pitched a new Banjo-Kazooie game to Microsoft. So, the interest is out there. Let's just wait and see what Activision does.

Alright, let's hear it PX'ers. What do you make of this? Let us know in the comments below.
