I don't want to write about video games any more, I want to deliver milk in the countryside and hang out with a cow and quirky people! Sorry, what, there's a game all about that called Milki Delivery that came out today? Alright, I'll write about video games again, especially when they look as charming as this one does.

The stakes at play in Milki Delivery are very low (as are the steaks, no butchery to be found here, only one very sweet looking cow I couldn't possibly slaughter). You play as Neha, and she's made a promise to her pet cow, the titular Milki, that you'll find her a friend (I think this is a world where there aren't any cows left; yikes!). To do that, all you have to do is deliver her milk! Accept because this is an adventure game, you'll have to help out a few folks along the way.

According to recent reports, it's a game very much about the journey, as when riding about this lush and bright countryside, you might find a group of cats that just need a little taste of that sweet creamy juice you've got. Or maybe you have some rope that a farmer needs to wrassle up some sheep. Sometimes you'll have to get a bit more involved with the various people you meet, but predominantly, you'll be delivering milk to folks who need it.

Getting around the place is quite simple too, you plot out your path ahead of time and let the game take you as it's all mouse driven. A relaxed experience to be sure, but the game's art is just so delightful to look at, I'm quite enticed by the idea of just slowing down and enjoying some pretty pictures and making friends along the way. You can make different kinds of milk, too, just be feeding Milki different ingredients. Not how that works in real life, but now I kind of wish it was.

In any case, Milki Delivery is out now, and you can pick it up on Steam.

GTA 6 won't let you use cheats until you complete the main story, and locks progression when you do

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Here's a twist: you can't use cheats in Grand Theft Auto 6 until you complete the entire game's main story.
  • That's what we discovered from our tests at least, after loading in saves at various points through the game to be sure, and it's also both a first for the series and a departure even from how developer Rockstar handled cheats in Red Dead Redemption 2.
  • In GTA 6, you'll again need to do some legwork.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Here's a twist: you can't use cheats in Grand Theft Auto 6 until you complete the entire game's main story.

That's what we discovered from our tests at least, after loading in saves at various points through the game to be sure, and it's also both a first for the series and a departure even from how developer Rockstar handled cheats in Red Dead Redemption 2. In that game,approximately half of the cheats were available from the off, and the other half required discovering specific newspapers from around the game's world to unlock.

In GTA 6, you'll again need to do some legwork. This time it appears that all of the game's cheats not only require you to finish the story, but also complete various tasks or challenges to unlock them.

The way it works is simple enough. Once you finish the main story, the "Cheats" tab - previously hidden - quietly appears at the far end of the Progress menu, accessible when you open the in-game map and scroll with the bumper buttons. From there, you can view various sub-sections of cheats, sorted by category, and a list of 10 or so cheats for each.

In a recent development, with each cheat there'll be a short explanation of what it does, and what's required to unlock it and, once unlocked, guidance on how to perform it. This is done via whipping out your phone, holding down the shoulder buttons and using various D-Pad inputs - much the same as GTA 5.

Recent findings suggest that there's also another caveat to bear in mind: when you use a cheat, you'll see a notification warning you that the game can't be saved while it's active, and that Trophies and Achievements are also disabled until you end that session. This makes sense, once you understand the nature of GTA 6's story - there is a cheat for giving yourself a load of money, for instance; another departure from GTA 5 where that popular cheat was removed - but given you'll need certain amounts of cash at various points of the story, enabling you to shortcut that would disrupt the way the narrative unfolds.

We'll have a guide from yours truly to all the game's cheats live on Eurogamer in the very near future, as the game releases here in the UK. In the meantime, if you find yourself on the fence about this one, be sure to give our GTA 6 review a look. As I put it there, giving the game five stars: it is "the most believable and unbelievable video game world ever made".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, diablo 4 is gearing up for its biggest post-launch event yet: the upcoming release of the Lord of Hatred expansion. As was the case with Vessel of Hatred before it, expansion releases alter the seasonal flow in a few ways, and Blizzard has now explained how.

Sources indicate that the game’s next season - its 13th - has been officially revealed as Season of Reckoning. The new season will kick off alongside the expansion’s release next week, and will be available to all players, just like all previous seasons.

Although Season of Reckoning will roll out as normal, the season itself won’t be as meaty, at least when it comes to the sort of gameplay mechanics and themes players have come to expect from each upcoming season.

According to recent reports, you’ll still find the normal Season Rank chase, Smoldering Ashes, and various rewards at each chapter. Season Blessings will also return, but that’s about it for progression outside of the game itself. If it’s any consolation, there are more goals and objectives to tackle this season.

The even better news is that, according to Blizzard, future seasons will follow the classic format, which makes sense. The fresh season will come with a battle pass, of course, featuring four Reliquaries, as usual. The first Reliquary is free, while the others are paid.

Sources indicate that blizzard has also confirmed the the pre-load for Lord of Hatred is available now on all platforms. Even if you’re not getting the expansion, patch 3.0.0's pre-load includes all expansion content regardless, so you may as well pre-download it to be ready for April 27/28. On launch day, you’ll also need to download a smaller patch, version 3.0.1.

Sources indicate that in case you missed it, we published our Lord of Hatred review earlier in the week. Give it a read if you’re curious about the expansion’s impact on the narrative, and how it changes core Diablo 4 gameplay.

Recent findings suggest that while you're out stealing cars for Moses, the GTA 6 BF Bandito will appear on your list, taking you out to the very rural roads of South Leonard County and the Buckskin Swamp. This GTA 6 heist is slightly harder than the others you might have carried out so far though, as this car will be on the move.Like all of Moses' targets, the rough location of the BF Bandito is marked on the map, but as you make your way there, you'll pass by some whoopin' and hollerin' country dwellers who are already taking the buggy for a spin. Here's how to get your hands on the GTA 6 Bandito and get paid.

The map marker will take you to the rough location of the BF Bandito, where you should keep your eyes and ears open for some locals riding around the swamps on buggies - one of these is the Bandito.

To claim it for yourself, you'll need to stop the Bandito driver, and there are a few ways to do this. If you clock him fast enough, particularly when crossing water, you can simply get in front of him, and he'll stop. Otherwise, you can chase down the Bandito, shooting the driver and his pals. Weirdly, though, when I did this challenge, the driver eventually just stopped and bolted, leaving the buggy free for me to take, though I'm not sure exactly what triggered him to do this. Essentially, just stay close, don't destroy the car by shooting it too much, and it'll be yours in no time.

If you're struggling to find some of the other GTA 6 cars that are ripe for the taking, then check I can also help you nab the Declasse Vamos, as well as Vanessa's cute GTA 6 pink Porsche - I mean, Pfister, which will be live shortly.

Grand Theft Auto 6 has been out in the hands of console players for a few days now, and a few of us at PC Gamer have been dusting off our PlayStations and Xboxes to dive into Leonida as we eagerly anticipate its eventual (but yet unannounced) PC release next year potentially.

I've been gaming it up myself and, as is always the case with GTA, I am absolutely loving driving around. Flying down the highway, exploring all the alleyways and retail areas, and taking out to the waters on a boat or jetski. All of it, of course, to the soundtrack of GTA 6's various radio stations.

According to recent reports, there are a huge number of stations in this game—19 of them, to be exact—with a ton of excellently-curated songs lingering within and famous cameo hosts. Usually I find myself just picking one station and sticking to it, but with GTA 6? I've been cycling between quite a few, each one offering something a little bit different.

It has been revealed that four stations have been grabbing most of my attention though. Pop station Flash FM has easily gained the most airtime in my playthrough so far. Am I listening to Ariana Grande in my everyday life? No. But am I bombing it down the highway while singing Break Free to myself every time it comes on? I absolutely am.

But I've also been peppering in a ton of 80s station Vice City FM. I mean, c'mon, you've got Weird Al Yankovic as a co-host, first of all. But you've also got straight up bangers like Lionel Richie's All Night Long, Simply Red's Money's Too Tight (To Mention), and Billy Ocean's Loverboy.

In a recent development, there's also Emotion 98.3, the radio station dedicated to songs about love (both being in love and being heartbroken, of course) and yes, I have stayed in the car waiting to hear Phil Collins' excellent drumming in In The Air Tonight. And finally, because I am a raging emo at heart, I've obviously had to whack on a bunch of The Chamber 106.6. Tool, System of a Down, and Metallica? Count me in.

According to recent reports, but what about you? If any of you PC gamers are partaking on console, is only one radio station catching your attention, or have you found yourself channel hopping just like me? Or is there somehow not a single station that's caught your fancy, instead finding the podcasts a more entertaining use of your listening time? Be sure to drop a comment and let me know.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that nvidia's board have indicated that they aren't about to do a big u-turn and reappoint recently resigned CEO Jensen Huang, following his departure after multiple alleged instances of extramarital cavorting were reported by the press. Since his exit last week, Huang has indicated he'd be open to making such a return, were it deemed best for both the firm and AMERICA.

"On November 12th, our board of directors revealed that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the tech giant's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member," Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones stated during an investors call on November 17th (thanks, Percieving Calls Gamer). "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.".

Recent findings suggest that that last bit seems likely to have been noted with the intention of quieting down some of the speculation around a Huang return that's been bubbling away since he removed his bum from the black and green throne and that the exec embraced in a statement put out yesterday. "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life," he wrote. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the board’s independent investigation.

"Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the firm navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. Nvidia is a once-in-a-generation company. If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO.".

For now at least, it seems leather jacketed GPUperman will not be triumphantly flying back into his former post amid a wave of corporate and patriotic fervour. Likely as part of continued efforts to reassure moneyfolk that they won't be making negative headlines again soon following Huang's departure, Nvidia's board announced yesterday that they're establishing a "latest standing committee responsible for board-level oversight of the firm’s national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management". One of Huang's alleged affairs was with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The Chinese government have denied the accusations of espionage.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress is currently serving as Nvidia's interim CEO while the company's board searches for a permanent sexy leather jacket man replacement.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Previously, all HoYoverse games with PC versions have always been directly available from the developer’s website, or through the Epic Games Store.
  • In a recent development, the main focus of the livestream, of course, has been Version 2.8, otherwise known as Fresh Eridan Sunset.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse just wrapped up a pretty exciting Zenless Zone Zero Special Program that not only delivered all the details on the next big update, it also came with the unexpected announcement that the action RPG is on its way to Steam.

Previously, all HoYoverse games with PC versions have always been directly available from the developer’s website, or through the Epic Games Store. In other words, Zenless Zone Zero will soon mark the massive tech giant’s debut on Valve’s platform.

In a recent development, the main focus of the livestream, of course, has been Version 2.8, otherwise known as Fresh Eridan Sunset. This upcoming release is scheduled for May 6, though the Steam version does not yet have a date.The new release sees the release of two new Agents, as well as the brand-new Wind attribute enemy.

According to recent reports, the release also acts as the last chapter of Season 2, and it sees Ramiel becoming the main target of different factions in the Outer Ring. The two new arrivals, together with Proxies and Cissia will embark on a quest to learn the new identity of Ramiel.

The first new Agent is Promeia, the executioner of Krampus. She’s an S-Rank Ice Anomaly Agent who can consume Trial by Cold to trigger Abloom on enemies. This is done by converting Corrosive Chill.

According to recent reports, by using her EX Special Attack, she can enter the Bound Absolution state, which allows her to automatically Perfect Dodge any attack that targets her. If you have another Anomaly or Support Agent on the team, Promeia can further boost the entire squad’s Abloom damage.

Industry observers note that the second addition in 2.8 is Starlight - Billy, also an S-Rank Agent, though wielding Physical Rupture instead. This is the upgraded form of Billy, and he arrives on a combat motorcycle to bring his signature Starlight Knight to the fight. Through it, he can deliver major Physical burst damage.

According to recent reports, the higher Billy’s health, the more Sheer damage he deals. In fact, all Physical damage he deals lands as Sheer damage. Further building on his tank-like role, his skills can also restore his own health.

Industry observers note that re-runs in Version 2.8 will be Lucia in the first half, and Orphie & Magus in the second. The other exciting addition coming with this update is the latest Wind attribute enemy, and the accompanying Vortex mechanic.

Recent findings suggest that when an enemy is inflicted with the Wind Attribute Anomaly, any other Anomaly attack type that gets applied will trigger Vortex, rather than Disorder. This deals AoE Anomaly damage of the type that matches the corresponding element.

Throughout the version’s runtime, you’ll be able to take part in the Marcel Bootopia-themed event, which gives you control of Eous and lets you explore a Bangboo resort island. The island has been closed due to an outbreak of Hollows, and you must rescue Bangboos and find treasures.

Industry observers note that if you do, you’ll earn Booltergeist and its Bangboo core for your troubles. This is an A-Rank Bangboo that can float around and fire lasers in combat. Its damage is further boosted whenever certain teammates are present.

In a recent development, the Ultimate Verdict Trial is another event you can check out that lets you fight alongside newcomer Promeia, or take part in other mini-activities that all reward Polychrome. Finally, you can look forward to a latest Hoshimi Miyabi outfit: Dignified Blossom, which will be available in the store.

Before you jump back in next month, it always helps to catch up on the latest Zenless Zone Zero codes to make sure you’re not missing out on any freebies.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that GTA 6 is out at midnight everywhere (19th November), but it's far from the only game in town. Indie publisher Devolver Digital is taking on the open-world behemoth with its very own Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, out the same day, and you can win a free copy of the platformer by proving you've deleted GTA 6 off your hard drive.

Recent findings suggest that "Want a free copy of November's hottest release? Repost this tweet with a video of you deleting your GTA6 pre-load along with #MakeRoomForVolvy for a chance to win a copy of Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed on Steam," the publisher wrote on social media.

Industry observers note that it's not every day you see a publisher promote its own games by asking folks to delete another company's release, but arguably the wildest part of the giveaway is that Volvy's Adventure isn't launching on consoles. Even if you were to scrub GTA 6's 212GB pre-load from your PS5 or Xbox, you're definitely not making room for Volvy.

Industry observers note that "Heads up: Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is launching exclusively on PC. While we expect to see console GTA deletions in your submissions, Steam keys are the only prize available for this giveaway," Devolver noted.

Sources indicate that devolver made quite an amusing GTA 6 parody trailer, as well, which sees Volvy and Miss Volvy running from the police and getting steamy in the shower. I've embedded it up above for your viewing pleasure.

According to recent reports, for the unaware, Volvy used to be a common fixture at Devolver Digital's frequently bonkers notE3 presentations. He's now somewhat of a organization mascot. But while Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is being presented as a "much-anticipated remaster of the original remake of the hit action-platformer," this is, in fact, Volvy's first proper game. Making up an elaborate history for Volvy is just part of the publisher's long-running and increasingly questionable gag.

Gunbrella and Gato Robot developer doinksoft is behind this one, a throwback side-scrolling platformer where our mouse-like mascot uses his oversized hand to helicopter over gaps, punch through roadblocks and, erm, fist himself underground, per the game's Steam page.

Sources indicate that devolver Digital has been waiting to steal Rockstar's thunder for well over a year now. The publisher threatened to release a game on GTA 6's release date way back in May 2025, and has pushed back its plan with each new GTA 6 delay. Gotta respect the commitment, at least.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We've been hearing about Xbox's Project Helix console for some time now, with Xbox always talking very vaguely about what we can expect from it, and perhaps that's because the vision has changed for the system over the years.
  • Industry observers note that today, the folks over at Windows Central are revealing details about the "original blueprint" for Xbox Project Helix, which include that it was going to be a "full gaming PC" akin to the ROG Xbox Ally with the ability to run console games on top.
  • They were seemingly even going to drop the paywall for multiplayer games in the process.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We've been hearing about Xbox's Project Helix console for some time now, with Xbox always talking very vaguely about what we can expect from it, and perhaps that's because the vision has changed for the system over the years.

Industry observers note that today, the folks over at Windows Central are revealing details about the "original blueprint" for Xbox Project Helix, which include that it was going to be a "full gaming PC" akin to the ROG Xbox Ally with the ability to run console games on top. Steam support would have been included, as would have Windows 11 in general.

They were seemingly even going to drop the paywall for multiplayer games in the process.

Recent findings suggest that "The original plan for Helix, which ran under a different codename until last summer, was for it to essentially be a full gaming PC with the capability to run all of your existing Xbox console games on top. It would be functionally similar to the Xbox Ally PC gaming handheld, with a gamepad-first Xbox-style full-screen interface, complete with the capability to exit out to the Windows desktop and install whatever you want. That, indeed, included Steam.

As part of this strategy, Xbox would have had no choice but to drop the paywall for multiplayer from Xbox Game Pass (formerly Xbox Live Gold). There's no universe where a true PC could function with a multiplayer paywall. I understand that, indeed, removing the paywall was costed into this strategy.".

All of this was apparently conceived prior to the component crisis that's caused hardware prices to rise significantly in recent times, and ultimately there's a feeling that the initiative might have changed somewhat as a result.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has also become the head of the brand since Helix was in the conception phase, and she may have her own ideas about dropping multiplayer paywalls and integrating Steam into the next-gen console. After all, a lot of people have wondered what Xbox stands to gain by partnering with Steam instead of focusing on the Xbox Store.

It's vital to highlight here that nobody knows what the current plan is at Xbox HQ, and Windows Central theorises that "maybe Microsoft doesn't even know itself". There's every chance we still may be looking at a console that can run Steam games and not require a multiplayer paywall, but there's probably an equal chance that Xbox has gone back the drawing board and decided to reel in its scope when it comes to PC support.

It has been revealed that let's wait and see, eh? We know we're definitely getting the ability to play PC titles on Xbox Project Helix no matter what, but the safe bet is that it'll be via the Xbox Store - and who knows what'll happen with the multiplayer side of things.

It has been revealed that for what it's worth, Xbox has this month committed to Helix being a console and not a PC, which seemingly goes against the original proposal for a so-called "full gaming PC". In that regard, it appears that things have changed.

Industry observers note that "We're very clear on the design goal: Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it.".

What are your thoughts on this? Let us know down in the comments section below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that remakes of the first two Max Payne games are on the way, and Rockstar's been helping Remedy get the releases in order. According to the Control and Alan Wake studio, collaborating with the purveyor of GTA 6 has been absolutely grand so far.

Jean-Charles Gaudechon, the CEO of Remedy, described the working relationship between the two outfits in glowing terms for Game File. "Honestly, it's been great," he claims. "You know why? Because I think they're super respectful of Remedy.".

Respect is a good start to any collaboration. Gaudechon then doubles down, just to make it clear everything's positive right now. "I'll say it out loud: They've honestly been an awesome partner," he adds. "And it's no bullshit.".

In a recent development, well, it seems he doesn't have any complaints, anyway. Remedy and Rockstar actually have quite a bit of history, since the studio that gave us GTA actually worked on ports of the first Max Payne, then published the second outright.

It has been revealed that it only makes sense, then, that they'd team back up to give both games a lick of paint and revision them for modern hardware. As you may well be aware, it's been a while since Rockstar's done anything outside of the Grand Theft Auto or Red Dead Redemption mines.

Industry observers note that time was the developer and publisher would be involved in all sorts of projects, but nowadays the focus tends to be a little more streamlined. I guess that's what happens when you make the biggest games in the industry.

The two have been working on these do-overs since around 2022, and we don't have a release window yet. Perhaps now that Alan Wake 2 and Control: Resonant are out of the way, Remedy can put in more resource, while Rockstar can finally do something that isn't GTA 6. I mean, how much is there to do post-launch for such a game? Our boy Max is waiting, people – come on.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that hoYoverse just wrapped up a latest Genshin Impact Special Program, where the developer revealed everything there is to know about the game’s next major upgrade.
  • This next update has a lot going for it, and it will be in players’ hands everywhere on May 20.
  • Luna 7 will take us back to Sumeru for its new Archon Quest, where a new crisis that threatens to plunge the nation into chaos is brewing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that hoYoverse just wrapped up a latest Genshin Impact Special Program, where the developer revealed everything there is to know about the game’s next major upgrade. Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana, or as its friends call it, Luna 7, was unveiled as part of the showcase.

This next update has a lot going for it, and it will be in players’ hands everywhere on May 20.

Luna 7 will take us back to Sumeru for its new Archon Quest, where a new crisis that threatens to plunge the nation into chaos is brewing. Nahida is out of the picture, and someone who looks suspiciously like Il Dottore has emerged.

If you complete this chapter at launch, you’ll earn up to 560 Primogems, as well as Nicole's Ascension Materials. Nicole is the first of three playable characters arriving with this revision. Something else you’ll unlock if you finish the chapter swiftly is a new Weekly Boss that HoYo says has “unpredictable abilities.”.

And if you haven’t played in a while, don’t worry, you can refer to the Guiding Notes feature to catch you up on what’s been going on in the world. This is part of a larger effort from the team to make story progression more seamless, and also includes improved quest autosave prompts.

In a recent development, nicole Reeyn is highest-profile and most interesting, being the first playable member of the Hexenzirkel. The mage is a 5-Star Pyro Catalyst wielder intended as a support member of the team. She can boost the ATK of all party members, even those not presently on the field. She also generates a shield while doing so.

Industry observers note that her Elemental Burst allows her to summon an Arcane Projection that follows the active character, sending out Coordinated Attacks that match their Elemental Type. Outside of combat, Nicole can help you find treasures by calling upon a Seelie to guide you to them. Quite fitting, as you’ll be exploring in the inside of the Witch's Lodge in Nicole’s Meeting Point in Luna 7, so bring her along.

Sources indicate that lohen, the Vice Captain of the Knights of Favonius' Fifth Firm, is the second fresh character. Also a 5-Star addition, he is instead a Cryo Polearm wielder designed for aggressive combat. His main use is dealing massive Cryo DMG, and he can do that by managing two resources unique to him: Joy, and Will to Win.

Through his Elemental Skill, he can enter the Masterstroke state, allowing him to build up (and consume) Joy to unleash enhanced skills. The more his teammates fight, the more Will to Win he biulds, which can later be used to boost his effectiveness further. For an even more powerful display of force, bring along a Hexerei character when he’s on your team.

Prune is the third and final addition. Prune is a 4-Star Anemo Catalyst wielder, and her kit is inspired by her Witch Hunter aspirations. Using a bell and a hammer, she can deal DMG of several elements at once, and trigger Swirl reactions.

It has been revealed that nicole, and Lohen will debut in Luna 7’s first half, while Prune will follow in the second. The first half will also see a Durin rerun, with Mavuika returning in the second half. You can look forward to a newly introduced limited-time event as part of Luna 7, with a focus on Klee's Little Hexenzirkel.

You’ll find a series of mini-games you can play alongside Prune, as well as Qiqi, Yaoyao, and Sayu. If you play, you could earn the Super Awesome Magic Key, an exclusive weapon skin. Miliastra Wonderland is doing its thing, too, with a new sports festival for you to take part in.

One new gameplay addition worth calling attention to is that Manekins can now perform actions in Teyvat. The Kamera, which you can use to capture moments with Manekins, is getting upgraded, too, with new editing tools and assets.

Before you pick the game back up, be sure to check out our recently-updated Genshin Impact codes page for some free stuff you may be missing.

#189240. Despite being £61.7 million in debt, bankrupt MindsEye devs Build a Rocket Boy are splurging on legal action against "a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews"

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1288 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy 📈 Bullish 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Despite being £61.7 million in debt, bankrupt MindsEye devs Build a Rocket Boy are splurging on legal action against "a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews"

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1288 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the firm's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors.
  • Sources indicate that BARB's largest debt by far is the roughly £36.5 million owed to NetEase, publishers of Marvel Rivals.
  • Sources indicate that build a Rocket Boy have been on a journey, it's fair to say.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the firm's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors. The documents also touch on founder Leslie Benzies and CEO Mark Gerhard's claims that MindsEye is the victim of an organised sabotage campaign. The company's leaders have apparently taken out even more loans in order to fund legal action against the suspected perpetrators, with the promise of a healthy payout. I'm not holding my breath.

Sources indicate that BARB's largest debt by far is the roughly £36.5 million owed to NetEase, publishers of Marvel Rivals. Asset manager Diameter Capital Partners are the second largest external creditor, having loaned BARB around £4.25 million. A further $19 million is owed to "group undertakings" – "group undertakings" meaning debts to parent companies, subsidiaries or fellow subsidiaries. Studio founder Benzies, meanwhile, is owed £1,158,167.05. Given that Benzies has been repeatedly accused of torpedoing MindsEye's fortunes by way of disruptive micro-management, I'm not sure many BARB staff would agree that he really deserves his million quid back at this stage, but that's what it notes on paper. Smaller IOUs include £10,434.11 for Amazon Web Services, £634.36 for Unity, and a mighty £19.90 for OpenAI.

Sources indicate that build a Rocket Boy have been on a journey, it's fair to say. Revealed in 2023, their flagship project MindsEye is a filmic GTA-ish action shooter initially billed as a full-fat demo for Everywhere, a game creation platform comparable to Roblox. MindsEye struggled to compel us before launch and did not find its people on release, with poor sales leading to layoffs even as BARB leadership insisted they could revive the game's fortunes.

The same leadership were subsequently accused by their own staff of "disastrously" mishandling the redundancies and enforcing "unbearable" crunch. Unionised BARB employees have now taken management to court for installing alleged surveillance software on their work PCs. The game's publishers Io Interactive noped out of the picture in March this year. Meanwhile, Benzies and Gerhard have thrown around accusations of a sinister espionage and sabotage campaign, carried out by unspecified perpetrators. They made a sort of revenge fantasy DLC pack about it, which our own Mark Warren characterised as we-already-have-Hitman-at-home. The bankruptcy documents shed more light on these twists and turns. According to the administrators, BARB were "funded mainly by equity investment from institutional, strategic and venture capital investors over several funding rounds, including a $110m Series D round in 2023." This followed a £32 million investment in 2020, as reported by GI. The company grew significantly during MindsEye's creation to around 500 UK and overseas employees. According to a group income statement, the company posted sequential operating losses of £47.5 million for the period ending September 30th, 2025, and £63.1 million for the year ending December 2024. The administrator proposals document also devotes some time to the aforesaid allegations of sabotage. "The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary," it reads. "The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties. The directors have indicated that such claims may be substantial in value, although the extent of any recovery remains uncertain and will be dependent upon the outcome of ongoing investigations, legal proceedings and asset recovery actions." A later section vaguely alludes to the sum BARB leadership hope to recover. "Prior to the Joint Administrators' appointment, the Company had undertaken detailed investigations and had commenced litigation against several third parties, with the assistance of the Company's former legal advisers, Brandsmiths, in connection with matters described earlier in the Proposals," the doc reads. "The Joint Administrators consider the litigation potentially to be the largest asset of the Administration." The document goes on that BARB management have "sought financial support from third party investors to fund the anticipated legal costs and expenses associated with the litigation", with some of these funding agreements already executed. "Further executed agreements and associated funding contributions are expected to be received, shortly, and a substantial litigation fund is anticipated to arise," it continues. The Joint Administrators are "at the moment engaging in the on-going litigation, progressing the funding arrangements entered into by the Company, and have assessed the merits of pursuing the litigation". They will liaise with relevant parties to "determine the most appropriate strategy for preserving and, where appropriate, realising value from this potential asset for the benefit of creditors and other stakeholders." The doc doesn't name who, exactly, is being taken to court. As far as I'm aware, it isn't us. Anyway, it's good to know that the company who owe over £60 million are taking on more debt in order to pursue a histrionic grievance for which they have yet to supply any real evidence whatsoever.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, GTA 6 is slowly rolling out across the globe. The crime epic's already available to play in countries such as South Korea and Newly introduced Zealand, but Japanese players are finding out that male nudity is only partially obscured by a thin black thong that covers Jason and the other men in Leonida.

Last week, we reported that GTA 6 might have been censored in Japan since the region's age rating board lacked any mention of the "sexual content" we knew it would include elsewhere. The Japanese version's install size was also notably smaller than other places in the world.

Now that GTA 6 is finally in the hands of players, we have a better idea of what was left out and/or covered up in Japan. Multiple social media accounts playing the game in Japan have reported that when you take main man Jason into the shower, his butt is only kinda covered up by a thong. At least in the version I played, Jason is usually fully naked while washing up.

GTA 6 censorship on the Japanese version is kinda funny lol https://t.co/u8v0f0cqz0.

エロシーンきた！　#GTA6 #GTAVI https://t.co/RKOEtkONlJ.

Another social media post spots a different male NPC wearing a very similar black thong during a cutscene that normally has him laid bare in international versions of the game. I'm guessing all instances of male nudity might be obscured similarly in GTA 6's Japanese version.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 is far from the only game that's dealt with regional censorship in Japan, however. Baldur's Gate 3 and The Witcher 3 had their most salacious scenes censored in some manner, for example. And even GTA 5 had to remove its infamous torture scene for approval in Japan. It's quite possible GTA 6 has had to cover more than just the backside of nude men to go on sale in the country, although those regional differences won't become entirely clear until players get further through the story.

Industry observers note that ahead of the game's full launch, GTA 6 managed to break Reddit and viewership records on platforms like YouTube and Twitch. Interesting tidbits are also flying out on release day, like the fact you can't replay missions or use cheats until finishing the story. Our Chris Tapsell still had a cracking time with the epic open worlder. "A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that," he wrote in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

Latest Update: GTA 6 discourse is suffering from the flat earther effect

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you ever watch science videos on social media, you've probably been served a video of someone debunking the claims of a flat earther.
  • It starts with a clip of some belligerent dope demanding to know why, if the earth is so round, ships don't disappear over the horizon.
  • It's good content, but if you linger too long on one of those videos, you'll get another, and then another, and pretty soon your whole feed will be debunking videos.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you ever watch science videos on social media, you've probably been served a video of someone debunking the claims of a flat earther.

It starts with a clip of some belligerent dope demanding to know why, if the earth is so round, ships don't disappear over the horizon. A greenscreened science communicator then appears, rubs their forehead, and demonstrates us a video of a ship disappearing over the horizon. Checkmate.

It's good content, but if you linger too long on one of those videos, you'll get another, and then another, and pretty soon your whole feed will be debunking videos. Now you're enrolled in a never ending lesson plan which features such insights as 'an all-meat diet is not good for you,' 'the moon landing was real,' and 'hating women is not in fact based.'.

The total effect of this is that the most ignorant and dishonest quacks and provocateurs get to set the level of discourse, and instead of investigating new metaphorical horizons in topics that interest you, you wind up watching people debate the existence of the actual horizon.

It has been revealed that which brings me to Grand Theft Auto 6. Despite making $3.79 billion on its launch day, it's easy to stumble across confident social media claims that it's a total flop and everyone's going to refund it. According to popular X posts, GTA 6 doesn't even let you steal cars anymore, and there are hundreds of Metacritic user reviewers insisting that it's far-left propaganda rather than the mass-market entertainment product it obviously is.

Recent findings suggest that it's the videogame discourse version of flat eartherism. The millions of people playing GTA 6 do not think it is a "cuck simulator" because you can buy a woman flowers, but it's hard not to react to the few dorks making that claim, even though focusing on debunking them severely limits the depth of the conversations we can then have about the game. Good luck discussing your feelings if you dislike GTA 6 for normal reasons!

Sources indicate that over the past few days, I've entertained sparks of hope that GTA 6 could be the flashpoint that brings us out of this era of videogame discourse. The millions of people playing it and not reacting like buffoons are surely irrefutable evidence that culture war dunces don't represent the masses.

But then again, we're still pointing at videos of ships going over the horizon to prove that the earth isn't flat.

Mystic Messenger's most loyal players are getting banned in droves for seemingly playing the game too much

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, mystic Messenger, arguably one of the best dating sims around, has been dormant for about seven years.
  • The free-to-play mobile dating sim has started banning players with seemingly too many Hourglasses - the game’s virtual currency - saved up in their accounts.
  • The news exploded on the Mystic Messenger subreddit overnight, with over a dozen reports from players logging in to play normally, only to receive an in-game notice that their accounts had been banned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, mystic Messenger, arguably one of the best dating sims around, has been dormant for about seven years. Despite not receiving new content or any meaningful updates in all that time, the game remains popular with its core fans, many of whom just woke up to some shocking news about their accounts.

The free-to-play mobile dating sim has started banning players with seemingly too many Hourglasses - the game’s virtual currency - saved up in their accounts. So far, it looks like players with 1,000 or more have been targeted, but others with far fewer hoards have reported getting the axe, too.

The news exploded on the Mystic Messenger subreddit overnight, with over a dozen reports from players logging in to play normally, only to receive an in-game notice that their accounts had been banned.

According to recent reports, the message players received is identical, and doesn’t mention the specific reason for the ban. “Your account has been banned because abusive behavior has been detected from your account,” it reads, ending with a support email address the affected user can contact if they believe they’d banned in error.

Industry observers note that it didn’t take a while for players to realise that most, if not all of the bans are for players with thousands of Hourglasses in their accounts. The virtual currency can both be acquired in-game just by playing, as well as through direct real-money purchases.

For a nearly ten-year-old game that stopped receiving content three years into its life, it’s easy to see how a dedicated group of players would be able to acquire so many Hourglasses by simply playing regularly for so long.

When contacted by the affected players, Cheritz, the developer and publisher of the game, has instructed them to send receipts of how they acquired Hourglasses (assuming they were purchased) to verify whether or not they’d been fraudulently obtained.

Considering that Mystic Messenger has practically been abandoned by its developer, certain exploits have emerged over the years that allowed players to farm Hourglasses faster than intended, but those instances have always been dealt with then and there.

The blanket and sudden nature of this ban is what’s spooked players, especially those who’ve been logging in for years and never thought accruing in-game currency from playing the game too much would make them the target of a ban.

Sources indicate that the running theory is that most of the bans are unintentional, and may be the result of a fresh automated security system that’s been implemented. It’s entirely possible, especially if its’s AI-based, that the new system simply couldn’t distinguish between those who have earned (or bought) their Hourglasses fairly, and those who used exploits.

The timing of the ban wave is also suspect. With the game’s 10th anniversary coming up in July, it could be that Cheriz is preparing to release a large update for Mystic Messenger, which may include upcoming content. If most of the playerbase is already sitting on massive amounts of in-game currency, they may simply use that to fast-track their way to unlocking the new content, which would greatly affect the developer’s bottom line.

According to recent reports, this is a problem that other live service games have run into in the past. Just recently, extraction shooter Arc Raiders added a cap to the amount of Cred players can hold in their accounts very quickly after its launch. That currency is used to buy cosmetic sets in the store, so the logic is easy to follow.

All of that has certainly put a damper on the enthusiasm of the game’s most active players, many of whom were excited to get together in person for the coming 10th anniversary, participate in community nights and so on to celebrate.

It’s also disheartening to see a fanbase so loyal; playing a game as regularly for so long without new content, to be treated so poorly. Even without knowing what the game is, it’s impressive that so many people have kept the flag of their favourite game flying for so long.

To find out how this dating system works, here’s a Mystic Messenger primer that explains it all. Once you’ve wrapped your head around it, you’ll no doubt want to pick the correct answers for every guest, and this guide will help you nail every one.

In a recent development, as you've probably heard, GTA 6 is out on consoles this week and targeting 30 FPS on that hardware. Despite reports claiming one may not be far away, there's still no official word on a PC port, hence why we've not got a review that delves deep into analysis of just how central to the experience the smell reaction system is.

The wait for confirmation of a PC version continues, then, and it looks like that might well be the only chance people get to play the crime sandbox at 60fps, with Rockstar having confirmed that higher frame rate modes aren't en-route to even the most beefy of consoles.

Speaking to Kotaku, GTA 6's devs made clear optional 60 or 40fps performance modes aren't on the way, even for the more powerful Pro variant of the PS5.

It has been revealed that "Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR)," Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers put it. "The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates.".

Industry observers note that so, there you go. The consoles just ain't got that dog in 'em. One would think, then, that being able to run GTA 6 in all its glory at higher frame rates will likely be a selling point for that PC port that's assumed to be on the way. Whether the average PC owner's graphics card and other bits will have the horses to deliver a smooth 60 is another question, and an especially pertinent one given the ongoing RAM crisis has made upgrading certain aspects of your setup ludicrously expensive.

If it requires a 5090 at a minimum, I guess those of us with less than absolute cutting edge cards will just have to keep playing Sleeping Dogs until the AI bubble bursts.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Eurogamer ↗ Open Full Page

It really seems like Xbox isn't allowed to say GTA 6 at all

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (526 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Like many major brands, Xbox is finding all sorts of ways to associate with the biggest game launch of the year: Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • As pointed out by multiple people on social media, the Xbox Wire post titled 'How to Get Ready for November 19' is one all about celebrating the massive release day of GTA 6, and helping players find ways to maximise their time with their Xbox consoles.
  • According to recent reports, "Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your Xbox console," the post reads, stopping short of saying why the day is important.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Like many major brands, Xbox is finding all sorts of ways to associate with the biggest game launch of the year: Grand Theft Auto 6. Unlike indie publisher Devolver Digital, however, Xbox has cleverly avoided ever mentioning GTA 6 directly in its marketing campaigns for GTA 6.

As pointed out by multiple people on social media, the Xbox Wire post titled 'How to Get Ready for November 19' is one all about celebrating the massive release day of GTA 6, and helping players find ways to maximise their time with their Xbox consoles. Despite that, it does not mention GTA 6 by name a single time.

According to recent reports, "Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your Xbox console," the post reads, stopping short of saying why the day is important. "We can hardly believe it's almost here, either.".

In a recent development, one day prior, Xbox Wire partnered with DJ Khaled to create custom doctor's notes for players to submit to their employers to take the day off. Why would you want to take 19th November off? Because you're apparently having "a serious case of Vitamin G deficiency".

It has been revealed that going even further back, Xbox revealed a custom-made Series X console it called X-Bite, which is a large, sculpted alligator that swallowed a Series X console. Why? Because "this November, Xbox is heading to Florida - home to incredible wildlife, unforgettable places, and every now and then, stories you have to see to believe.".

Florida, of course, is the real-world US state GTA 6's Leonida is based on, but in keeping with the theme of not referring to the game - or its made-up state - directly, the blog does not.

Now, Xbox has directly named GTA 6 in places, but only when, seemingly, the post is about factual information. This Xbox Wire post reiterates GTA 6's Xbox Cloud streaming availability, and this one is a look-ahead at games launching the following week on Xbox. But that's about the extent of what you can expect.

So what's going on here? The simple guess is that PlayStation has a co-marketing deal with Rockstar, meaning no other console platform gets to use GTA 6's name in marketing. Sony is allowed to make custom, GTA 6-themed consoles, branded, limited-edition DualSense controllers and blaster the game all over the PS Blog, social media, and even change the PS App's icon colour to match the hue of GTA 6's.

This is all too similar to when, each year, various brands encourage you to buy their products to be ready for The Big Game, which is very distinct from the Super Bowl happening on the same day. Like Xbox, those brands simply don't have the rights to the real thing.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 is available now on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. In Eurogamer's five-star review, Chris Tapsell wrote, "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that.".

In a recent development, avengers: Doomsday is packed with heroes and villains from the past quarter-century of Marvel movies. But there's one all-powerful figure who is quite clearly being held back – and it's got fans wondering what (if anything) he will have to do in the upcoming battle against Doctor Doom.

So, how do you solve a problem like Bob? The character, first introduced in Thunderbolts, is presently lying dormant and chilling at Latest Avengerz HQ after being twisted into Sentry, a Superman-like figure who can send people to The Void with but a mere thought. Can you really leave that on the table if you're going up against Doom?

Well, it's a discussion that has spilled over to Reddit, with audiences debating the ramifications of unleashing Bob onto the world.

"Sentry is obviously gonna be there as an absolute last resort since the Avengers probably don’t wanna risk the Void coming back until they have no other choice," one mentioned.

According to recent reports, another added, "Doom is a master manipulator. Giving him access to the Sentry/Void is like a death invitation.".

In a recent development, others joke that Bob will simply be Bob for the entirety of Avengers: Doomsday, kicking his feet and doing the dishes while the rest of the team brings the fight to Doom. There's a suggestion, though, that any major deaths – including to Florence Pugh's Yelena – would turn Bob into the unstoppable Sentry once more, with no allies to help calm him down this time.

Personally, I think Bob is being held back just to continue the age-old question of 'Who would win in a fight?' Pitting Sentry against Doom too soon not only risks answering it, but risks making Bob's power level seem diminished when he could be saved instead of Avengers: Secret Wars.

Discover what happens next – and if Bob puts on the Sentry suit once more – in Avengers: Doomsday, out in the UK on December 16 and in the US on December 18.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The longest game of Dota I've played was comfortably past the 70-minute mark. Matches that gloriously long-winded can be fun in small doses, but they can also be exhausting and infuriating—this is Dota we're talking about, after all. The latest patch to rearrange the venerable MOBA, 7.42, is finally here, and it's got tons of changes that might just prevent your games from going feature length.

It has been revealed that the most exciting of these, for my money, is the Greater Horn of Battle: a guaranteed drop from the Tormentor neutral monster that summons a wave of super creeps in all your team's lanes (the patch notes refer to them as the more powerful mega creeps, but players have noted the stats don't match up that way). If you've played League of Legends or Deadlock, it fills a niche similar to the Rift Herald or Deadlock's Unstable Rifts—an objective you can complete in the earlier stages of a game to push lane(s) hard.

It's an ability that, if timed correctly, could force the other team to scramble to protect each lane or risk losing lots of ground. And it's not the only change with the potential to speed up matches.

Industry observers note that base hero health has gone up from 120 to 200, with the caveat that strength now gives less health per point, meaning that heroes will be sturdier early on but slightly squishier later. The Glyph of Fortification, a teamwide spell that makes buildings invulnerable, no longer resets its cooldown when certain buildings go down. Heroes also now gain experience passively, even when dead, meaning that you never completely stop growing stronger as the match progresses.

According to recent reports, it will probably take some time to see if this actually meaningfully reduces match times or if these changes even stick around for long, but personally, anything that makes Dota a little bit speedier has the potential to reignite my passion for the game. Whenever I dip in these days, it's to play the fastest mode possible—Turbo, which accelerates every aspect of play and gives you oodles of gold just for existing—but it's so different from the traditional Dota setup that it may as well be a upcoming game.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that steam is abuzz this week with a couple of long-anticipated releases, but in Forza Horizon 6’s case, at least, the game isn’t even out for what will be most of its players.
  • That version of the game includes more than just a few days of early access, of course, but you’d think the $120 price tag would’ve only been palatable to a small group of players.
  • Forza Horizon 6, which has spent 16 weeks in Steam’s global top sellers list, currently occupies the number two spot, having jumped up three spots this week in anticipation of the launch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that steam is abuzz this week with a couple of long-anticipated releases, but in Forza Horizon 6’s case, at least, the game isn’t even out for what will be most of its players. The anticipated sequel in the open-world driving game series doesn’t officially launch until May 19, but owners of its most expensive version - the Premium Edition - can play it right now.

That version of the game includes more than just a few days of early access, of course, but you’d think the $120 price tag would’ve only been palatable to a small group of players. Not the case with this game.

Forza Horizon 6, which has spent 16 weeks in Steam’s global top sellers list, currently occupies the number two spot, having jumped up three spots this week in anticipation of the launch. The game has also naturally been popular with players, so popular in fact that it has already overtaken the player counts of all other Horizon games on the platform.

In a recent development, at the time of writing, the game has peaked at 128,157 concurrent players on Steam alone (via SteamDB). The figure has already climbed several times during the writing of this story, so you can only imagine how much higher it’s going to get deeper into the weekend.

All of that, of course, days before the official launch on Tuesday, when, theoretically, the majority of the game’s audience will be able to start playing. In just a few short hours, Horizon 6 has already gone well above Forza Horizon 5’s peak concurrent of 81,096, as well as Forza Horizon 4’s peak 75,689 players.

Steam is the only platform that publishes player numbers, of course, but it’s easy to see how similar the enthusiasm is going to be on Xbox. Though the game is not yet part of the Game Pass line-up, those who don’t want to wait could buy the Premium Edition Upgrade to get the included content, and play it right now.

Game Pass, and Xbox / Windows Store numbers don’t factor into Steam’s, which is another thing to consider when viewing the numbers holistically. Indeed, given how successful Forza Horizon 5 has been on PlayStation 5, Horizon 6’s upcoming release on Sony's console is bound to be even bigger.

Forza Horizon 5 has been off to a similarly flying start in the first few days of its own advanced access launch, so it’s obviously not surprising to see Horizon 6 do better there. In case you missed it, check out our review of Forza Horizon 6. In short, we really liked it, even if we expected more.

Chronicles: Medieval devs Raw Power are bankrupt, but their sandbox RPG lives on at a new studio co-founded by Satisfactory devs Coffee Stain

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (368 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games.
  • In development since 2022, and slated for Steam early access release in 2027, Chronicles: Medieval is a game about building vast armies of men in metal hats and horrifying doublets, then fighting alongside them in real time.
  • According to recent reports, the original devs included people who worked on The Witcher 3, Total War, and Crusader Kings III, which may not surprise you from the foregoing descriptions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games. The game will now be made by a fresh developer, owned 25% by a few former Raw Power devs and 75% by Coffee Stain. Coffee Stain will fund the game's on-going development.

In development since 2022, and slated for Steam early access release in 2027, Chronicles: Medieval is a game about building vast armies of men in metal hats and horrifying doublets, then fighting alongside them in real time. It sees you positioning archers behind spears and finessing your cavalry flanking actions, all the while occupying a fleshy human body that can be hacked and stabbed. It's set during the Hundred Years' War between England and France over the 14th and 15th centuries, and gives you a volatile sandbox world of warring factions and patrols.

According to recent reports, the original devs included people who worked on The Witcher 3, Total War, and Crusader Kings III, which may not surprise you from the foregoing descriptions. It's not entirely clear who has made the leap to Coffee Stain's newly founded studio.

It has been revealed that raw Power declared bankruptcy on 30th October, subsequently calling on players to help them find funding. During the bankruptcy proceedings, Coffee Stain successfully bid 36.75 million Danish Krone for Chronicles: Medieval, which comes to around four million pounds or 5.4 million dollars. According to CEO Anton Westbergh the project "ticks many of the boxes that we believe to be fundamental for a great game, and we think it has a good chance of becoming a strong long-term IP for the group." The game yet sits at 26th on SteamDB's most wishlisted, despite Raw Power's funding troubles.

Gaming doesn't want for simulations of shrieking feudal folk, but Medieval has a certain swagger, even when you remove Tom Hardy from the picture (and you should - he only ever voiced that one trailer). Here's hoping the newly introduced team can find their feet under Coffee Stain, and that whoever hasn't made the transition finds good work elsewhere.

Industry observers note that hoYoverse has today delivered full details on the next major update for Honkai: Star Rail. Version 4.3, dubbed The Lethe Below the Living, will be available for all players on June 1. The upcoming update adds a latest chapter to the Planarcadia arc, and introduce a new playable character.

The fresh narrative chapter will also unveil more about Mortenax Blade, the Trailblazer themselves, and the husk of the Aeon.

According to recent reports, mortenax Blade is the hero of this chapter, and he’s going to step into the World in Canvas. The goal is to - by borrowing the power of Voracity - excise Shuhu from his body and end the curse.

It has been revealed that the Trailblazer goes on a trip of their own in Version 4.3, this time to Inkford Hermitage, right on the edge between the World in Canvas and the real world. They’re going to undertake this journey to warn Graphia of the Asat Pramad threat.

In case you hadn’t already guessed, Mortenax Blade is this version’s new playable character. The 5-Star Fire-Type swordsman is on the Path of Nihility. Blade’s Ultimate allows him to enter an enhanced state by deploying a special Bounded Field.

Recent findings suggest that while the field is active, all enemies receive more DMG. Entering this state is also how Blade unlocks his skill, which uses a Sword Formation to deal more damage. This is then used to essentially unlock a second, more powerful Ultimate for him.

The benefits of Mortenax Blade’s kit extend to his teammates, too. Any ally who attacks an enemy with him on the team, they inflict a debuff on them. This also builds up a special Charge that Blade can later use with his Skill.

According to recent reports, version 4.3’s launch arrives alongside the Gift of Tempered Blade event. Through it, you can claim a latest Trailblazer Outfit piece for free, but only after getting Mortenax Blade from Warping. The first phase’s rerun will be Yao Guang, and the second phase will bring back both Cyrene and Phainon.

It has been revealed that you can also expect the Wispae Amusement Park to arrive within the World in Canvas, which you’ll get to design. You can blueprint where the rides will go, pick the different themes, set visitor routes and more.

Sources indicate that starward Mode is another upcoming addition, which can be found in Memory of Chaos, Pure Fiction, and Apocalyptic Shadow. Starward will see you take on three different stages, which you’ll need three teams for. Clearing each challenge with full stars will reward you 100 Stellar Jades extra per chase.

In a recent development, there’s more coming down the line, too. A new Fate/Stay Night [Unlimited Blade Works] collaboration will arrive in a content up this summer. The event will give players a chance to earn Gilgamesh or Archer for free by logging in.

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (523 w)

Digital Foundry Analyses Whether GTA 6 Could Benefit From 40FPS On Xbox Series X

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (523 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Purexbox

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Over the weekend, there was a whole lot of buzz amongst the GTA 6 community about a Quick Resume glitch that unlocks the game's frame rate on Xbox Series X and S, potentially allowing it to reach 60FPS and higher.
  • Follow-up tests demonstrated that the results were averaging more around the 30-35FPS range consistently, and some of the game's animations appeared to be running at double speed.
  • Rich Leadbetter of DF found that he reached an average of 36FPS on Xbox Series X in the first hour of the game:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over the weekend, there was a whole lot of buzz amongst the GTA 6 community about a Quick Resume glitch that unlocks the game's frame rate on Xbox Series X and S, potentially allowing it to reach 60FPS and higher.

Follow-up tests demonstrated that the results were averaging more around the 30-35FPS range consistently, and some of the game's animations appeared to be running at double speed. The experts at Digital Foundry have now weighed in on this, and they've come to pretty much the same conclusion - that it's not really a viable way to play.

Rich Leadbetter of DF found that he reached an average of 36FPS on Xbox Series X in the first hour of the game:.

"Unfortunately, while the unlock glitch is academically interesting, it doesn't provide a huge improvement to responsiveness. Our capture tools show frame-rates in the 30fps to 40fps range on Series X, with Rich recording an average frame-rate of 36fps during the first hour of the game.".

The sped-up gameplay is also mentioned, described as an "oddity" that "makes the game inconsistent and harder to control", although this is said to be more likely a result of the bug rather than GTA 6's code being tied to frame rate.

According to recent reports, nevertheless, there's one specific advantage that's brought up as part of this glitch, which is that it reduces the game's input lag. Digital Foundry's tests showed that the game provided around 170ms of lag at the 30FPS mark, while a 40FPS scene dropped it to around 120ms. However, the varied frame rates are said to provide an "unsettling" feel overall, and one that probably outweighs the smoother feel during specific 30FPS+ moments.

The outlet states that a 40FPS mode when using a VRR supported display "could still make sense" on Xbox Series X, but "the game's CPU limits remain the largest barrier against such a mode" due to occasions where GTA 6 can't even reach 30FPS as things stand, while it might also require extra work such as implementing FSR upscaling tech.

"A 40fps mode with VRR could still make sense, but it's far from an open-and-shut case to say that such a mode would be an improvement overall against the current 30fps cap. It might also require extra work, such as integrated FSR 4 on Series X in service of a higher frame-rate when GPU limited, which wouldn't be the work of a moment. Finally, it looks like a 60fps mode is fundamentally unachievable on current console hardware.".

Who knows whether Rockstar Games will be able to put in the work to provide a 40FPS mode in the future, but we're going to bet they'll stick with 30FPS and simply aim for 60FPS when Xbox Project Helix and the PS6 hit the market. They've got plenty of work to do with the PC version of GTA 6, not to mention the GTA Online version of the game that's surely in the works, so pushing to hit 40FPS on current-gen consoles seems unlikely.

What are your thoughts on this? Let us know down in the comments section below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Rings of Power could have looked very different, according to David Fincher. The Fight Club director claims he was approached about becoming the showrunner of the Lord of the Rings prequel.

Speaking to Josh Horowitz on his Happy Sad Confused podcast, he opened up about navigating interests from streaming services when working creatively, speaking about working on Mindhunter and The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth at Netflix, when he revealed he was also offered The Lord of the Rings show as well.

The Social Network director explained: "I got offered, what is The Lord of the Rings thing at Amazon?" Horowitz replied, "Oh, Rings of Power?" before Fincher revealed: "Oh I got offered that." When quizzed about whether he was approached to just be a director, he explained it was an offer to "showrun" the series.

"This is before it went to Amazon, and I was like, 'No way', that is an extension of a corporate interest," Fincher continued. "I look at James Gunn and I think, you know, those are bigger balls that I have. I would not want to take on DC and all of its dysfunction." Fincher also revealed in the chat that he had long talks with Kathleen Kennedy about taking on Star Wars too.

It's not clear at what point Fincher was offered the chance to work on what would become The Rings of Power, but given he says it was before it went to Amazon, he was likely involved when the Tolkien Estate was looking at shipping out the television rights for The Lord of the Rings in 2017.

It has been revealed that it's reported that Netflix and HBO pitched for this with ideas including a remake of the original trilogy and an Aragorn and Gandalf series. It's possible that Fincher was approached for one of these, but it seems he was out of the conversation before Amazon invited pitches themselves for a fresh story.

Amazon met with the Russo brothers and several other writers before they eventually handed the show to JD Payne and Patrick McKay who are the showrunners of the series today.

For more on The Rings of Power, check out our The Rings of Power season 3 review and our breakdown of The Rings of Power season 3 release schedule.

GTA 6 needed a dedicated team to make sure all its different body types could share animations: 'It was a huge team effort'

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • We don't know precisely how massive GTA 6's "big boy" budget was, but let's put aside the alarming excess of contemporary mass-consumption entertainment for a moment and talk about the real big boy: bulked up Jason.
  • While GTA 6's body morphing might not go quite as far (in terms of waistband measurements) as its predecessor San Andreas—or even a game like Fable 2—it does boast extensive variety of different body shapes among its cast, and making that work at such a high level of visual fidelity took an entire dedicated team.
  • In an interview with IGN, Rockstar vice president of animation Mark Tennant noted it was an early decision in development to "push the variation in character sizes and body types … This required us to establish a very robust way to share animations between characters while still resolving multiple points of contact, such as most vehicle interactions and grappling in hand-to-hand combat.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We don't know precisely how massive GTA 6's "big boy" budget was, but let's put aside the alarming excess of contemporary mass-consumption entertainment for a moment and talk about the real big boy: bulked up Jason.

While GTA 6's body morphing might not go quite as far (in terms of waistband measurements) as its predecessor San Andreas—or even a game like Fable 2—it does boast extensive variety of different body shapes among its cast, and making that work at such a high level of visual fidelity took an entire dedicated team.

In an interview with IGN, Rockstar vice president of animation Mark Tennant noted it was an early decision in development to "push the variation in character sizes and body types … This required us to establish a very robust way to share animations between characters while still resolving multiple points of contact, such as most vehicle interactions and grappling in hand-to-hand combat.".

It also took eschewing a "traditional approach" in favor of "fresh techniques," the sort I imagine you can only implement at Rockstar levels of budget and manpower. "We also had to grow a team dedicated to overseeing the implementation, which required close collaboration with the art and rigging teams," stated Tennant. "All these aspects needed to come together to make it work, so it was a huge team effort.".

It has been revealed that in the same IGN piece, senior technical art director Valmor Garcia remarked the ultimate goal was to ensure each character had "singular awareness and visual identities," which included giving them unique faces and anatomy (the six-figure animation count is part of that too, I imagine). All the blood, sweat, and so on seem to be paying off given the game's absolutely massive launch, but Saints Row 3 is still the only crime sandbox that lets me replace all my character's dialog with meaningless zombie grunts, so it's impossible to say which is better.
