GTA 6 developers at Rockstar are worried about being laid off after shipping "the biggest game of all time"

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (440 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rockstar has successfully shipped Grand Theft Auto 6, after years of work and more than a billion dollars spent.
  • But that may not be enough to prevent layoffs at Rockstar, some people working within the studio fear.
  • "After the big day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it's hard not to worry about what the future holds," Uriarte wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar has successfully shipped Grand Theft Auto 6, after years of work and more than a billion dollars spent. GTA 6 is already one of the highest-rated games ever - Eurogamer awarded it five stars in our GTA 6 review - and it's expected to be among the most successful, best-selling games ever.

But that may not be enough to prevent layoffs at Rockstar, some people working within the studio fear. Nestor Uriarte, an animation programmer at Rockstar North, wrote about their concern for their job and those of their colleagues in an article on The Guardian.

"After the big day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it's hard not to worry about what the future holds," Uriarte wrote. "It says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".

Uriarte's piece comes as Rockstar staff's efforts to establish a union reach a critical point. A tribunal between the studio and fired IWBG union members just concluded, though the verdict may not arrive for many weeks or months.

According to recent reports, rockstar's UK studios are currently voting on recognising an official Rockstar workers union. Uriarte is in support of it and has urged colleagues to vote in favour of it. Results of that vote are expected today.

"Winning union recognition would be a huge step forward in securing a meaningful say over our conditions at Rockstar, but its significance would reach far beyond that," Uriarte pointed out.

"As one of the biggest and most influential game studios in the world, what happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry - one in which workers' voices are taken into account more.".

Across its 12 offices around the world, Rockstar's headcount grew to 4,711 during GTA 6's development - double its size when it released Red Dead Redemption 2.

Sources indicate that as popular and profitable as Rockstar's games are, the firm has initiated layoffs in the past after shipping a major project. While there's no way of knowing whether the same is going to happen for GTA 6, the justifiable concerns - given the current state of the industry - are there. According to the ASGC Games Industry Layoffs Tracker, more than 12,000 developers have lost their jobs this year so far, up from more than 9,000 people last year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Early on in GTA 6, you'll gain access to the JoySystem, a game console with a handful of games you can play. One of those is Tenebrae Lux, a black and white, first-person puzzle game. In this GTA 6 guide, we have a Tenebrae Lux walkthrough, guiding you through the puzzles to reach the ending.

Tenebrae Lux features randomised elements in some of its puzzles, so your experience may vary from what you see in our images and videos.

Below is our walkthrough of Tenebrae Lux, revealing puzzle solutions and where to find notes.

There are 11 notes to collect in total, but the last two require you to collect the previous nine.

In a single playthrough of Tenebrae Lux, you can find those 9 notes hidden in 17 possible locations. Collecting these 9 notes will then allow you to find the 10th and 11th notes.

After waking up on the island, you must solve at least three grid-based puzzles located on the beach, though there are five to find in total — two of which are necessary if you're looking for every note.

As is the case with all the other Board Puzzles, Board Puzzle #1 is randomly selected from a batch of puzzles; you won't always be presented with the same one.

According to recent reports, the goal is to input the correct string of numbers into the telephone on the back wall. However, there is no defined phone number for you to use; it is a randomised solution.

To learn the phone number, you must pass through several incarnations of the same room to discover differences in the environment, one by one.

Monopoly Go x The Simpsons crossover is almost here

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Monopoly Go players have been looking forward to a major crossover event for what felt like months, and though most of the details ended up leaking, nothing actually beats official information.
  • The world of The Simpsons has officially arrived in Monopoly Go, and there's a whole lot for players to dive into.
  • Industry observers note that available June 3 through July 29, the new event allows Monopoly Go players to jump in the world of The Simpsons.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Monopoly Go players have been looking forward to a major crossover event for what felt like months, and though most of the details ended up leaking, nothing actually beats official information.

The world of The Simpsons has officially arrived in Monopoly Go, and there's a whole lot for players to dive into. The show's creative team even produced a new animated short, featuring Mr. Monopoly, and Mr. Burns.

Industry observers note that available June 3 through July 29, the new event allows Monopoly Go players to jump in the world of The Simpsons. You'll be able to build, and explore all around multiple iconic locations from the show.

Along the way, you'll run into Simpsons characters like Homer, Marge, Bart, Lisa, and of course, Mr. Burns. Developer Scopely teamed up with the show's creative team to create many references, and Easter Eggs for you to discover. You'll find some of those on chance cards, but most of the world has been changed to be part of The Simpsons, including getting to bribe Chief Wiggum to escape jail.

The developer promises a deeply connected world with Simpsons narratives and characters that alter seasonal maps, and offer unique sticker sets and animated sequences to dive in. Incidentally, this is The Simpsons' first appearance in a mobile-exclusive game in 13 years.

Here's a breakdown of everything you can expect, straight from Scopely:.

It has been revealed that episodes: Narrative-driven encounters that create stories inspired by The Simpsons. Episodes play out across seasonal boards, sticker sets, and minigames, all capped off with an animated short.

Industry observers note that sticker sets: Every Episode comes with its own limited-time sticker set, taking cues from the latest Simpsons story. Collectible artwork, character journeys and other rewards are yours to claim for the duration of each Episode.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that in a first substantial enhancement since acquiring SteamDB from its founders back in September, the owners of Nexus Mods have outlined some latest additions coming to , the two sides in the deal have declared some additions coming to the community-run backend database.
  • "We're now a couple of months in since [the takeover] announcement, so I thought it was about time we shared a quick patch on what we've been working on behind the scenes, along with a few changes you'll start to see rolling out over the coming weeks," Victor Folmann, CEO of Nexus Mods owners Chosen wrote in a blog post on SteamDB.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that in a first substantial enhancement since acquiring SteamDB from its founders back in September, the owners of Nexus Mods have outlined some latest additions coming to , the two sides in the deal have declared some additions coming to the community-run backend database. Affiliate links aimed at providing options to help folks find the cheapest price for a game and a new tab dedicated to the mods Nexus host for a game are incoming, as work on behind-the-scenes improvements continues.

"We're now a couple of months in since [the takeover] announcement, so I thought it was about time we shared a quick patch on what we've been working on behind the scenes, along with a few changes you'll start to see rolling out over the coming weeks," Victor Folmann, CEO of Nexus Mods owners Chosen wrote in a blog post on SteamDB.

In a recent development, there are two main new features he pointed to that you'll notice popping up on SteamDB soon. The first is one that anyone could have seen coming, a new tab on each moddable game's page that shows off some mods hosted for it on Nexus Mods and a host of modding-related data. "The new tab will help you discover mods for games you're browsing on SteamDB, making it easier to see whether a game has an active modding community and explore what it has to offer," Fomann wrote. "For now, we'll only be showing mods from Nexus Mods, as we already have access to that wealth of modding data, making it a straightforward starting point for this new feature.

"We appreciate that some of you might be wondering why we're not including Steam Workshop, too. It's certainly something we'd be open to exploring as we develop the feature further, along with other modding sources. With that in mind, if you run a modding website and would be interested in having your community's mods included, we'd love to hear from you.".

In a recent development, that seems perfectly fine, but the other incoming feature's a bit more controversial given SteamDB's historically not been all about the money. "One thing we've seen people ask for is an easier way to find the cheapest place to buy a game, and we're now working on making that possible," Folmann wrote. "We'll be introducing affiliate links to authorised game retailers, giving you more options when looking for the best available price on a game.

It has been revealed that "We recognise that introducing affiliate links may raise some concerns, so we want to be clear about how they'll work. First and foremost, as I mentioned, we'll only feature authorised retailers; we will not be including grey-market resellers. We've also made a deliberate decision about how prices are displayed: retailers will be ordered by the cheapest available price in your currency, not by whichever retailer offers us the highest affiliate commission. If a retailer doesn't offer pricing in your currency, we'll still show deals in other currencies provided they are available in your region.".

Folmann was clear in the initial announcement of the takeover that Nexus Mods' bosses would be actively looking into ways SteamDB could make more money to sustain itself, so the addition of these links isn't out of the blue either. Whether SteamDB regulars agree that they're a "lighter-touch" way of earning the site some cash without detracting from the traditional experience of using it is another matter. I'll need to see how I feel once I've actually navigated a few pages with the links in as part of looking up stuff about games, but my first instinct is that as long as the pages don't end up revolving around the links and it's still easy to get to the info you want without interacting with them, I probably won't be too put out.

Beyond those tweaks, Folmann mentioned "improvements to how updates are tested before they go live" and how rapidly the team can react to concerns have been among the less obvious work going on behind the scenes. "We're still in the early stages of what we want to achieve, and there's plenty more work we need to do and would like to work on," he wrote in closing.

Folmann and co only took over Nexus Mods in June last year, making them still relatively fresh custodians of both it and SteamDB.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The search for secrets in World of Warcraft: Forever continues ever onwards, with a latest breakthrough coming to light in recent days. The latest discovery? An elusive new cat that can be tamed by hunters in one of the game's new zones.

It has been revealed that the cat's name is Ta'Shkal, and they can be found on Mount Hyjal. An endgame levelling zone, players will have to reach at least level 57 in order to safely make their way up there and recruit this new pet.

The way you do so is relatively simple. You need to find a small corrupted cat figuring within the Felblood Scar region of Mount Hyjal. Once you've found that, you then need to travel up to a hidden lantern south of the Mourning's Rest area. With the figurine in your bags, you'll be able to interact with the lantern, spawning the cat for you to tame (granted you're playing a hunter).

So what's the significant deal about this cat? Well, aside from the fact it's got a strange colour scheme of green fur with orange stripes, the cat also has a base attack speed of 1.0. This means it'll attack once every second, which is pretty fast and allows for greater damage output from your pet. This inherently makes the pet valuable for endgame hunter players, who are looking to improve their performance in PvE and PvP.

Recent findings suggest that this is not the only secret discovered by World of Warcraft: Forever sleuths. Last week, they pieced together a hidden quest chain that leads to two special swords. As of writing, only one has been found, though progress continues in pursuit of the second.

The game has been out for just over two weeks now, and continues to prove popular among new and returning players. It's the biggest launch in the series' history, and has gone down well with people so far. Even if it has recently suffered its first controversy with a now-fixed gold exploit.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 launches on console today.
  • In an article supporting this month's union vote at Rockstar North, one of the game's animation programmers argues that "workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".
  • The animation programmer in question is Nestor Uriarte, writing in The Guardian's Comment Is Free section.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 launches on console today. It's widely expected to sell more copies than main character Lucia Caminos has skin pores, more copies than there are words even in Eurogamer's five-star review, which I believe Chris Tapsell has written specifically to exhaust and destroy such neurones as I have remaining. And yet, staff at Rockstar Games are apparently worrying about being laid off, as development winds down and investors start to bicker about Line Going Up Even More.

In an article supporting this month's union vote at Rockstar North, one of the game's animation programmers argues that "workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".

The animation programmer in question is Nestor Uriarte, writing in The Guardian's Comment Is Free section. Following some personal reflections on his time at the studio, he calls on other Rockstar devs to get behind the union, describing it as both "a huge step forward" for a company that has previously faced allegations of "crunch culture", and a win for UK game developers at large. "What happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry – one in which workers’ voices are taken into account more," Uriarte writes.

Recent findings suggest that the vote at Rockstar North will run till 26th November, and could give rise to a union spanning over 1600 developers, according to umbrella organisation the Independent Workers of Great Britain. If that comes to pass, it would make the Rockstar union the largest recognised videogame developer union in the UK.

It comes as the company and a group of fired workers await the result of an employment tribunal battle over alleged "union-busting". Rockstar has accused the workers in question of "gross misconduct" and a breach of confidentiality by means of a union Discord server. Amongst other things, the legal brawl has revealed that Rockstar had a mole on that server for two and a half years, prior to the firings.

As for the prospect of further job losses, after GTA 6 goes on sale, Uriarte cites a wave of mass layoffs across the industry that has affected the creators of even commercially successful games like Battlefield 6 and Netflix's FIFA World Cup.

According to recent reports, "After the big day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it’s hard not to worry about what the future holds," he writes. "Studios across the industry have been slashing huge portions of their workforces, with an estimated 24,000 roles axed globally over the last two years. It notes a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".

According to recent reports, the obvious context here is that GTA 6 has been a massively expensive production, with a development team headcount in the thousands. While one could accuse Uriarte of fear-mongering, I do find it hard to believe that executives at parent organization Take-Two aren't weighing up some timely "down-sizing" right now. In general, videogame companies have a long tradition of axing the books once a game has been shipped, despite arguments that keeping experienced teams intact often pays off. In Rockstar's case, however, it's also worth bearing in mind that the GTA 6 rolling out this week is only part of the package. There's also the hazy prospect of the next incarnation of GTA Online, which – going by GTA 5 sales – will be a money spinner for many years, and will require a sizeable staff to maintain. Oh, and of course there's the PC version.

According to recent reports, echoing many peers, Uriarte also argues in his piece that it's important to unionise now in order to negotiate proper protection against generative AI cost-cutting initiatives. "The rapid emergence of AI is transforming how studios work and raising fundamental questions about the future of our industry," he continues. "Across the sector, the skills that workers spend years developing risk being devalued as their creative work is replaced by AI.

"Rockstar has mentioned it is committed to preserving jobs and it has been clear that our games will continue to be made by people," Urirarte concedes. "But with recognition we’d have a seat at the table to manage this industry-wide transition together.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Unreal Engine 6 will not launch with the engine's long-standard Blueprints scripting system.
  • "UE6, including UE6 Early Access, won’t include Blueprints or the Actor Gameplay Framework.
  • Recent findings suggest that "In June, we remarked Blueprints and Actors would coexist in UE6 Early Access and 6.0, so UE5 projects could upgrade incrementally while the new Scene Graph framework matures.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unreal Engine 6 will not launch with the engine's long-standard Blueprints scripting system. The news came in a Friday, November 19 post on the Unreal Engine website, written by Epic Games executive vice president of development, Marcus Wassmer. Here's Wassmer's top-level summary from the post:.

"UE6, including UE6 Early Access, won’t include Blueprints or the Actor Gameplay Framework. Gameplay will be built in Verse and on the new Scene Graph framework.

Recent findings suggest that "In June, we remarked Blueprints and Actors would coexist in UE6 Early Access and 6.0, so UE5 projects could upgrade incrementally while the new Scene Graph framework matures. However, with recent advances in AI capability, we expect AI to massively help with converting UE5 projects to UE6, if not make that process fully automatic. That also means we can deliver UE6 on time (or sooner!) while meeting its design goals: a new data model, a Verse-first architecture, modularity, and AI operability.".

Recent findings suggest that blueprints have not (and it appears, will not) be deprecated in Unreal Engine 5, and the company maintains that projects will still be easy to convert from UE5 to UE6. Wassmer cited a declining cost in AI task completion as one reason for this belief, as well as the team's ongoing, but apparently successful conversion of Fortnite's Blueprint library to UE6's Verse programming language through an AI-assisted process.

Blueprints are a widely-used feature of Unreal. Former Valve developer Chet Faliszek, an AI skeptic, has put out a vlog on the subject. Essentially, Faliszek argues that Blueprints (and features like them in other game engines) represent a middle ground between artistic and technical work, an introduction and skill builder for less technically-minded developers. Without them, such developers seemingly have to either learn Verse code, or integrate LLM prompting into their workflows.

Recent findings suggest that "We made a newly introduced skill in the middle there, between normal and expert," Faliszek stated of intermediate tools like Blueprints. "To lose that determinism from game design, and instead have to prompt AI⁠—or write your own Verse … It's losing those tools that made all those designers and all those artists so powerful, to be able to do really powerful things and have access to really deep-down things, but in a safe way that the engineers can decide what that meant to them.".

According to recent reports, A dark horse game of the year candidate, the first-person RPG Queen's Domain, was made with Unreal Engine. I recently spoke to co-developer Eric Berger, who specialized in art and design alongside the more technically-focused Bradley Boothe, a relationship that rhymes with the ones Faliszek outlined in his video.

I spoke to Berger before seeing Epic's latest press release, but Berger already indicated that Unreal's AI pivot is prompting Freshly Baked Games to switch engines for its next project. I followed up with Berger about this Blueprint news, and the developer noted that Blueprints were a major part of the workflow on Queen's Domain.

Recent findings suggest that I'm a layman in game development, but I think Wassmer's post elides that there is a large qualitative difference between doing any work via LLM prompt versus the old-fashioned way⁠—I don't like or want to use these tools, myself, and I don't think that's an unpopular stance. Commenter ZILtoid1991 on Faliszek's video compared the move to Apple removing headphone jacks on the iPhone, a comparison I find fruitful.

From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews.

It was hugely unpopular at the time, and is still derided by enthusiasts, but it also worked. Other manufacturers copied Apple, and everybody has bluetooth headphones now⁠—or Apple's own, proprietary Air Pods. But Apple had far less success trying something similar with its laptops: The lack of ports on late 2010s Macbooks proved disastrous, and Apple has since reintroduced more (and a wider variety of) ports on newer models of the popular line. I certainly have my own anti-AI, pro-headphone jack preferences, but we'll have to see how this plays out with the Unreal Engine.

I have double-checked and yes, original 'GTA killer' Driv3r really was that rubbish

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1225 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • At this point the tragedy of Driv3r, or Driver 3, or my personal favourite Drive-thrur, is well thumbed.
  • Recent findings suggest that A more widely forgotten detail is that, for a while, there was a non-zero chance - a belief, even - that Drive Three Er was going to be the opposite.
  • Recent findings suggest that you likely know the rest, though one of the dangers of familiarity is the subsequent breeding of complacency, which in this case can manifest as a thawing acceptance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At this point the tragedy of Driv3r, or Driver 3, or my personal favourite Drive-thrur, is well thumbed. A familiar litany of unrealised ambition, heinous bugs, dull open-world design, and an expensive yet audibly bored voice cast, the accidental comedic highlight of which is Michelle Rodriguez flatly reeling off car theft orders from what sounds like the inside of a Michelle Rodriguez-sized tupperware container.

Recent findings suggest that A more widely forgotten detail is that, for a while, there was a non-zero chance - a belief, even - that Drive Three Er was going to be the opposite. The 2003-2004 hype cycle had sowed the notion that this would in fact be the open-world crime thriller to knock Grand Theft Auto off its perch, and even 22 years before GTA 6's idolising reviews, that was no small promise; Rockstar were still enjoying the balmy success of Vice City, and we could see San Andreas cresting the hill on a stolen, shining BMX. "Ah, but did they have Michael Madsen doing doughnuts in car parks?," publishers Atari asked the world, either unaware or in denial of the spluttering, clapped-out rattletrap they were about to wheel into the showroom.

Recent findings suggest that you likely know the rest, though one of the dangers of familiarity is the subsequent breeding of complacency, which in this case can manifest as a thawing acceptance. I succumbed to this myself, having recently installed a legally unlinkable copy of Drivethreeuh, mind opened to the possibility that maybe it wasn't that bad. Six hours later, I am here to tell you: it was.

Recent findings suggest that almost nothing here works, figuratively and literally. Within three minutes of the opening mission, before Madsen's undercover cop Tanner goes undercover, you're ordered to join some marked police cars to head for a bust – but because the rozzers' primary function is to give chase to you, later on, driving too close crosses their wires, provoking them into blue-on-blue ramming maneuvres. Later, in a motorbike sprint down an inexplicably exploding beach, cartel goons are positioned across the sand, presumably to take drama-enhancing pot shots. They're so slow, however, both to notice your presence and to physically raise their guns, that they're barely out of their idle animations by the time you whizz past. And your own guy isn't much better: an assassination mission, which ends with your target cornered from an elevated position, requires that you take a few steps backwards first, as Tanner can't drop his shootin' arms low enough to land a hit from the balcony he's on.

Unlike Vice City's Tommy Vercetti, he can at least swim, which by 2004 standards gives the seaside Miami and Nice maps a fair verisimilitude, particularly when a shot-up boat engine forces the abandoning of ship. No amount of product-of-its-time concessions, though, can account for how woodenly unpalatable the on-foot action is. Controls are stiff and shooting feels meaningless, with zero tangible sense of bullets being sent nor received; killing a man carries all the weight of just shouting at him to lie down, and if it weren't for sound effects and the dwindling health bar, I could park Tanner in front of a firing squad of identically-modelled thugs with almost zero impression that his lungs were filling with Uzi rounds.

Industry observers note that driver, of course, began as a pure wheelman sim, later installments only letting you hoof it after someone at developers Reflections began smelling that Rockstar money. It was therefore always unlikely, even for the purported GTA killer, that this would achieve action-adventure sophistication in its bipedal bits. Even so, god, it's woeful. Stingy checkpointing also means that failure is often punished by having to replay those tedious, flavourless shootouts in full.

The driving is better, which is a bit like saying there's decent cheese in this cheese and smallpox toastie. It's reasonably slidey, when throwing the back end through a curving French alleyway, and in contrast to the gunplay, there is a somewhat realised tactility to ploughing around in two tonnes of rolling metal. It has problems of its own, mind. Cars feel okay when they're moving, but contact and crashes are leaden, sluggish, visually underwhelming occasions that I would call non-events, were they not so slow to recover from that a single nasty impact can scupper a timed mission. Granted, I quickly re-learned how vital it is to keep both eyes on the road, as other vehicles, pedestrians, lamposts, and other detritus tend to pop into existence some mere fifty feet in front of my speeding bumper.

The result, of both this graphical shortcoming and the overly punishing crashes, is a getaway car sim that too often encourages you to drive like cataract-ridden grandparent. Worse, whoever put Letty Ortiz in a lunchbox must have also been in charge of the engine noises, producing an array of miserable high-rev dins – especially for the motorbikes, which screech like amateurishly autotuned vacuum cleaners. There are also shades of that deranged cop AI in ordinary commuters, who I've repeatedly seen swerving and slaloming around empty lanes, seemingly for no reason beyond violent confusion.

It has been revealed that strangely enough, my 2026 return has largely dodged the game's infamous glitchiness, the worst instance of physics defiance being a garage door that appeared to lift Tanner into the air before propelling him, incorporeally, through the car shed's roof. I recall much worse, from the days when I'd have my dad rent it for me from Blockbuster. Mission-critical NPCs getting stuck on walls; flipped pursuit cars spinning endlessly; getting flung into space when walking on an overturned vehicle (a common occurrence, given the actual 'crawling out' animation sometimes failed to play, the game instead teleporting you onto the spring-loaded underside instead).

Sources indicate that I've thus far escaped these, but as far as I know, they're still lurking dormant, and none of what I've witnessed with adult eyes has been funny or stupid enough to imbue Driv3r 3 The Third with a Wiseauean so-bad-it's-good quality. It's just bad. It was always bad. Why did I even entertain the possibility that it wasn't bad?

In a recent development, reflections, to their credit, accepted their folly. Narratively unrelated sequel Driver: Parallel Lines tucked away a bin full of discarded copies, at least until Ubisoft bought up the series and patched it out, and for all the fantastical coma silliness of direct followup Driver: San Francisco, that was sensible enough to keep Tanner where he best belongs: hands on the wheel, foot on the gas, gun holstered. And was a far, far better game for it, too.

As 2011's San Francisco launch also remains the most recent Driver release, I regretfully can't end with the assurance that DrIIIver's legacy is a mere blip on a redeemed franchise. That stain stank, and did for ages, very possibly to the extent that GTA's one-time biggest rival never recovered.

Sources indicate that still, even if Reflections couldn't fully turn around their fortunes, the consistent improvement from this to Parallel Lines to San Francisco highlighted that they did learn something. Maybe so too did anyone else who went on to make an open-world action game. Which wouldn't be the worst outcome; after all, those who do not learn from gnarled, stinking wrecks like this are doomed to repeat them.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, ryan Cohen, CEO of GameStop - the self-proclaimed "world's largest retail gaming and trade-in destination" - is not happy with the emerging trend of games releasing without discs.
  • In an interview with Bloomberg, Cohen explained: "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend.
  • Sources indicate that these comments come in the wake of GTA 6's launch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, ryan Cohen, CEO of GameStop - the self-proclaimed "world's largest retail gaming and trade-in destination" - is not happy with the emerging trend of games releasing without discs. Per the CEO, the industry's move away from physical games and towards a digital-only future is harmful to both consumers and businesses.

In an interview with Bloomberg, Cohen explained: "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend. Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it’s also hurt GameStop.".

Sources indicate that these comments come in the wake of GTA 6's launch. The game, expected to be the biggest video game launch of all time, is not shipping on discs at all. Even if you purchase a physical copy of the game, what you will actually take home is a 'code in a box' - giving you a code you can redeem on your console of choice that entitles you to a digital version of the game. GTA 6 is not the first game to do this, but it is the most high-profile. Similarly to discs, codes are also region-locked (at least on the PS5), meaning that the proliferation of codes as a format isn't even helping make games more readily available in certain markets.

Recent findings suggest that cohen notes he's been in conversation with "the obvious [publishers]" but that he's had little sway on their looks. "Of course they don’t like [trade-ins] because removing a used copy eliminates an alternative to buying newly introduced," he told Bloomberg. "They're taking away competition.".

Recent findings suggest that though Cohen doesn't name GTA 6 specifically in the Bloomberg interview, it's clear that he's talking about Rockstar's megaton launch (he explicitly tweeted "GTA. On a disc. In a case. On your shelf. Like if you still want a physical copy" two days ago). The lack of trade-in potential is clearly harming his business; the Bloomberg article reveals pre-owned and refurbished products make up 22% of the GameStop's sales, down 32 percent from the same time a year ago.

Industry observers note that of course, the proliferation of game-in-a-box products doesn't end with GTA 6. Sony aims to stop producing physical discs for newly introduced PlayStation games starting in January 2028, moving to a digital-only model despite pushback from consumers and certain developers and publishers. The outcry is doing little to influence Sony's decision, however.

Disc or no disc, GTA 6 is expected to cross $2bn in its opening weekend, and at the moment that is looking like a conservative figure, too. It's estimated the game has sold well over 19.05m units at the time of writing. Despite the astronomical sales, though, employees at Rockstar are still worried about layoffs. Additionally, a tribunal between the studio and fired IWBG union members (who were fired for apparent breaches of their NDAs) just concluded, though the verdict may not arrive for many weeks or months.

If you need a hand with any of the myriad things GTA 6 asks you to do, you can read Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Sony has shared a selection of staggering statistics relating to the launch of GTA 6 on PS5.

From launch on 19th November through to the end of the title's opening weekend, Sony recorded over 39 million unique players.

The game set a latest record on PlayStation for the highest number of concurrent players on any game.

PS5 players have logged 683 million hours of GTA 6 playtime, and on average, every owner on PlayStation has played it for 17.4 hours.

Industry observers note that outside of the console's launch and Christmas holidays, the launch of GTA 6 resulted in "the largest number of newly connected PS5 consoles on a single day". GTA 6 was the first game played on 70% of those newly introduced PS5 systems.

In a recent development, the day after release, Rockstar Games announced GTA 6 had sold 32.5 million units across PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. With these upcoming stats from PlayStation, we know it's sold over 39 million copies on PS5 alone, as of yesterday.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 will continue to sell for years to come, as there'll be a PC version next year along with a brand latest iteration of GTA Online. We've got a 10/10-rated GTA 6 PS5 review on the site, and we're working on our comprehensive GTA 6 guide right now.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that if you've been looking to pick up a newly introduced DualSense Wireless Controller for your PS5 in the Black Friday sales, then you'll have noticed that the discounts are quite uneven.
  • There seems to be an exception, though.
  • In a recent development, currys' PS5 DualSense controller discounts match other retailers', but with much more selection.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that if you've been looking to pick up a newly introduced DualSense Wireless Controller for your PS5 in the Black Friday sales, then you'll have noticed that the discounts are quite uneven. While most retailers are discounting the extras to roughly the same £43 price point, the actual models of controllers reduced vary wildly by store.

There seems to be an exception, though. The Currys PlayStation Black Friday sales have struck a wide array of color models for DualSense controllers; the selection is much more varied than Amazon's, with colorways reduced that aren't discounted elsewhere. That includes the DualSense's premium versions, like the sought-after Icon Blue retro model, as well as the perhaps controversial yellow-and-black Wolverine limited edition controller.

In a recent development, currys' PS5 DualSense controller discounts match other retailers', but with much more selection. By my count, eight different colorways are reduced from the eleven stocked at the retailer, including the vibrant pink and camo-patterned models, as well as some standard alternatives.

Industry observers note that some of Sony's more premium DualSense colorways are seeing discounts too: the Icon Blue and Wolverine Limited Edition models are among them. These function the same as the normal models, but with more unique designs. Not only are they not on sale at rival retailers, but some don't even stock them at full price.

If you buy one of these controllers from Currys, you get an additional benefit which we'll loosely chalk up as a 'Black Friday extra'.

The premium DualSense controllers are functionally identical to the standard ones. Don't buy one and expect to suddenly get better at your favorite game.

The real reason to buy one is to celebrate your fandom of whatever the controller is inspired by. If you loved the Wolverine game earlier this year (or, more realistically, the character), that controller might be a fun one to add to your collection. Icon Blue was part of a series Sony put out about a year ago, celebrating the cerulean tone which is closely associated with the PlayStation brand, but it was pretty hard to find stock of when it first released.

Unfortunately, other limited edition DualSense colorways aren't seeing the same level of discounts at Currys, but are a bit more affordable than their launch prices of £74.99. For example, the 007 First Light controller isn't officially reduced with a Black Friday discount, but it is sitting at £56 at the retailer. Meanwhile, Amazon has it listed for £87.99. Other limited edition DualSense colorways at Currys under that £74.99 price include the Chroma, Pearl, and Remix versions. Unsurprisingly, the GTA 6 model isn't seeing any kind of price reduction at the moment.

If you're worried about buying a controller now, thinking they could get cheaper in the coming week of sales, I'd imagine that's unlikely. Most retailers reduce DualSenses to the same price each year, and we're already seeing multiple hit this £43 mark; it seems that's where they'll stay.

We're keeping tabs on all the best Black Friday deals for gamers, which includes all the Black Friday PS5 deals worth going for. And if you need a PS5 controller but don't feel like you need to stick to a DualSense, we've got a round-up of the best PS5 controllers you can buy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that britney Spears has made a celebrity fashion statement once or twice in her lifetime, and a recent run of lacy, sheer dresses has been credited to a look she wore back in 2001. While her VMAs dress that year still lands on lists of fans’ favorite fashion looks, I think the look predates this, and credit might actually go to Catherine Zeta Jones, here.

First, let’s talk about the Spears LBD. After an influx of see-through dresses have invaded red carpet events in recent weeks, people are talking about Spears’ Dolce & Gabbana 2001 dress (which is one VMAs memory I do hope she remembers). It was fitting everywhere but around the wrists and forearms, where the dress flared. She paired the fully sheer dress with a black bra and low-rise underwear, and I’m pretty sure I can remember her “cool girl” chewing gum while she walked onto the red carpet. Here’s the dress.

I would never take away any of the wonder around this Spears look. She’s always known how to rock a little black dress, but this is like the holy grail of dresses and it's almost impossible to emulate. I actually think the recent trend of black lace on celebs looks more like a fit Catherine Zeta-Jones once wore, and we can thank her daughter Carys Douglas for reminding us.

Industry observers note that carys Douglas dons her famous mom’s clothing periodically, so when she wore a Gucci top her own mother had worn as part of an ensemble back in 1996 for The Long Kiss Goodnight premiere, it wasn’t a big surprise. Though Zeta-Jones’ original fit included sheer pants, Douglas repurposed the gorgeous top with a skirt for a Gucci event that feels like the silhouette designers have been going for with black lace of late. Take a look.

For comparison’s sake, here’s Catherine Zeta-Jones in the look in 1996.

I really do think the Entrapment actress’ look not only came before Spears’ iconic fashion moment, but it’s also similar to what we’ve seen on younger actresses recently. Gucci also deserves a little bit of credit for being ahead of the curve, and also for putting together some stunning looks, including this one from Dakota Johnson, when the sheer trend came back. Recently, Mckenna Grace wore a similar fit for The Hunger Games. Then Hailee Steinfeld stepped out in a sheer black dress that definitely reminded me of Douglas and her mom.

We’re heading into winter, and we typically see a lot of black after the browns of fall fade out, but I just wanted to give an icon her due where I feel it is due. Though Ms. Spears’ dress is one I will always be thinking about.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that please note, this guide contains massive spoilers for some of the endings of Grand Theft Auto 6. If you don't want to know what happens, please stop reading!

There are multiple endings to GTA 6, and not all the endings take place in the same location. One of the potential final scenes during the GTA 6 story mission, The End of the Road, takes place on a bridge in the Leonida Keys.

According to recent reports, after discovering the cops are onto them, Jason and Lucia drive away from Cal's house and head to Brian's marina to find an airplane. The police rapidly trap them on a bridge with a roadblock ahead and multiple cars behind them. Lucia wants to keep going but Jason thinks it's all over for them. The player is then given a choice, "Swim for it" or "No Surrender.".

It has been revealed that AGAIN, MASSIVE SPOILERS BELOW! STOP NOW IF YOU DON'T WANT TO KNOW THE ENDINGS!

Jason and Lucia decide Tomas is better off without them in his life. They drive through the roadblock, shooting at the cops. They're both shot to death and we see them dead in the front seat of the car, still holding hands. During the end credits, we see Tomas living happily with Lucia's aunt and her husband and children.

Jason and Lucia decide to jump off the bridge and swim to freedom.

It has been revealed that however, a second choice appears once you've chosen 'Swim for it.' As Jason gets out of the car, a prompt for Lucia to 'Exit' the car appears. You can choose for Lucia to follow through with the plan by pressing the button, or change your mind and let the prompt expire.

Recent findings suggest that A: 'Swim for it' and 'Exit': The couple will get out of the car together and walk to the edge of the bridge. Lucia jumps but Jason does not, letting himself get arrested by the cops. During the credits, Lucia signs the deal which keeps her free and sends Jason to prison. We see her bring Tomas to visit him, so Jason finally meets his son, though it's through glass.

B: 'Swim for it' and don't 'Exit': If you choose to swim for it but don't choose the 'Exit' prompt, Jason will get out of the car but Lucia will remain in the car. The police will open fire and kill them both. As with the No Surrender option, we see Tomas living with Lucia's aunt's family.

C: 'Swim for it' and 'Exit' (with $2 million in Buck Me savings): If you delayed the Protective Custody mission of GTA 6 until you had deposited $2 million in savings, the Swim for it and Exit choices will show the same results, but during the credits, Lucia uses the money to get Jason released from prison. Lucia picks him up at prison, and Jason meets Tomas and holds his hand.

It has been revealed that note: These are not the only endings to GTA 6. I've seen several more endings that do not take place on the bridge at all and don't involve these particular choices.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that the web pages of Lifeinvadder, Bleeter, and Eyefind have instead given way to BuckMe, Scooter Bros, and WhatUp apps.
  • "It didn't feel necessary for us," Rockstar North boss Rob Nelson told Kotaku.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The internet of today is a far cry from the days when Grand Theft Auto 5 was released, which is partly why Rockstar didn't bring back its own satirical version of the web in GTA 6.

Recent findings suggest that the web pages of Lifeinvadder, Bleeter, and Eyefind have instead given way to BuckMe, Scooter Bros, and WhatUp apps. The reason? Smartphone apps just made more sense.

"It didn't feel necessary for us," Rockstar North boss Rob Nelson told Kotaku. "We definitely wanted to lean into apps and create these apps.".

Though some of the apps in GTA 6 perform similar tasks to the web of old, Nelson mentioned the team didn't want players to be distracted from the game's detailed open world by staring at screens. That also extends to getting players to appreciate the value of money, and witnessing the progression of Jason and Lucia as they go from pawnshop robberies to staging major bank heists.

"They don't really need websites to be buying a lot of shit, you know what I mean, and so everything grows very organically," Nelson remarked, adding that websites may return in the future.

Recent findings suggest that "I remember asking Stu Petri, our head of 2D and UI, about websites, and he was like, 'For what? What do you need it for?' So, that was it," he added.

In materials supplied by Rockstar ahead of our review, Sam Grosset (associate UI director at the studio) also explained that a lot of thought went into how the apps work, and how easily the phone needed to fit into your play style in order for it to work as effectively as possible.

"We ensure the UI feels like a natural extension of the game world, supporting players without interrupting gameplay or breaking immersion, unless necessary to do so," said Grosset. "The UI should be complementary to the game and appropriate for each scenario. It was a massive shift for our phone interface to be in-hand, but it supports that feeling of playing as Jason or Lucia and helps us stay embedded in the world.".

Rockstar would continually "raise the bar, question assumptions, explore latest possibilities, and learn through rigorous testing and iteration" in order to make these apps - and the UX/UI in general - feel in line with the production quality of the rest of the game.

In Eurogamer's GTA 6 review, Chris Tapsell awarded the open-world crime game five stars, raving about its absurd level of detail, compelling characters, exciting action and of its big heart.

If you're looking to spend the next several days playing Rockstar's latest hit, Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough has detailed guides on everything from individual missions, to core mechanics like the upcoming Wanted Level, and relationship and romance.

This means you can kick off a playthrough as a lowborn leader of a travelling band or a wandering noble with claims on realms ruled by others. No longer are you glued to the throne from day one to the day you quit for good - power's a privilege which can be earned and revoked depending on what you get up to. Though, it's worth noting that only three ways of operating as a landless adventurer are being made free to access with this revision. You can be an aimless wanderers, sword-toting mercenaries, or scholars. If you want your band to earn their living as explorers, free booters, or legitimists, you'll still need Roads to Power.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sigh. Boys. I would say men, but even with his shredded physique and ex-military career, GTA 6 protagonist Jason is such a boy that it goes from being funny to endearing.

Industry observers note that all the signs are there as I explore his beachside stilt house for the first time. Spartan living room furnishings consist of a sofa, coffee table, and a single rickety armchair. A peek in the fridge and pantry confirms my suspicions: the dude is surviving on protein shakes, protein bars, two day old coffee, and maybe a handful of gas station potato chips. Rockstar here pokes fun at every stereotype of the simple, single man, with no partner to appease or even make little considerations for as he goes about his day.

But after Cal's bro time visit to play video games starts with the two men reconfiguring said living room in Lucia's honor, I've decided to reform this bachelor into the ultimate Wife Guy – but why oh why did he have to choose that necklace?!

Sources indicate that I make it my business to do everything that Lucia might appreciate and improve my relationship status in GTA 6. Each interaction that will earn her acknowledgement is signposted with a little pink heart. Home improvements are a big one, but getting sexy is my top priority.

According to recent reports, getting Jason in ship shape for his missus was not hard, at least from a physical perspective. Glancing at the fitness app, I see he's already ripped and has a low bodyfat percentage (what a show-off) at the start of the game, but there's always room for improvement.

From kettlebells to bench presses, squats, and pull ups, Lucia clearly likes her man in tip top shape. My Jason is shredded now – Key Lento's very own beach bum hunk – and I take every opportunity to show flirtatious GTA 6 neighbour Mandy my disinterest in her possibly cannibalistic games. I go so far as to blow off main missions, emerging from the glittering waters outside Jason's crib at 2am to find a text from substantial boss Brian postponing a job because "it's a little late now". I lock in Jason's cardio workout with a protein shake and a cigarette, and go to bed excited to see my gains.

But everything I have done to make Jason the perfect man for Lucia suddenly comes under threat the day before her release. I pick up some spare clothes from Andy, just as she asked. I buy every single thing at the grocery store, including a fancy wine, bread, cereal… you know, real gourmet stuff. I order a bouquet of roses, the most expensive option at the florist. But then I reach Siren's Cove to buy her a necklace and my only choice is a gold-plated alloy chain with a brass pendant.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

In a recent development, it's very clearly a cheap dud of a necklace, aluminum trash sprayed with the thinnest layer of "eight karat" gold – something so flimsy, you'd never find in a real-life jewellers. Still I let the store clerk ply her trade, speaking in hushed, grandiose tones as Jason nods along in complete oblivion, expecting that at some point, Jason might ask what else she has in stock. To my horror, he does not. The necklace is the only option, and it costs $475. It almost makes me cry to hand over the cash for that cheap piece of tin. Not only because Jason just got massively ripped off, but more to the point: what if Lucia hates it?

Sources indicate that again, Rockstar is making fun of the sweet, well-meaning, blissful ignorance that some men have around "girl things". Of course Jason doesn't know that this necklace is garbage. He's a simple dude, just a bro, just an overgrown kid in a man's hard-muscled body. The real lesson isn't to buy your partner the most expensive thing at the store. It's to do little things that will mean a lot to her, even if she's about to discover a nickel allergy she never knew about before.

GTA 6 has been updated to support PS Plus Premium cloud streaming directly to the PS5 and PS Portal.

To be crystal clear about this: the game has not been added to the PS Plus Premium catalogue and you will still need to own it.

However, assuming you’ve purchased the game – and millions of you have – then you’ll now be able to stream it directly from Sony’s servers, assuming you’re a PS Plus Premium member.

Recent findings suggest that there are a number of use cases for this, but the most likely is you’re away from your console and still want to play on your PS Portal. Now you won’t need to rely on Remote Play; you can just stream it directly.

This feature wasn’t available at launch, but I’ve been able to test it on my PS5 here in the UK and it’s working well.

There was some reporting prior to release that Microsoft had secured “exclusive” streaming rights to this title, but they were quickly clarified. This revision now confirms boss Asha Sharma misspoke.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, over the last couple of weeks, some Nvidia owners noticed their SSDs were taking a hammering, reporting their driver's log file was being overwritten constantly, sometimes to the tune of 30 GB every hour. Which obviously isn't great for the lifespan of the valuable SSD you've got it installed on.

In a recent development, given the problem was caused by recent driver updates, rolling back to version 621.01 was the best solution until Nvidia could do something about it. Which they did, releasing a hotfix as version 621.35. It's not available in the GeForce app yet, but you can download it directly from Nvidia's site. Not that you should.

Recent findings suggest that as users on the Nvidia subreddit are reporting, the problem persists. While the hotfix reduces the peak write rate and prevents it for a short while after reboot, it eventually creeps back in. One user reported that overnight the log file was still being rewritten by approximately 4.5 GB every hour.

In a recent development, so yeah, the best solution remains to roll back to version 621.01 and, as always with Nvidia drivers, to hold off on updating to the latest driver until it's been confirmed safe. If this ongoing saga sounds familiar, it's because the same thing happened to AMD's GPU drivers earlier this month. Maybe vibecoding driver updates and then vibecoding fixes for their inevitable bugs isn't the best way of doing things.

He's written for Rock Paper Shotgun, The Substantial Issue, GamesRadar, Zam, Glixel, Five Out of Ten Magazine, and Playboy.com, whose cheques with the bunny logo made for fun conversations at the bank. Jody's first article for PC Gamer was about the audio of Alien Isolation, published in 2015. Jody edited PC Gamer Indie from 2017 to 2018, and he eventually lived up to his promise to play every Warhammer videogame.

  • It has been revealed that however, despite a successful October, Modern Warfare 4 hasn't managed to land in Circana's top ten list of year-to-date biggest sellers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Despite its somewhat muted critical reception, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has predictably topped the US video game charts in October. The Infinity Ward-developed shooter was October's best-selling game in the US across digital and retail, beating the month's other massive-hitters, including Gears of War: E-Day and Star Wars: Galactic Racer.

That's according to market analysis firm Circana's latest US market report, which revealed Modern Warfare 4 was October's leader in dollar sales. This marks the 19th-year running that a Call of Duty game topped the charts in its release month, a streak that began with November 2008's COD: World at War.

It has been revealed that however, despite a successful October, Modern Warfare 4 hasn't managed to land in Circana's top ten list of year-to-date biggest sellers. In fact, the only COD title on the list is the Black Ops 2 port released this summer. NBA 2K27 continues to lead Circana's ranking, having overtaken Resident Evil: Requiem last month to secure the top spot. It's a reverse of Circana's September report, when NBA 2K27 failed to lead its own debut month but claimed the top spot in the year-to-date list. Here's the list of the top 10 year-to-date:.

Away from Modern Warfare 4, October saw the release of several other well-performing and critically acclaimed games, and six of the top ten were upcoming releases. That hasn't stopped Circana from posting 14 percent lower spending on games compared to October last year. Analyst Mat Piscatella noted much of that dip can be attributed to a major slump in mobile spending, and also because October 2025 was particularly strong, with both Battlefield 6 and Pokémon Legends: Z-A releasing. Here's October's top 10:.

In Eurogamer's Modern Warfare 4 review, Dom Peppiatt awarded it four stars, writing: "Modern Warfare 4 represents the highest tide for Call of Duty in seven years. Infinity Ward needed to pull off a balancing act I don't envy; injecting just enough nostalgia into a series propped up with so many conventions and expectations there's barely room for anything new, alongside enough innovation and intrigue to keep people interested.".

Sharna Burgess isn't holding back on how she feels about Harry Shum Jr.'s shock elimination and the discourse around this season of Dancing With The Stars. As conversations continue about whether the show should allow contestants with professional dancing experience, she wants changes to the voting.

Ahead of the finale on the 2026 TV schedule, Burgess was responding to questions from fans on her Instagram Stories. When asked if she was surprised by Shum Jr. being sent packing, this is what she had to say (via Us Magazine):.

Sadly no, I felt it was going to be another shock elimination. Not because they deserved it but simply because the online discourse is so wild that [it] was pretty clear who fans were ‘voting off’ and how they have felt about dance experience contestants.

In a recent development, the online fandom was going on in recent weeks about how unfair it was for Dancing With The Stars to have both Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Dewan in this season. That, paired with Tatyana Ali's continued improvement over the episodes, created a major discussion over whether it was better to watch dancers develop or ones who were already great.

The only way Ali was going to make the finals was for one fan-favorite to be sent home, and as improbable as it was, Harry Shum Jr. left over the remaining competitors. Sharna Burgess isn't the only DWTS cast member upset about the elimination, but she is one of the only ones calling for serious reform to the voting system:.

Recent findings suggest that [It’s] so disappointing to see our voting system is now being used by viewers to vote people off instead of voting for your favorite. I say we got [sic] back to yall only have 10 votes total and you have to figure out how to dish them out. This voting ppl off thing is so insanely negative and not what we are built on and it’s seemingly given fans the chance to manipulate the show. JMO.

It has been revealed that sharna Burgess wants Dancing With The Stars to start limiting the voting and only giving fans ten votes, period, rather than ten per couple. Under this thinking, I'm assuming the idea is that viewers couldn't vote for everyone but the person they want eliminated. Would that be enough to turn things around?

Personally, I have doubts. To start, there's always the possibility that the voting can be tampered. For example, there was a big rumor that Maura Higgins had to go to the hospital ahead of the semifinals, which might've impacted her votes from those who feared she'd be eliminated.

Plus, the obvious flaw in this plan is that the viewers could still influence the vote and just encourage everyone else to vote for anyone but Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson. As I'd written previously, I think the solution is for DWTS to work toward equality between contestants as far as skill level.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Industry observers note that I'll be interested to see how the conversation continues after the finale, and how whoever is crowned the winner may shape it. There are already big pushes online for Connor Wood to take home the big prize, and others hoping for Tatyana. All this before a single performance on the dance floor, which is another conversation entirely. Will there be changes to voting, or will this all blow over by the time next season rolls around?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that I like to think I'm difficult to hypnotise, but I confess, I'm a sucker for those Youtube adverts for the mobile vertical shooters.
  • It has been revealed that show me one of those ads, and I'll always watch to the end in the hope that this time, the protagonist will Study The Blade, conquer their harmatia, and slay the damn ogre.
  • According to recent reports, per the Steam page, it claims to have turned the above advert format into a whole upcoming "deeply strategic genre", the "gates shooter", by stirring in "elements of roguelikes and bullet heavens".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that I like to think I'm difficult to hypnotise, but I confess, I'm a sucker for those Youtube adverts for the mobile vertical shooters. You know the ones: boglins pour towards an auto-firing player, who must dodge about to grab upgrades while whittling down the horde. The player in the advert always does pretty well for 20 seconds, but ahhhh, then they get just a tiny bit overconfident, mistime how long it'll take them to erode the health of an ogre midboss, and: bam!

It has been revealed that show me one of those ads, and I'll always watch to the end in the hope that this time, the protagonist will Study The Blade, conquer their harmatia, and slay the damn ogre. I've never actually played any of the mobile shooters in question, mind you. I'm far too cultured for that, you dope! Except that I've just been playing the demo for Korridor, which is supposedly "based off" of the ads, but might as well be one of the games they're promoting, for all I know.

According to recent reports, per the Steam page, it claims to have turned the above advert format into a whole upcoming "deeply strategic genre", the "gates shooter", by stirring in "elements of roguelikes and bullet heavens". I need somebody to authenticate whether this is a truthful statement, or developer TinyToad pulling a fast one. In the meantime, I'll say that 1) I have now managed to kill several ogres, 2) I like Korridor's electro-metal soundtrack.

Recent findings suggest that in Korridor, you're a bald medieval monk garbed in Poundshop Adeptus Astartes platemail. You've woken up in a dungeon of mysterious provenance, and must walk very slowly down its corridors korridors while shooting and punching goblins, wraiths and demons hurrying the other way. Each enemy has a numerical health indicator, and the basic challenge is working out whether you can empty it before they walk into you – which costs you a proportionate amount of health, mitigated by armour. As you go, you'll walk through a choice of gates that grant buffs such as faster health regen, bullet penetration, or nippier horizontal motion.

The fact that you don't control how fast the monk trudges vertically allows the game to synch the onslaught pretty tightly to the thudding, growling score. It reminds me a little of Thumper, though it isn't nearly so invigoratingly malevolent. So far. At intervals, the beat thickens and all the enemies burst into a sprint, throwing their arms up and conveying the strong impression that they are more running away from something than running at you. There's clearly a dreadful entity at the far end of the dungeon. Perhaps it is another overdressed monk with an even bigger gun.

Industry observers note that is this how those mobile games actually work? If it is, then alas and alack, all is lost. I've finally succumbed to those adverts, and all it took was some disingenuous Steam copy promising to place them at a critical remove. Curse you, TinyToad. Curse you and your gates. If you were actually a toad, I'd step on you. Still, now that we've broken the ice, can you please make another game in which I get to play one of those gloating giantesses in Hero Wars? Because I know some people who dig that kind of thing.

  • If you're a raider, then you were likely one of many Warriors of Light awaiting the data center party finder merges.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On the way to the newly introduced expansion Evercold, ever-beloved Square Enix MMO Final Fantasy 14 has seen a couple of long-awaited server matching changes roll out across Europe, Japan, and North America – and it seems they're not quite over yet.

If you're a raider, then you were likely one of many Warriors of Light awaiting the data center party finder merges. As a Chaos player myself, I know I certainly was, and I'm thrilled to see Savage and Ultimate listings by the dozen now – but I never expected to get to play alongside folks from the US. It seems I (and every other Europe-based player) will indeed get to next month, though, as Square Enix outlines in a latest announcement online. And we have Evercold to thank. "To help alleviate server congestion following the release of Patch 8.0, we will be enabling cross-region Data Center Travel between the North American and European data centers during scheduled maintenance on Tuesday, December 1, 2026," as the studio reveals. It's no secret that "login queues tend to become extremely long during peak times following an expansion release," after all. "As peak play times differ between North America and Europe, another physical data center may be less crowded and serve as a viable option when login queues on your usual data center are long." If you're worried about latency (high ping, my not-so-beloved), that's valid – but Square Enix urges you to give it a "try" before Evercold. This isn't a permanent server crossover, so to speak, however… at least, not yet.

To help alleviate server congestion following the release of Patch 8.0, we will be enabling cross-region Data Center Travel between the North American and European data centers during scheduled maintenance on Tuesday, December 1, 2026. Details 🌍↔️🌎️ https://t.co/DmKrmJ9Fw9 https://t.co/6Y89rP9eNWNovember 24, 2026.

In a recent development, square Enix only "decided to temporarily open travel between these two data centers as part of our efforts to mitigate congestion" – but "will continue to take community feedback into account as we carefully evaluate the possibility of permanently enabling travel between the North American and European data centers, as well as opening travel between other physical data centers." That's pretty dang massive. What effect could this have on those of us interested in harder content, though? Comments on X show understandable concerns regarding party finder population. As one reads, "This completely decimates EU PF btw, you'll do to EU what you did to Chaos." It's a real worry, honestly, when I remember how dead Chaos was after Light took off – but the reality is that high ping doesn't make for easy raiding, so there's hope yet.

Recent findings suggest that this does sort of leave players in Oceania out, too, which they point out on Reddit. As a fan notes, "I'm happy for everyone, however as an OCE player, when things are quiet, it would be nice for me to travel! I feel like this'll make OCE worse." It's difficult to tell what'll actually happen to any region in question until the server changes roll out in a few days, I suppose, but there's an undeniable bright side here.

Industry observers note that those of us in Europe will finally get to make our way over to Balmung and see if it lives up to its… interesting… reputation. That's enough to leave me looking forward to December, if I'm honest – cursed Limsa Lominsa roleplay and all.

Final Fantasy 14 fans celebrate newly introduced "mass-production Limsa e-girl outfit" as Square Enix finally turns a datamine into an $18 reality.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that closing statements in Rockstar and IWGB's employment tribunal case - revolving around the GTA 6 developer's alleged 'union busting' and the firing of 34 employees - have now been read, bringing the hearing to an end. There's currently no timeline for a verdict, however, with one commentator suggesting a judgement could take weeks or months to arrive.

In a recent development, the case, which began in September and has included evidence from 23 claimants in the months since, must now be considered by the judge, who will determine if Rockstar unfairly dismissed employees in breach of their employment rights. Rockstar has been accused of unlawfully firing workers for being part of a union, but the GTA developer insists employees were dismissed for breaching confidentiality agreements.

According to recent reports, people Makes Games' Chris Bratt has been following the case closely and reporting on proceedings as they've unfolded. With closing statements now complete, Bratt quoted Judge Lucy Wiseman as saying, "I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case. What I will say is that I will use my best endeavors to get that judgement out as quickly as I possibly can.".

Recent findings suggest that however, Bratt suggests it could be ""anywhere from a few weeks up to a few months before we actually hear the judgement", noting "The firings themselves, let's not forget, happened over a year ago now. This has been a slog.".

Industry observers note that one fired Rockstar worker involved in the case spoke with Bratt after the closing statements to share their thoughts. "Honestly it's just sort of blended together," they said. "It’s been so long, that after the first six months or so it became the new depressing reality. I'm hoping the judgement will release us from it.".

Last month, the conclusion of the tribunal hearing was delayed after cross examination of witnesses ran long.

Yesterday's closing statements come at a time when all eyes are on GTA 6 as it finally releases this week, concluding years of development for both current and former employees. Many of those workers involved in the case urged players to support the game despite the legal dispute.

It has been revealed that additionally, Rockstar employees are currently voting on whether they want recognised union representation at the studio. If the vote passes, it would be the largest recognised union across the entirety of the UK video game industry. The deadline for union votes is 26th November.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Update [Tue 24th Nov 2026, 2:27pm]: Our sister site Push Square has also now published a guide for this Easter Egg:.

Original Story: One of the coolest things about GTA 6 since release has been watching players discover all kinds of Easter Eggs, such as the Mario-inspired hats that were shared by our sister site Nintendo Life yesterday.

We reckon this is the best one so far though - a secret portal that takes you into a nightclub from the original 2002 version of Vice City for the PS2 (which technically means it takes you back to its 1986-inspired setting).

It has been revealed that the process of getting here is long-winded, and detailed in full in the video from Dan Allen Gaming up above. In a nutshell, you have to go to the Badger R&D Radio Tower in Key Lento and use the power switch and press a button to make the Malibu logo appear on the TV. From there, visit 12 LPL substations around the map without fast-travelling, and press the correct buttons in the specific order (from the video) when you reach them. You'll then get a text, at which point you head to Reactor 2 at the LPL Turtle Head Power Station between 7pm and 6am to find the portal.

It seems someone called Memelo was the first to discover this trick:.

Industry observers note that another really cool part of this Easter Egg is that when you combine all the substations together, the wording on the outside of them adds up to "Life is Passing Me By", which references a classic cheat code from the original Vice City. You actually have to use the buttons to enter this cheat code and make the portal appear.

As mentioned, you get two free items for your trouble as well, which are Tommy Vercetti's classic shirt and bike from the 2002 game. These appear as soon as you're thrown out of the portal and back into the so-called real world!

Finally, we'll also highlight that although pretty much all the footage we've seen of this Easter Egg has been exclusive to the Jason character, it does appear to work with Lucia as well. That noted, we've also come across many players who claim the portal isn't showing up for them, so we're not sure what's causing it to fail in those situations.

Anyway, crazy stuff right?! Who knows what other insane Easter Eggs might be discovered over the coming days and weeks - some people have mentioned they're seeing a "flashback" pop-up after completing the Vice City one, with a suggestion there may be another four flashback sequences yet to be found. Let's hope so!

Have you tried this? Did you get Tommy Vercetti's items? Let us know down in the comments sectiobn below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As GTA 6 finally arrives, increasingly outspoken games industry legend Warren Spector - known for seminal immersive sims including Deus Ex - has offered both praise for the game's achievements and lambasted its "billion dollar" development model, writing, "I just hope GTA 6 is the last of its kind even if it’s the best we have to offer".

Recent findings suggest that spector declared his retirement from games development in August following struggles at his OtherSide Entertainment studio, and has been vocal about the state of the games industry in the months since, notably saying anyone at EA responsible for the "travesty" of BioWare's closure should be "ashamed". And now Spector has taken on GTA 6.

According to recent reports, "First, congratulations to everyone who worked on GTA 6. It looks like it will be a high point of sorts for our medium and our business," he wrote in a post on LinkedIn. "However… its billion dollar development cost and an undoubtedly crazy marketing budget don't represent a business model anyone else can or probably should emulate.

In a recent development, "That's especially true," Spector continued, "when thousands of developers are out of work. A billion dollars pays for a lot of games and a lot of salaries. Personally I'd rather have hundreds of games and full employment than one game no matter how amazing it is.".

The "sure success" of GTA 6 proves a point he's made "for years", he noted: "That no game that matters ships on time and/or on budget". Highlighting GTA 6's year-long delay and reported billion dollar budget, Spector suggested, "Give a game the time and money to prove its potential (key word, potential) and you have a chance of making something great. Underfund a game or force it out the door before it's ready [is] guaranteed failure no matter how much potential it has.

"So, again, congratulations," Spector concluded. "Ambition and innovation are necessary for the medium to reach its potential. I just hope GTA 6 is the last of its kind even if it's the best we have to offer.".

Sources indicate that despite Spector's concerns, GTA 6's arrival is, as expected, already causing shockwaves across the industry. It has broken pre-order records for Xbox and PlayStation stores, smashed the all-time livestream viewer record, and apparently briefly broke Reddit too. And is its success deserved? Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell thinks so, saying it "pushes back the horizon of video games once again" in his five star GTA 6 review.
