Industry observers note that "I made a game for the Epic's 'vibe-coding gamejam' megajam without using any AI in four days," they expanded on not Bluesky. "Sorta ran out of time so gameplay didn't turn out how I wanted, but hey it's still pretty aura.".

Other submissions the megajam included a game called THIS GAME IS AI SLOP and one dubbed Goon Patrol - Director's Cut. If you're wondering how a game without genAI use could be allowed to stand among the slop masterpieces, it's because Epic ended up having to make clearer not long after the jam was unveiled that submissions didn't have to make use of genAI as a hard rule, leaving it up to the developer how much or little was worked in.

Still, I imagine noted genAI advocate Tim Sweeney's not best pleased that a game deliberately swimming against the slop tide indicates up at the top if you hit up the Popular filter. Then again, he's been very busy posting key things about the situation with Jensen Huang and Nvidia lately, so maybe he hasn't noticed.

Forgotten car combat game Destruction AllStars has been in some stage of extinction for years now, but if you do have the PS5 game in your library, then today truly is the last day you can play it in any meaningful manner.

From tomorrow, 25th November 2026, the last of its game services will be taken offline.

The multiplayer servers were already permanently pulled in May 2026, and within the next 24 hours, "all remaining game services will be taken offline", per communication from Sony.

Single player modes had still been available to play, but those will be removed too when their servers are taken offline.

It has been revealed that quite literally the only content left in Destruction AllStars after tomorrow is an arcade mode and challenges. Even then, though, Sony warns the "functionality and player experience" tied to that content could be impacted.

Basically, if you want to experience even a sliver of the Destruction AllStars experience, you've only got today left to do it. It's already been delisted from the PS Store, so if you don't have a copy now, you're completely out of luck.

It's not like you'd be missing out on much, to be fair.

Destruction AllStars never made a splash in terms of quality or popularity. While it did have a small playerbase during its days with active servers, the game swiftly died out after a February 2021 release.

Sources indicate that will you be playing Destruction AllStars one last time today? Let us know in the comments below.

With two incidents and Disney’s desire to cut back on live entertainment, I’m really starting to worry about the future of the show.

The fire reportedly broke out during Fantasmic’s second performance of the night shortly before the show’s finale. While the Mark Twain finale was able to go on, flames can be seen behind the boat on the small stage set up on Tom Saywer Island. Thankfully, the fire was small compared to the 2023 incident that turned the Maleficent dragon animatronic into a giant fireball and forever changed the show. There’s been no word on the extent of the damage this time around, but considering the show was back Sunday night it safe to assume that nothing was affected and no cast members were harmed, thankfully.

Sources indicate that two fiery incidents are definitely a cause for concern, and with Disneyland executives’ history of scaling back entertainment to cut costs, I can’t help but worry about the show’s fate. After all, Fantasmic boasts a large cast of incredible performers and several floating units. Plus water screens, projectors, and fireworks. I’m no expert, but I’m willing to bet it’s one of the most costly attractions at Disneyland. Not to mention, the show is still feeling the loss of the Maleficent Dragon, which makes the battle between Mickey and Maleficent lackluster.

While I don’t think Disneyland would end the show without also announcing a replacement, I do think Disney fans should prepare themselves. After all, Disney fans aren’t known for taking latest changes well. Just look at the uproar that happened when it was announced Dinosaur would close to make room for a new Indiana Jones attraction at Disney World.

It has been revealed that disneyland has been having a rough go at things this month. On the first day of the holiday season, the Anaheim theme park’s iconic fake snow was accidentally turned on during a rainstorm, creating a mess. Back in October, Frontierland experienced widespread flooding. With park tickets being so expensive, it’s unfortunate to see cracks in Disneyland’s magic, but not even the mouse can control the weather or unexpected fires.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 has only been out for a matter of hours, and players have already tracked down a UFO in the woods and a Bigfoot in the swamps.

Sources indicate that the UFO encounter is a random night-time event in Kelly County, on a dirt road near the Starlet Motel safehouse east of Port Gellhorn. You'll need to have finished the game's first chapter, and it's most reliable after 2am in-game.

In a recent development, as word spread late yesterday (18th November), it seems the event will kick off if you find a car at the side of the road with its headlights flickering, its trunk open, and clothes strewn around it. Follow the trail into the trees towards a blue glow, and you'll catch a UFO beaming down on a woman before it drops her and flies off. Head back to her car, as she requests, and the UFO returns for you. You apparently black out and come round three days later, and a bronze trophy called The Truth Is Out There should unlock.

You can seemingly trigger the event as either Jason or Lucia, and it isn't needed for 100 percent completion.

And that's not the only close encounter you can expect, either. YouTuber Lazarbeam bumped into Bigfoot on the afternoon of 18th November, hours before the game introduced in the UK, while one Reddit user reported that they weren't quite sure what they'd stumbled on, titling their post "I think I found Bigfoot".

Leonida's version of Bigfoot is actually the Skunk Ape, Florida's own swamp cryptid, and it can be found in the swamplands near Cottonmouth Lake in Mariana County as soon as free roam opens up. Listen out for a loud roar, then use Jason's tracking ability to follow it through the swamp. You may find it feeding on a deer carcass, while a second sighting has been reported south of Watson Bay.

Industry observers note that either way, the trail seemingly ends at a strange, human-like tree. Investigate it, and Jason blacks out, triggering a short cutscene in which the creature creeps up on him, as shown in this video. He later wakes near his vehicle, drenched in sweat. Save your ammo, though, as shooting at it won't do you any good.

Cryptids and aliens are, of course, something of a Rockstar tradition by this point. GTA 5's Mount Chiliad mystery kept players hunting for years, and Output Lag has already spotted two NPCs in a GTA 6 bar talking about goings-on there. Nobody has cracked a full Chiliad-style puzzle in the new game yet, but I'm sure that's just a matter of when, not if.

GTA 6 debuted today on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, although some have been getting in on the action earlier as a whopping 2m Xbox players in the UK and US took advantage of the trick of changing their console's country. Even Newly introduced Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty. "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

Industry observers note that eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, ubisoft have laid off 166 developers, with this latest round of cuts at the Assassin's Creed and Far Cry publishers taking place at two of their studios in Eastern Canada.
  • Both IGN and GamesIndustry.biz report that the cuts, which amount to just under 4% studios' total combined headcount, affected staff working on recently cancelled or significantly changed projects.
  • According to recent reports, "Ubisoft is reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations," Ubisoft said in a statement handed to both sites.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, ubisoft have laid off 166 developers, with this latest round of cuts at the Assassin's Creed and Far Cry publishers taking place at two of their studios in Eastern Canada. Both studios affected, Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec, had a hand in last year's Assassin's Creed Shadows, with Montreal especially being a major and long-tenured development hub for the company.

Both IGN and GamesIndustry.biz report that the cuts, which amount to just under 4% studios' total combined headcount, affected staff working on recently cancelled or significantly changed projects.

According to recent reports, "Ubisoft is reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations," Ubisoft said in a statement handed to both sites. "As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.

"We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues. We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources.".

It has been revealed that ubisoft Montreal are currently working on Assassin’s Creed Hexe, reportedly a witchy tale set during the time of the Holy Roman Empire, which switched creative directors earlier this ear and is one of the games Ubi are keen to get out of the door. What Quebec have been up to since Shadows shipped is less clear. They're a much smaller than Montreal and were founded in 2005.

According to recent reports, ubisoft have been carrying out mass cuts across their studios worldwide all the way through this year. Ubisoft Singapore and Trials developers Redlynx. Ubisoft Winnipeg, Belgrade, and Barcelona. Long-time Tom Clancy studio Red Storm. Ubisoft's Paris HQ. Three German studios including Anno devs Ubisoft Mainz. All have been subjected to some form of cuts or closure.

Meanwhile. changes to remote working policies have also contributed to strikes at Ubisoft studios in France and Italy.

Solidarity to all of the Ubisoft workers who've been affected by these layoffs in Montreal and Quebec.

Sources indicate that for six seasons now, Abbott Elementary fans have faithfully watched the relationship between Janine Teagues (Quinta Brunson) and Gregory Eddie (Tyler James Williams) progress. The pair have gone from good friends to committed lovers over the past several years and, now, it seems we’re on the cusp of a proposal. Many viewers are hoping an engagement will come during the Disneyland-set 100th episode that’ll air amid the 2026 TV schedule. I’d love that as well, but I also have a question about two other characters.

Industry observers note that gregory and Janine are, of course, the core couple on Abbott, but plenty of other romantic relationships amongst characters have been highlighted as well. As we anticipate what lies ahead for Janine and Gregory, I can’t help but wonder what the future holds for Ava Coleman and O’Shon, who’ve been dating since Season 4. I’ve enjoyed seeing their relationship develop as well as the funny moments that have resulted from that. With that, it’s hard not to wonder what the long-term plan for them might look like.

Sources indicate that it’s clear that the affable O’Shon (Matthew Law) and Abbott’s diva of a principal Ava (Critics Choice winner Janelle James) are on steady footing after some initial growing pains. At this point, the pair have not only vacationed together, but they’ve also reached the point where they can throw a party as a couple. (That Halloween shindig they held this season was fantastic). Some may think it’s a bit early to consider a proposal for these two, but I don’t think it’s wild to think it could happen by the end of Season 6.

Gregory first expressed interest in proposing to Janine at the end of Season 5, which was about two years after the two finally got together. Ava and O’Shon will be reaching that mark later in the sixth season and, while great TV couples have different timelines, I could see O’Shon popping the question soon. Plus, given how encouraging O’Shon has been amid Gregory’s attempts to propose, who’s to say the former doesn’t want that for himself sometime in the near future?

Industry observers note that of course, I’m not saying anyone needs to be jumping the broom by the end of this season. I just wouldn’t mind seeing one or two engagements by the time Abbott’s finale rolls around next spring. That may seem like a long shot for Ava and O’Shon right now, but I’m feeling very good about Janine and Gregory’s chances of hitting that milestone.

The True Story That Inspired Abbott Elementary’s Choice To Move The School Into A Mall.

Gregory has been trying to orchestrate the right moment to present Janine with a ring. During the show’s latest episode, “Competition,” he attempted to land a reservation at a popular Italian restaurant, where he could propose. Ironically, that plan became moot once Abbott’s Step Team punched their ticket to Disneyland, and Janine informed her man that they’d serve as chaperones on the trip. So it now seems like a given that Gregory will attempt to propose while he and his lady are in “The Happiest Place On Earth.”.

Industry observers note that what’s more is that the pressure is going to be on, as Janine is aware of her beau’s intention to pop the question (thanks to a major slip-up on Ava’s part). So the pressure is really on for Eddie to craft the perfect proposal. The Disneyland episode could indeed present him the right situation to do just that and, if Gregory does pull it off in great fashion, it might set a bit of a bar for O’Shon to clear if he eventually takes that step.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Warning: There is discussion of suicide in this story.
  • In a recent development, it’s been seven months since Storage Wars star Darrell Sheets died by suicide in his home in Arizona, and it sounds like the other stars of the show, like Brandi Passante, are still, understandably, processing his death.
  • Sources indicate that sheets left the show as a full-time cast member in 2019 after suffering a heart attack.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Warning: There is discussion of suicide in this story.

In a recent development, it’s been seven months since Storage Wars star Darrell Sheets died by suicide in his home in Arizona, and it sounds like the other stars of the show, like Brandi Passante, are still, understandably, processing his death. Season 19 of the reality show kicks off on the 2026 television schedule on November 28th, and ahead of its premiere, Passante talked about Sheets’ passing and how it has affected both her personally and the production of the show.

Sources indicate that sheets left the show as a full-time cast member in 2019 after suffering a heart attack. He remained in contact with the rest of the cast, including Passante, and he made occasional guest appearances after retiring. In a discussion with TV Insider, Passante talked about how his death has affected the show, including how the rest of the cast work with each other:.

It definitely changed the dynamic with everybody. We’re all a little softer and kinder to each other since that happened. There was a lot of beef and animosity before between most of us. Some things are not worth fighting.

Sheets’ death, like so many do, really seems to have put things in perspective for the rest of the cast. Their rivalries are what make the show so endlessly watchable, but in the end, they have known each other for almost two decades now, so something like this is bound to change things. Sheets’ manner of death is also a particularly difficult thing to endure, according to Passante:.

I’ve endured a lot of deaths in that same manner over the years, and that is just a grief that, you know, kind of sticks with you. It’s not like losing somebody to cancer or a heart attack. It’s something that you think maybe you could have helped prevent. It’s one of those difficult deaths that you never can really wrap your head around.

In a recent development, anyone who has lost a loved one to suicide knows how Passante feels. It can feel completely helpless. For her part, Passante is doing what she can, including checking in on Sheets’ son, Brandon, who was by his father’s side at all the auctions until Darrell left the show. Passante noted:.

I talk to [his son] Brandon a lot now. We didn’t really chat much over the years when they left. We would talk every once in a while during holidays or something, but now I just try to keep tabs. He sends me little messages maybe once a week. I just like to check in on him because it’s a hard thing to swallow. I’m sure that he’s missing his dad.

Ultimately, Passante summed it up quite succinctly by saying simply, “It sucks.”.

There has been a lot of drama on Storage Wars over the years, and while much of it is contrived for the show, behind-the-scenes has been filled with drama, too. Passante has been in the middle of some of it when she divorced her long-time partner in life and in business, Jarrod Schulz, after Season 13 of the show. There has been nothing like the tragedy that befell Sheets, though, and keeping everything in perspective is important.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever now has more people playing each week than World of Warcraft has seen in 15 years, according to Blizzard.

Recent findings suggest that "Another fun statistic for you! #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years!" executive producer and World of Warcraft vice president Holly Longdale posted. "Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth. We're doing this together, for Forever!".

Longdale was quoting a post from the official World of Warcraft account, which shared a batch of "By the Numbers" stats for the latest edition.

Since it released on 4th November, players have created 15,160,147 characters and 140,764 guilds, completed 1,480,343,357 quests, and defeated 9,786,925,806 enemies.

Recent findings suggest that another fun statistic for you! #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years! Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth. We're doing this together, for Forever! 💙♾️ https://t.co/bMLQduLri2.

They've also formed 71,309,889 parties, used 28,696,386 camping items, and there have been 28,938,569 PvP kills.

Collectively, we've died a lot, too - 196,851,761 times in total, with Archmage Arugal, the final boss of Shadowfang Keep, seemingly the deadliest boss.

"You're breaking records by the day!" the post read.

Earlier this month, Blizzard said WoW: Forever was the biggest launch in World of Warcraft history by peak concurrent players, and that it had brought in the highest number of returning players the game has ever seen.

Longdale added at the time that it had pulled in the most upcoming players for a WoW launch in 15 years. It has since suffered its first controversy, though, with a now-fixed gold exploit.

Industry observers note that last week, players pieced together a hidden quest chain that leads to two special swords. At the time of writing, only one has been found, though progress continues in pursuit of the second.

The game has been out for just over two weeks now, and continues to prove popular among newly introduced and returning players.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Is there something going on today? A lot of talk about committing crimes and the like, I just can't quite put my finger on why… Ah well, couldn't be vital or interesting. What is interesting, however, is Keepsake County, a "midwestern stealth game" that has introduced on this inauspicious day about stealing stuff from "hideous farmhouses in the middle of nowhere.".

With the sarcastic intro out the way, I will address the elephant in the room: Vovly's Adventure: Reslimed is out today too. Fine, fine, yes I know GTA 6 is the game everyone's talking about, but Forward Instinct, the devs behind Keepsake County, seem well aware of that in their launch day post for the game: "Folks, thanks for your incredible patience. Keepsake County is finally OUT! And yes, it is deeply ironic that it wound up being today, of all days, that we got the green light to finally release, but here we are.".

Keepsake Country was supposed to release earlier this month, but seemingly got caught up in the backlog Valve are faced with that's undoubtedly been caused by genAI games. In any case, the burgle-em-up does look quite delightful. I'm not sure if I can quite put my finger on exactly why I get this feeling, but it calls to mind a more complex version of the kind of game you'd find on Cartoon Network's website back in the day (which is a high point of praise, I'd like to be clear).

According to recent reports, each house in Keepsake Country is procedurally generated, meaning you never quite know what to expect when you enter. There's lockpicking, resident tie upping, and of course stealing to be done, but it doesn't just stop at the house. Parking your car, for instance, is an crucial thing to consider; do you want it hidden so you're less likely to be discovered, or right at the front door so you can make a speedy escape? Not to mention you have to deal with the fuzz showing up at some point if you aren't quick enough!

Gear and the like can be improved between runs, meaning you can lockpick faster or delay the cops, it all seems quite systemically thoughtful. Very much some immersive sim vibes from this one, just on a much smaller scale. And most certainly worth considering picking up on a release day like today! If you're interested in doing so, you can pick it up on Steam right here.

GTA 6 is hiding an extremely cool Easter egg related to 2002's GTA: Vice City. While it's a really fun reward and absolutely worth looking for, it involves quite a complex set of steps to make it happen. In this GTA 6 guide, we're going to explain how to find the Vice City Easter egg.

Full credit to Memeio for discovering this secret!

Sources indicate that below is a full walkthrough of how to do the Vice City Easter egg in GTA 6 and get the Tommy Vercetti rewards. Follow these steps and you can find the Vice City Easter egg for yourself.

Note: Because this is a walkthrough of the whole process, you may find spoilers below.

Your first stop is the Badger R&D radio tower in Key Lento, not far from Jason's home. Here it is on the map for reference:.

Go to the tower and climb it, walking up the internal stairs and then climbing the ladders to reach the top:.

In this room, there's an electrical box on the wall with a lever you can pull; set the lever to the upper 'ON' position:.

On the opposite side of the room, push the button on the equipment:.

You should hear a sound effect play (taken directly from GTA: Vice City).

Sources indicate that on the back wall are a couple of posters that provide some clues as to what you need to do. First is a poster for LPL, the power company in GTA 6. The second advertises the JoySystem bearing the phrase, "Lose Track of Time":.

"Lose Track of Time" is a reference to "Life Is Passing Me By", which is a well-known cheat code in GTA: Vice City that speeds up the in-game clock.

Recent findings suggest that your goal now is to visit 12 substations all across Leonida in a particular order. When you reach each one, you will need to press certain buttons, slowly entering the old school cheat code.

Note: You cannot fast travel to these locations, you must reach them all manually. Also, some of these substations are staffed and you will be trespassing while you're on the premises, so be careful.

Let's go through each stop on your substation tour:.

Industry observers note that the first substation is in Vice City's Downtown district. Here's its location on the map:.

Look left to see a building with an 'L' by the door:.

Go inside and find the machine with a label on it that reads "Press D" — push that button:.

Recent findings suggest that substation #2 is located in the Balsero district. Here it is on the map:.

And again, a bit more zoomed out:.

Hop the fence and go inside the door next to the letters 'iF':.

In the room inside, turn left and approach the machine with the label 'Press D' and push the button:.

Substation #3 is back in Key Lento. Here it is on the map:.

Sources indicate that hop the fence and make your way to the main building. You're looking for a door next to the letters 'Ei' on the wall:.

Go inside; just to the right is a machine with the label 'Press •'. Push the button:.

Substation #4 is located on Penmarch Isle in the Washington Beach region. Here's where you'll find it:.

And here's a slightly more zoomed out view:.

If you’re curious, all the clues can be found in the apartment, and you’ll get a pretty nice ride out of it, too – at least once you find the location it hints towards.

It has been revealed that the GTA 6 laptop pass word is Muffins Queen 15, found from various clues around the house. Below I'll run through all the info you need to find what you want.

In a recent development, when you first find the laptop you’ll be able to put in a few guesses, but none of them will be right. Instead, you’ll need to unlock the correct prompts by searching around your safehouse. First, head to the entrance hallway to find the shrine to Boogie’s dog (above).

  • Industry observers note that baglow, credited as a writer on the original GTA and who served as "head of propaganda and indoctrination" at DMA Design (the studio that would become Rockstar North) in the '90s, said that back in the day of GTA 1, the devs didn't even have a script.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, lots of people will tell you that Grand Theft Auto 6's Lucia Caminos marks the series' first female protagonist. Lots of people are, of course, wrong. GTA 1 had eight selectable protagonists, four of whom were women, while GTA 2 for the Game Boy Color let you play protags Candy or Gretchen (along with a bunch of other men) in addition to the PlayStation game's default Claude Speed.

That vital pedantry out of the way, it's undeniable that Lucia is GTA's first female protagonist since the series became the culture-swallowing goliath it is today. In a chat with CBC's As It Happens, GTA OG Brian Baglow stated he reckons it's "long, long overdue".

Industry observers note that baglow, credited as a writer on the original GTA and who served as "head of propaganda and indoctrination" at DMA Design (the studio that would become Rockstar North) in the '90s, said that back in the day of GTA 1, the devs didn't even have a script. "We started with a tech demo, a way of moving around a city… I came in to actually add the story, add the script, after the levels had been built".

That was mostly a process of, shall we say, finding inspiration: "we were making it up as we went along… it was a case of going into every crime movie, every heist, every caper, every TV show, cop show, crime drama, and lifting elements that I hoped would resonate with people".

Recent findings suggest that baglow sounds, rightfully, rather proud of his time spent working on such an notable series, but he has his qualms as he casts his eye back over it. "The representation of women, it has not been good, and that's putting it very mildly", he says, "so I'm delighted that we now have not only a female protagonist, but a Hispanic female protagonist. I think it's been long, long overdue, and I can't wait to get to grips with the game and see how in-depth it goes.

"I think it's showing a level of maturation because from the very earliest days it was a very young group of almost entirely male developers in Scotland".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Phil Spencer is a legend of the Xbox division, having helped redefine the brand after a disastarous Xbox One launch in 2013, and spearheading such initiatives as Xbox Game Pass, Xbox backwards compatibility, crossplay, and a renewed focus on gaming rather than continuing the push towards "TV, TV, TV" that had proven so controversial.

It's very possible that without his influence, Xbox would have shut its doors over a decade ago.

We haven't heard anything from Spencer since he declared his retirement earlier in 2026, but he's still very actively playing games on his Xbox consoles, including some of this year's new releases.

For example, he's racked up 940/1000 gamerscore in Echo Generation 2, 650/1000 in Forza Horizon 6, 585/1000 in Replaced, and he's also been playing the likes of Halo: Campaign Evolved, Gears of War: E-Day, Sopa - Tale of the Stolen Potato, Baldur's Gate 3, Vampire Crawlers and even Sunset Overdrive in recent months.

One of Phil's most beloved qualities as Xbox boss was that he proved himself to be a hardcore gamer, being someone who actively seeks to play games in his spare time. New Xbox CEO Asha Sharma is somewhat the opposite, admitting back in February that she doesn't "pretend to be the best gamer" and that it's ultimately not her goal to be.

Anyway, Phil is busy enjoying his retirement right now, and we wish him all the best from everyone here at Pure Xbox. We unfortunately never got a chance to meet the man ourselves, but always admired his leadership from afar.

Here's hoping he might start hitting the interview circuit and doing what the likes of Peter Moore and Nintendo's Reggie Fils-Aimé have done in the past, as we'd love to see him sticking around the industry in some capacity going forward.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, rupert Grint is the latest cast member from the Harry Potter films to join the Broadway run of Harry Potter and the Cursed Child, right on the heels of Tom Felton's successful run. With Ron Weasley in tow, he's already fielding questions about whether Emma Watson and Danielle Radcliffe could be next to join the stage play.

The actor, who will reprise his role as Ron for the production, confirmed it would be his last time playing the character. As such, Collider wanted to know if there was a chance of his former famous co-stars joining. Grint didn't say definitively one way or another, but offered up this:.

It would be fun. I don't know. I mean, it's obviously different for everyone. It was an intense time. When we finished, I really enjoyed stepping away and not really even thinking about it, because it was such an intense… I mean, it was enjoyable, and they looked after us, but it was a substantial part of us. So, yeah, maybe. I don't know. It'd be fun.

Industry observers note that I'm sure the last thing Grint wanted to do was try to put the pressure on Radcliffe and Watson to say no, knowing the complicated thoughts both may have about returning. Daniel Radcliffe has been pretty adamant about refusing any opportunities to return, and Emma Watson has shied away from acting so much that there were rumors a few years back that she had retired.

Recent findings suggest that people are always free to change their minds of course, and Rupert Grint is evidence of that. He initially stated he'd only return if everyone else did, and now he's in a position where he's being asked whether his co-stars will join him onstage for Harry Potter and the Cursed Child. He talked about his return and how he felt immediately after the film franchise ended way back when:.

Sources indicate that yeah. It's funny. It's interesting, going back. I spent so much time after finishing Potter kind of moving away from it and doing other things, which I've really enjoyed doing, but I think now it's a very different role in a very different context. And weirdly, it's kind of lined up that I'm the exact age of the character in that story, so it's just felt like a good time.

It does feel like a good time, what with a newly introduced Harry Potter TV show on the way. The series' arrival on the 2026 TV schedule will likely spark even more interest than usual in the franchise, and possibly encourage a lot of millennials craving nostalgia to see Grint back as Ron.

Timing aside, I'm sure it doesn't surprise anyone that actors love to work. For Rupert Grint, the return to being on stage pulls back to his start as a child actor, and that's going to be a great joy for him:.

And I love Latest York and being on stage. It's been a while since I've done that, and it's a very key thing to me. It was my childhood, and I have a very strong connection to that character and that world. I think I'm not going to get many other opportunities to play him again. It probably is my last, and I think it'll be fun.

It should be fun, especially given what Ron Weasley is up to in Harry Potter and the Cursed Child. He's running the joke shop Fred and George founded, while his wife Hermione is the literal Minister of Magic. As far as acting is concerned, it's more of a supportive role, but one that Rupert Grint will likely bring a special sparkle to.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

I'm still waiting to see if Grint, Emma Watson, or Daniel Radcliffe will show up in the Potter TV series. Part of me thinks they'd do it for the fans, but at the same time, I could see them wanting the upcoming cast to have a chance to do their own thing, without drawing attention to themselves. I guess all we can do is wait and see what happens!

Rupert Grint's run on Broadway in Harry Potter and the Cursed Child kicks off on February 2nd and will end on May 30th. I'm sure getting a ticket could be a struggle, but I'm eager to see what the demand will be for fans to see one of the core stars back in the franchise!

#189138. Space station horror-FPS Derelikt is a lively retro throwback to Alien: Resurrection, though it's better at shooting than scaring

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (708 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Space station horror-FPS Derelikt is a lively retro throwback to Alien: Resurrection, though it's better at shooting than scaring

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (708 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I don't expect every PS1-styled, cosmic horror, nakedly Alien: Resurrection-homaging retro FPS to suffocate me under a blanket of misery.
  • Recent findings suggest that still, Derelikt is fortunate that it's a good shooter, as it often gets muddled on whether it wants to be a horror game as well.
  • It turns out Derelikt's derelict dwellers are both perfectly susceptible to mundane lead, and sparing users of ambush tactics at most; several even stand around with their backs turned, as if waiting for you to surprise them with a lethal pipe swing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I'm a reasonable man. I don't expect every PS1-styled, cosmic horror, nakedly Alien: Resurrection-homaging retro FPS to suffocate me under a blanket of misery. Some of the lighter moments in Derelikt, which released last week, even land: I was grinning my cheeks off as I gorged on the Eldtrich knowledge sealed within an alien obelisk, while repeatedly hanging up on the aghast scientist who kept videocalling me to stop.

Recent findings suggest that still, Derelikt is fortunate that it's a good shooter, as it often gets muddled on whether it wants to be a horror game as well. It certainly threatens the spooks, trapping you in an oppressively dingy asteroid rig in the orbit of Saturn - the scariest of the ringed gas giants! - and warping most of the other staff into vaguely echinodemic monsterpeople. Also, opening the inventory reveals it to be made of rectangles, a classic symptom of a video game character about to get mangled in the nerves and face.

But nah, shotgun go boom boom. It turns out Derelikt's derelict dwellers are both perfectly susceptible to mundane lead, and sparing users of ambush tactics at most; several even stand around with their backs turned, as if waiting for you to surprise them with a lethal pipe swing. And, even on Medium difficulty, the opening spell of fight-or-run scarcity quickly gives way to an abundance of ammo and health pickups that can easily fill the pocket grid to bursting. I don't claim to have been playing perfectly, but I'm about halfway through and the only way I see myself running low on bullets is if I start using them to punch the complete works of Thomas Campion into a wall.

Industry observers note that it's indecisive tonally, as well. The dialogue, and there are a fair few survivors to chat with, seems interested in emulating the gravitas-starved, "Woah man" style of New Millennium action game scripts. Which I can sort of see the logic behind, given the visuals and sound design also, and arguably much more painstakingly, mimic that era. But the downside remains that it ends up with a gravitas-starved, "Woah man" style, just with an extra dash of sideways-winking awareness. Again, it only sometimes works, and it's never scary or eerie. But then there are also more earnest attempts to spin uneasiness, with pages of deranged scribbles left behind by the dwindling crew, and at least a couple of genre-classic wall daubings, which tend to leave me wishing developers Visuwyg had just picked a lane.

It has been revealed that again, though, underneath all the smartarsing is a quality little shooter. The retro presentation does little to soften the heavy, industrial kick of its gunfire, and although many of the meatier freaks are more absorbent than they look, their pained thrashing really helps sell the impact of every individual shot. I also don't really mind the lack of Dead Spacey surprise attacks, as the station's narrow confines tend to force you into tenser, close-range encounters in an organic way anyhow.

In a recent development, more impressive still is how Derelikt manages to fabricate a cold, apprehensive atmosphere befitting its fallen space base, in direct defiance of its own quasi-comedic script. This is mainly thanks to the clanging, low-lit station itself, which teases you with just enough flashes of comfort – a stretch of marble floor here, a messy rec room there – to make your quick return to its steel guts feel all the more unpleasant. Some credit must also go to the puzzling, the cardkey hunts and code searches of which initially had me fearful of the more obstinate, opaque, classic horror style preferred by fellow backwards-looker Silver Pines. Instead, it's more like a compacted Deus Ex, hinting at the need to peek at people's computers and scour the environments for the needed codes. Which makes for generally smoother progress, yes, but also gets you more involved and present inside Derelikt's infested walls.

Midway-through impressions, then: it's a little silly, and perhaps a little confused, but Derelikt finds its focus whenever something needs making dead. I shall continue blasting xenos and burning my eyes out with magic rocks until – no, madam, please hold – further notice.

#189137. Latest Update: Infamous GTA 6 leaker CyberLeek is back, and this time the group claims to have leaked a full development build of the game

Latest Update: Infamous GTA 6 leaker CyberLeek is back, and this time the group claims to have leaked a full development build of the game

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (491 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that cyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game launched, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site.
  • Various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB.
  • In a recent development, "It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that cyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game launched, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site. This new leak appears to be making good on a threat posted back in October, where the group stated its intent to release a full, playable build of the game.

Various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB. Eurogamer has seen the site and can confirm this is what the group has claimed, however I have been unable to verify the existence of any actual files. On the site, CyberLeek claims this build is from November 2026 - meaning it is very close to (if not the actual) release build. The 'executable file appears to be missing from the build, however, meaning you cannot actually - yet - get it up and running. CyberLeek is threatening to release this file at a later date, however.

In a recent development, "It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads. "[Cyberleek] holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent. Now. Every file except one. The main executable is held on a countdown." CyberLeek claims the executable will be released earlier than planned if its crypto token reaches a predetermined value. Many of the leaks to date have been related to a CyberLeek crypto scheme. Previously, it was estimated that the group cashed out at least £200,000.

It has been revealed that what does all this mean? There's a very realistic chance that the game could be up and running on PC soon - undercutting Rockstar's unannounced PC release by a matter of months, if current rumours are to be believed. "This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps," the statement continues. "[CyberLeek] told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons.

"If the Xbox build cannot be made to work and support holds, [CyberLeek] will work to get a PS5 build - a fallback, most likely never required. Either way: the Xbox build is going out. No double dipping for Take-Two/Rockstar." It seems these are not empty threats.

Recent findings suggest that cyberLeek has been a thorn in Rockstar's side for a while now. The group initially claimed it took this action in the name of "Gamers' Rights", supposedly fighting for consumers in relation to the controversial discontinuation of game-discs and the digital-only future being pursued by game publishers. Rockstar has previously issued statements regarding the leaker, noting that the leaks are "heartbreaking" and that "this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time". Take-Two tried to subpoena Discord for information pertaining to the leaker's identity.

Stealing the Schafter V12 in GTA 6 is one of the car theft missions you'll have to complete to gain Raul's trust, but similar to the BF Bandito or Declasse Vamos, it's a little tricky. Make sure to grab the silenced pistol from the trunk of the car outside—not necessarily because you'll need it, but because it's a handy weapon to have.

In a recent development, now, as you can see in the video above, you can get into the chop shop by climbing up the van around back and then onto the roof. Recent findings suggest that sneak back towards the centre of the chop shop and turn left to find the Declasse Vamos, a black unassuming car. You also kill everyone inside if you wish, but my way above will get you that non-lethal Criminal Profile rating.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Christoph Hartmann, general manager of Massive Entertainment, claims he wants the Ubisoft division to position itself as the "A24 of gaming.".

Earlier this year, the Star Wars Outlaws and The Division developer's role grew substantially as the existing studio became the lead of one of the five creative houses that Ubisoft divided its studios between following its "major reset." Creative House 2 is Massive Entertainment, which was described as the home of "competitive and cooperative shooter" experiences, including The Division, Ghost Recon, and Splinter Cell.

Speaking to Variety, Hartmann explains, "I want us to be definitely not just a shooter house," citing MOBA title March of Giants as an example. He adds, "I want us to be a label which really looks after the core gamer.".

In a recent development, he explains that the studio is "not going to do" racing, sports, or "casual kids" titles, "But could we do an RPG one day? Could we do MMO? Could I maybe do even a strategy game? Sure." He continues, "If we have the talent internally or something happens, then we bring it on.".

Hartmann indicates his "dream" is to become "the A24 of video gaming." He explains this as "a place I describe with winning Oscars and still being commercially successful, definitely having [an] impact on what they're doing," and calling it the "coolest place" in the entertainment industry.

It has been revealed that ultimately, the key thing with A24 is that the distributor's films weren't overnight hits and it took a while for it to become as beloved as it is. With something like Skull and Bones or Beyond Good and Evil 2, it's hard to imagine those games not having a staggering amount of money spent on them based on their development hell.

The real challenge will be for Ubisoft to not lay off developers at the whiff of failure – or even success, as Ubisoft laid off 166 devs at Assassin's Creed and Far Cry studios last week and on the same day called Black Flag Resynced "among the industry's most successful action-adventure remakes.".

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

A24's biggest hit is Backrooms which made just over $400 million earlier this year, but that was the studio's first film to cross $200 million worldwide, and it took until Everything Everywhere All at Once in 2022 – a decade after it was founded – for a film to break $100 million. And even now there's only been seven movies total by A24 to reach that milestone.

In a recent development, so if Massive Entertainment wants to be the A24 of games, it and Ubisoft need to be realistic about what that means. The old adage of "I want shorter games with worse graphics and I'm not kidding" comes to mind.

Down 1,100 staff in 6 months, Ubisoft dumps its money into gen AI with a whole subsidiary called Motherbrain "focused on AI for gameplay.".

#189134. Breaking: Ubisoft claims Assassin's Creed Jade is still alive as it merges two of its Creative Houses

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Eurogamer ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Ubisoft claims Assassin's Creed Jade is still alive as it merges two of its Creative Houses

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (656 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ubisoft has confirmed that while Assassin's Creed Jade - its mobile entry in the series - is still in development, its focus remains with console and PC.
  • Speaking during the earnings call for Ubisoft's first-half results, CFO Frédérick Duguet said mobile was "still an opportunity for the medium to longer term, with games such as AC Jade on Assassin’s Creed", according to a transcript of the call published by Investing.com.
  • Industry observers note that "Looking at what we can see in terms of long-term financial return, in the mindset of having a stronger focus in terms of capital allocation and financial returns, we consider that we would rather put our resources on bigger opportunities," Duguet mentioned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft has confirmed that while Assassin's Creed Jade - its mobile entry in the series - is still in development, its focus remains with console and PC.

Speaking during the earnings call for Ubisoft's first-half results, CFO Frédérick Duguet said mobile was "still an opportunity for the medium to longer term, with games such as AC Jade on Assassin’s Creed", according to a transcript of the call published by Investing.com.

Industry observers note that "Looking at what we can see in terms of long-term financial return, in the mindset of having a stronger focus in terms of capital allocation and financial returns, we consider that we would rather put our resources on bigger opportunities," Duguet mentioned. "Today, we can say that console and PC remain our core focus for our biggest franchises.".

He added: "The focus is really to make sure that we come with strong growth on console and PC, and notably PC, which is a more dynamic platform than ever.".

Recent findings suggest that ubisoft last confirmed its China-set mobile game was still in the works in March, when it was mentioned in the publisher’s Assassin's Creed: Into 2026 blog. Assassin's Creed now sits within Vantage Studios, Ubisoft's joint venture with Tencent, which rolled out last year.

Industry observers note that ubisoft's results also confirmed some more changes to the way the organization is run, with the publisher saying its fresh operating model is "now fully in place". Creative Houses 3 and 5 have been combined under the leadership of Julien Bares "to leverage synergies between Live experiences across platforms".

It has been revealed that all leadership roles across the Creative Houses are now filled, too. An external general manager has been appointed for Creative House 4 and is set to join in January 2027, though Ubisoft hasn't yet confirmed who. That follows September's appointment of 2K and Amazon Games veteran Christoph Hartmann to lead Creative House 2, home to The Division, Ghost Recon, and Splinter Cell, which was renamed Massive Entertainment at the same time.

Outside the Creative Houses, Motherbrain, the team behind Ubisoft's generative AI experiment Teammates, is now a subsidiary in its own right. It's working on "smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large-scale systemic worlds". A separate unit has also been set up to look after brands that don't belong to any of the Creative Houses.

Ubisoft states the fresh structure is already paying off, pointing to the commercial success of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced and renewed momentum for Rainbow Six Siege, which it says ranked among the top 10 games across Xbox and PlayStation for monthly active customers over the half.

That stated, the publisher nonetheless posted a net loss of €254.5 million for the first half of the year, with net bookings down 16.5 percent to €644.7 million.

The news comes just hours after Ubisoft confirmed 166 job cuts at its Montréal and Québec City studios, the latest in a year of layoffs. They're part of the "major organisational, operational and portfolio reset" that Ubisoft confirmed in January. That initial announcement was accompanied by the news of two studio closures - affecting its Halifax mobile and Stockholm teams - plus the cancellation of six projects, including the much-delayed Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake.

Since then, 105 jobs have been cut at Red Storm Entertainment, the Ubisoft studio behind the Ghost Recon series, and around 380 employees were reportedly laid off when the publisher's Winnipeg and Belgrade teams shut in June. In October, Ubisoft closed Trials developer RedLynx and downsized its Singapore Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced team, impacting a total of approximately 120 employees. Amid all this, Ubisoft developers have been on strike in response to the publisher's sweeping layoffs.

On the weekend, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on a new Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

I Knew Blade Runner 2099 Reviews Would Praise The Visuals, But I’m Surprised By Critics’ Massive Critique

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1067 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cinemablend

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that blade Runner 2099 has arguably been one of the most anticipated titles on the 2026 TV schedule, and there’s a good reason for that.
  • It has been revealed that if there’s anything to know about the Blade Runner universe, it’s that it has major dystopian vibes, and that particular aura is definitely present in 2099.
  • Blade Runner 2099 is a disappointing continuation of the iconic series which leans too heavily into the dark and downbeat side of its future dystopia rather than finding ways to elevate its lead characters in that world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that blade Runner 2099 has arguably been one of the most anticipated titles on the 2026 TV schedule, and there’s a good reason for that. Not only does it expand upon the classic science-fiction franchise, but it also has two capable leads in Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer (who do plenty of stunt work). The show debuts later this week, and reviews are finally starting to roll in. Having seen the show in its entirety for myself, I figured there would be high praise for the visuals, but I am surprised by one particular critique amongst critics.

It has been revealed that if there’s anything to know about the Blade Runner universe, it’s that it has major dystopian vibes, and that particular aura is definitely present in 2099. The series continues to highlight a version of Los Angeles in the distant future that’s far from pristine. Surprisingly enough, though, it seems that the show is proving to be a little too dark for some pundits’ liking. Scott Collura of IGN praises the visual style of the series, though he takes concern with just how bleak the proceedings get:.

Blade Runner 2099 is a disappointing continuation of the iconic series which leans too heavily into the dark and downbeat side of its future dystopia rather than finding ways to elevate its lead characters in that world. Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer are both miscast as a buddy-cop team that subsist on fear and mistrust and angst, while the more interesting characters don’t get nearly enough to do. While the production design, visual effects and overall look of the show are a wonder to behold, 2099 also leans so heavily into its creators’ own fandom at times that it can be distracting.

In a recent development, 2099 – which, of course, takes place 50 years after 2017’s Blade Runner 2049 – sees Replicants having become the ruling class, while humans are treated like vermin. At the center of the story is Cora (Hunter Schafer), a human trying to escape her circumstances by posing as a Replicant Blade Runner. In the process of doing that, she is partnered with Olwen (Yeoh), a dying Replicant Runner. The story does indeed get dark, but I didn’t have much of an glitch with it. As for The Guardian’s Rhik Samadder, though, he indicates:.

Industry observers note that if you’re a cyberpunk who mainlines ennui and likes watching actors you can’t see, speaking words you can’t hear, this show may well knock your fishnet socks off. But why spend this much time immersed in a doomed world, when you could open up a window and watch the real one? It’s live!

Samadder also notably calls the visuals both “impressive” and “oppressive” in a way. However, also mentioning that the series also “plunges us into a far darker world” than the Blade Runner movies (which don’t directly tie into 2099). Likewise, Aaron Pruner of CNET isn’t really a fan of the overly dark setting and aesthetic. In his somewhat mixed review, Pruner praises the show’s execution while also posing this question regarding the bleak vibe:.

It has been revealed that could a little bit of levity help break up the monotony? Possibly. But, again, that would go against the grain of the Blade Runner franchise. And not for nothing, the original wasn’t at all funny, yet nuanced characters like Roy Batty (Rutger Hauer) and Pris (Daryl Hannah) brought life and color to the dreary, rain-slick streets of Ridley Scott’s original.

The darkness doesn’t seem to be deterring everyone, though, as Alison Herman of Variety has glowing thoughts on the show. Aside from praising Hunter Schafer, Herman also admires series creator Silka Luisa’s adherence to this storied continuity birthed by Philip K. Dick:.

Sources indicate that ‘Blade Runner 2099’ dutifully incorporates the franchise’s visual and thematic touchstones. Despite the passage of time, computer screens still have the blocky, vintage look of early PCs; a psychotically violent replicant named Clotilde (Amy Lennox), an early convert to a cult of personality that promises her and Olwen’s kind eternal life, is a clear echo of Daryl Hannah’s cartwheeling Pris from the original film. ‘Blade Runner’ has always hewn to the beats of a detective noir, and over time, has acquired mainstays of its own that ‘2099’ dutifully nods to.

It has been revealed that that’s definitely a big compliment, considering how beloved Ridley Scott’s original 1982 film is and how much critical praise Denis Villeneuve’s 2049 received. Still, not everyone is impressed. TVLine’s Dave Nemetz finds the sci-fi show to be overly bleak as well. Not only that, but he also isn’t too taken with the visuals like a number of others are:.

Industry observers note that we get it: The L.A. of the future is a rough scene. But there's no spark of joy or hope here to offset the bleakness... just more bleakness. ‘2099’ should at least provide some sci-fi eye candy, but the visuals are a disappointing rehash of the sleek, neon-soaked aesthetic of the original ‘Blade Runner.’.

Although I can’t say I saw these critiques about the show’s vibe coming, I can’t blame others for not caring for its dark nature. To me, this kind of style is just baked into the DNA of the franchise, though I can admit that Blade Runner 2099 does delve into murkier territory at times. I’m curious as to how fans will feel when all eight episodes of the show become available for Prime Video subscription holders on November 25.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that valve giveth, and Valve taketh away in their latest Steam Machine availability update.
  • Sources indicate that it's not all bad news, though.
  • One could, with the aid of a Torx screwdriver and a conveniently illustrated guide, work around the 2TB model's lack of existence by nabbing a readily available 512GB Machine and replacing its stock SSD with a chunkier aftermarket drive.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that valve giveth, and Valve taketh away in their latest Steam Machine availability update. The dinky SteamOS PC continues to have a terrible time with AI industry-inflicted hardware parts shortages, which at least for its flagship 2TB model, have become such a problem that Valve are suspending newly introduced orders until further notice. While Valve's post says that they "have wrapped up sending purchase invites out to all remaining 2TB reservation holders" – meaning if you'd previously reserved one, you'll still get your chance to buy – "supply restraints" have put the kibosh on any new orders for now.

Sources indicate that it's not all bad news, though. The cheaper 512GB Steam Machine has achieved "add-to-cart status", which is Valve's slightly odd way of saying you can snap one up without having to join a reservation waitlist. Just like in the Before Times! The post does add that 512GB stock is still limited, so that might sell out too if they can't source enough parts to build upcoming ones, though this is still the first time that the refreshed Steam Machine has been waitlist-free since launching in June.

One could, with the aid of a Torx screwdriver and a conveniently illustrated guide, work around the 2TB model's lack of existence by nabbing a readily available 512GB Machine and replacing its stock SSD with a chunkier aftermarket drive. A not-terrible, budget two-gigster can be had from £240, which when added to the 512GB Machine's £879 outlay, actually works out a little less than buying a 2TB Machine as is. SteamOS is free to download and install, and swapping out the Steam Machine's SSD is considerably easier than the plasticky brain surgery of Steam Deck drive replacement.

Of course, ideally none of that would be necessary, and we could all fill our living rooms with sub-£700 Steam Machines that had never been choked by the greedy hands of industrial-scale RAM hoarders. But that's not the world we live in. Indeed, Valve end the post by rather chillingly suggesting that their hardware prices may rise yet again.

According to recent reports, "We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units," they say, "but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels; as a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them. The 2TB model in particular will be especially constrained.".

"We anticipate having more information to share come January.".

Season 2 of Ace Combat Online begins on 1st December, 2026, and there's plenty of newly introduced stuff for frequent flyers to enjoy.

There are upcoming aircraft, including the Su-30SM -Mihaly- and the X-40 Nightmare.

You can also deck out your F-15C with a upcoming 'Climb King' skin, while the Mirage 2000-5 gets the 'Experimental' skin.

It's not just planes getting new looks; you can kit out your pilot with new clothing and emotes.

Industry observers note that season 2 brings some new missions to Ace Combat Online, too. Co-Op Warfare gets the Kaninfot Valley mission, while Anchorhead Bay has been introduced to Co-Op Assault mode.

On top of all that, there are of course fresh premium and free Ace Passes to progress through, unlocking further cosmetic rewards.

Recent findings suggest that plenty to keep you busy, then. Are you still enjoying Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve? Tell us in the comments section below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, you'll need to find Auntie's Place in GTA 6 once you've get the laptop password to unlock Boogie’s laptop in the Chapter 3 safehouse. The messages that gets you claims there’s a surprise at Auntie’s Place, but there’s no hints as to where that is, and it’s not marked on the map as it’s not a place you can actually interact with.

According to recent reports, to find Auntie’s Place in GTA 6, first head to Twa Ponya Tattoo parlour in the north of Vice City. Then, look across the street and you’ll see a small restaurant with a red sign. This is Auntie’s Place. It’s also around the back of Aline’s Thrift Store, if that helps.

In a recent development, the car isn’t at the restaurant itself. Instead, behind and to the right of it there’s a locked garage. It may have a red car parked outside. You’ll automatically have the code you need to enter if you’ve unlocked Boogie’s laptop and read his messages. If not, you’ll need to head back to the apartment and take a look around for the clues hidden there. If you get stuck, we’ve also explained where you can find them and what words they hint towards.

Inside the garage you’ll find Vanessa's Growler, a pink Pfister (Porsche) sports car. The car will automatically be added to your owned vehicles. You’ll also unlock this garage as a place to store one vehicle. It’s called the Del Rio Boulevard Garage.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • With World of Warcraft: Forever's first raids set to release in early December, developers of the game have spoken about endgame itemisation and their desire to disrupt the "best-in-slot" (BIS) mindset that's been at the core of WoW's progression for years.
  • This information stems from the latest episode of the official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast.
  • According to recent reports, "I essentially want to get rid of BIS," Moon noted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With World of Warcraft: Forever's first raids set to release in early December, developers of the game have spoken about endgame itemisation and their desire to disrupt the "best-in-slot" (BIS) mindset that's been at the core of WoW's progression for years.

This information stems from the latest episode of the official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast. In it, senior game designer Aidan Moon revealed his philosophy around the game's itemisation, which he played - and plays - a major role in designing.

According to recent reports, "I essentially want to get rid of BIS," Moon noted. "I think BIS is not a good thing for a video game that's supposed to be about role-playing. That's why I've introduced the creature subtype system, where things are more effective against murlocs [for example]. We've introduced the biome system too, and in the raid it's different.".

Sources indicate that he gave an example from upcoming raid Barrow Deeps, which will be split into different biomes that offer opportunities for such creature subtype gear to be put to use. "If you go to the left wing that's snowy; if you go to the right wing, that's haunted; if you go down below, that's cavernous. ... I think your BIS should be different for every single boss if you're making a theoretical BIS list.".

In a recent development, moon acknowledged that the system is open for players to interact with to the extent they're comfortable with. Some players might bring optimised gear for certain bosses, while others might not, opting instead for generally good gear to perform well regardless of the fight.

It's an excitingly different approach that goes against the established norms of WoW's endgame raiding. In other versions in World of Warcraft, gear progression is more linear: people go into raids with an idea of what gear drops are best for their character, and intentionally hunt these pieces to replace the set they're wearing. It's a vertical sense of progression. Will theoretically having multiple sets of equipment, for multiple situations, change this?

It has been revealed that best-in-slot gear is an especially pertinent topic in WoW Forever at the moment, given the most dedicated players are reaching max level, or nearing it, and are hunting for items in preparation for the upcoming raid. I'm currently ticking off equipment from a best-in-slot list for a Balance Druid. Whether this player behavior will change when the changes are implemented remains to be seen. Perhaps the approach will expand, with players continuing to hunt down generally accepted 'good' items while also seeking side pieces that provide situational bonuses along the way.

In a recent development, the Blizzard discussion on raid itemisation went beyond standard power items. Chase items, those with especially low drop rates, were also talked about by Moon, noting that Barrow Deeps continues several such items that he hopes will keep players returning to it for years to come.

The items Moon is likely referring to here probably relate to mounts, pets, situational gear, and perhaps campfire bonuses.

For example, I obtained an upgraded campfire earlier in the game that allows a greater campfire to be built that allows more buff items to be placed around it.This has essentially locked me in as a campfire slave for the upcoming raid tier, and valuable to a raid composition.

World of Warcraft: Forever has proven extremely popular since its early November release. The game broke franchise records for Blizzard on launch, and has more weekly players than WoW has seen in 15 years. Judging from early impressions of World of Warcraft: Forever, the game has real merit.

Wild, right? Mr. Ted Lasso himself, alongside two of his co-creators Brendan Hunt, Joe Kelly, sat on the idea for a while until one day they were overflowing with ideas. And then, they sat on it again until this happened. In Sudeikis’ words:.

It wasn’t until Bill Lawrence came to me with an idea for another TV show that I was like ‘Ah, this isn’t the right fit.’ He goes, ‘Well, if you have any ideas…’ I go, ‘Well, here’s a stack of papers of stuff we wrote down.’ And he read it, and was like, ‘Oh yeah, there’s definitely a show here.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Someone, I won't name them just so I don't get them in trouble, once said that EA doesn't shoot you, it puts a gun on the table and then comes in everyday and asks you if you'll shoot yourself, and they just keep coming in over and over until eventually you just are like 'Ugh, fine. Just stop bugging me about it, I'll do it.' And so the reality is that EA can legitimately say 'we didn't make BioWare do this, they chose to do this', but if you dig underneath that statement the reality is that the options on the table were all terrible. We chose the least terrible of the options." Via an interview with Pembridge.

Last month we got the devastating news that BioWare, the legendary studio that brought us Mass Effect, Dragon Age, and classics like Neverwinter Nights, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, and the OG Baldur's Gate was being shut down. The decision was made by EA, just a year after it was acquired by a consortium made up of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and investment firms Silver Lake and Affinity Partners (owned by the son-in-law of US president Donald Trump, Jared Kushner).

The reasons? Underperforming games. Dragon Age: The Veilguard didn't hit the mark, Andromeda wasn't well received, and Anthem, the live-service shooter, shut its servers down for good earlier this year.

Industry observers note that it's a bad string of events for sure, but former Dragon Age boss Mark Darrah doesn't believe that it's all down to BioWare's poor management. The studio was backed into a corner by EA and the pressure to perform.

Decisions like using the Frostbite Engine, "making Dragon Age 2", and "shipping Anthem" were all products of BioWare needing to hit financial targets set out by EA. "They basically noted 'Gotta hit your financials, so what are you going to do?' Darrah claims. "'Are you going to ship KOTOR a year sooner than you think is going to happen? No. Are you going to pull Mass Effect in a year? No. It was never clear what the consequence of 'no' was, and it still isn't. But it seemed really dire at the time. So you gotta do something, so what are you going to do? Did they make us make Dragon Age 2? No. But they made us do something.".

Ubisoft have revealed their Motherbrain. It's far less cool than it sounds. Rather than being a giant floating slab of thinky meat that can do telepathy, Motherbrain is a studio dedicated to doing development stuff with generative AI. As you might expect, it consists of the folks who worked on Ubisoft's "first playable generative AI experience".

Sources indicate that motherbrain's reveal as "a dedicated subsidiary focused on AI for gameplay innovation" came via Ubisoft's latest earnings report, where the company trumpeted that their "latest operating model" is "now fully in place". The model is the reorganising into creative houses responsible for different game series that Ubisoft announced at the start of this year, with leaders for all of the houses now arranged.

"We have also established Motherbrain, the team behind our first playable generative AI experience Teammates, as a dedicated subsidiary developing proprietary technologies for gameplay to empower creators and open up new possibilities for richer, more immersive and engaging player experiences," CEO Yves Guillemot mentioned.

It has been revealed that you'll never guess what his next few lines were. "We remain on track with our cost reduction program, reflecting our commitment to a focused and disciplined organization as we are preparing for a significantly stronger content cycle," the exec noted. "In parallel, we have made progress on our refinancing plan with the objective of securing competitive terms and putting in place an efficient medium-term plan over the coming months.".

Recent findings suggest that that'd be the wave of layoffs and closures Ubisoft have been rolling out all through this year, most recently getting rid of 166 staff at Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec, both of which worked on Assassin's Creed Shadows. Ubisoft Singapore and Trials developers Redlynx, Ubisoft Winnipeg, Belgrade, and Barcelona, long-time Tom Clancy studio Red Storm, Ubisoft's Paris HQ and three German studios including Anno devs Ubisoft Mainz are all on the list of bits of the company affected in some way by the cuts.

Changes to remote working policies have also contributed to strikes at Ubisoft studios in France and Italy.

Ah well, at least there's seemingly money there to support the developing of those proprietary technologies infused with genAI brainiacery.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia has reinstated its disgraced former CEO and leather jacket collector Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and director of its board, according to a press release today.

Huang, who co-founded Nvidia back in 1993, was forced to resign from his positions at the organization earlier this month, after it came to light he had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman named Alice Huang, a former executive at Singaporean tech firm Megaspeed International who was suspected by US intelligence of being an asset of the Chinese Ministry of State Security. Huang also reportedly carried out two additional affairs with Nvidia employees.

According to recent reports, he was replaced by Nvidia CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. The Nvidia board initially responded to pressure from tech industry leaders to bring Huang back with a statement that he would not be reinstated. He has now been reinstated.

"Nvidia today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board", confirmed the corporation in a press release. "The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia.

According to recent reports, "In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk". Huang has a close relationship with US president Donald Trump, and Trump has backed calls for Huang's reinstatement.

Markets were unhappy with Huang's dismissal earlier this month; when it was announced, Nvidia shed billions of dollars in market value as traders adjusted to the prospect of a future without his leadership. The announcement of his reinstatement has sent Nvidia share prices skyrocketing by over 30%.

Recent findings suggest that "I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution", said Huang. Meanwhile, Nvidia has formed "a committee comprised solely of independent directors to investigate" Huang's affair with a possible Chinese intelligence asset and states that "investigation will proceed to conclusion.".
