📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When we think of secrecy surrounding movies, naturally we think MCU, but the amount of secrecy that went into The Odyssey is insane. While I knew everything about it was kept under wraps, I didn’t realize just how much until I heard John Leguizamo’s story about landing the script, and it’s WILD.

Recent findings suggest that the actor portrays Odysseus's blind and devoted servant Eumaeus, a role that has been largely praised by critics. Turns out, Christopher Nolan knew exactly what he was doing when he cast Leguizamo in the part, and he didn’t even need to eat dessert first. The actor has previously gushed about working on the movie and the amazing shooting locations, but now he’s dishing to Kevin McCarthy on his On Film podcast about the Mission Impossible-level secret keeping that went into keeping the script under wraps:.

I would go to lunch at Odeon, his favorite restaurant. So we meet. He talks about the character. First of all, he talks about his career and everything. So that was just amazing to sit with him and hear him talk about his career was incredible. And then he says, ‘I have this role for you. It's one of the most loyal characters in Western literature.’ And I was like, ‘Wow, that's a lot to live up to.’ He goes, ‘Yes.’ And I was like, ‘I'd love to do it if you'll have me.’ He offered me the role right there before dessert.

Industry observers note that leguizamo’s performance as Eumaeus has been called “sublime” by critics, and it’s easy to see why Nolan thought he was the right fit. Though the actor understands there’s a certain scene in the movie that earned him some hate for “the rest of cinema history,” and if you’ve seen it, then you know what he’s referring to. The actor didn’t even know the extent of his part until he got the script, which came to him as a top secret mission fit for James Bond:.

Industry observers note that A week later after we close the deal. I have to be home at 12:00 on a Tuesday to receive the script. Nobody else can receive it. I have to receive it. Sign for it. And it comes in a blood red color that you can only see, you know, during a full solstice. [laughter] I don't know. It's impossible to see, dude. The black ink is shiny, and the red makes it so you can't copy it. But it's hard to read. It's really difficult to read.

In a recent development, perhaps Marvel needs to take some notes from Nolan. While this seems like an insane level of secrecy for a book to screen adaptation, I admire the commitment to "no spoilers." Though the journalist asked the most important question, who delivered the script? Surely, FedEx wasn’t tasked with such a feat. Turns out one of Nolan’s personal assistants hand delivered it. However, there was still another step for him to be able to keep the confidential script:.

That's given to me, and I'm not allowed to share with anybody. My assistant had to sign an NDA.

The cloak and dagger seems to have worked as not even Tom Holland seems to have leaked anything. Additionally, Leguizamo shared that whenever Nolan made tweaks, the actor would have to turn in the old pages. This was definitely a first in his career, but one he feels was completely worth it, and I have to agree as the actor seemed to easily embody the role.

It’s not easy to bring an epic of this scale to life, and it was clear from the get-go that Nolan had a vision. Now that The Odyssey hit the 2026 movie schedule over the summer, the actor can focus on a different role. Though maybe one that doesn’t come with as much secrecy? Leguizamo will reprising his role as Sid the sloth in the upcoming 2027 movie, Ice Age: Boiling Point, which is set for a February 5, 2027 release.

Sources indicate that someone should ask him if he was given the Ice Age 6 script in red. Regardless, I’d love to hear his co-stars take on the spy antics it took to keep the script out of the wrong hands.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As unveiled in a statement by Arika president Akira Nishitani (and translated by Time Extension, thank you), Akira Kurabayashi, a director at the combined dev/publishing studio and a creator whose work spans three decades and several genres, sadly passed away as a result of heart failure late last week.
  • Kurabayashi initially worked as a programmer on smaller titles at Taito, including early 2.5D fighting game Fighters' Impact (later localised as VS.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As unveiled in a statement by Arika president Akira Nishitani (and translated by Time Extension, thank you), Akira Kurabayashi, a director at the combined dev/publishing studio and a creator whose work spans three decades and several genres, sadly passed away as a result of heart failure late last week.

Kurabayashi initially worked as a programmer on smaller titles at Taito, including early 2.5D fighting game Fighters' Impact (later localised as VS. in America). He then moved to Arika in 1996 and continued his work in 2.5D fighters with the Street Fighter EX series, a subseries which took the originator of the fighting game genre into the third dimension for the first time. While that subseries didn't last long, its spiritual successor Fighting EX Layer made waves in 2018, bringing back original characters from SFEX and even including Fatal Fury's Terry Bogard.

Fighting EX Layer started out as an April Fools' joke back in 2017, but the reaction to the trailer from fans who missed the SFEX series convinced Arika to bring the series back, even without the Capcom IP. The final result is an interesting 2.5D fighter that combines conventional mechanics, such as magic series combos and supers, with the unique (for better and worse) Gougi system, where of in-match perks are chosen from a deck of cards at roundstart. I had a good time playing it for its systems (and Terry is very fun in it), but the Gougi system brought to mind Street Fighter x Tekken's infamous paid Gem debacle, which no one should be reminded of. Anyway. In addition to 2.5D fighters, Kurabayashi also contributed to Tetris: The Grandmaster, Tetris 99, PAC-MAN 99, and ARIKA's collaboration with SNK in the form of their 'SNK Revamp Project'.

Nishitani gave a few personal words towards Kurabayashi in the statement:.

Recent findings suggest that "We are deeply saddened to have lost a dear colleague who has created numerous works with us and supported Arika for many years. We express our heartfelt respect and gratitude for his immense achievements to date, and we will cherish and carry on the skills, experience, and attitude toward game development that he left behind. I would like to express my deepest gratitude for the kindness you showed us during their lifetime, and I respectfully pray for the repose of their soul.".

Condolences to Kurabayashi's family.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The GTA 6 Declasse Vamos is a stunning pillarbox red muscle car that Moses wants you to pick up for him as one of the many side quests available in GTA 6. While some of Moses' targets are easy in-and-out type situations, others are a little trickier, and the Declasse Vamos heist, located just north of Grayson in South West Lummox County, is one of them.The GTA 6 Declasse Vamos itself is located in a locked garage next to a very interesting shack whose owners apparently love stealing a road signs. This is your hint to finding the garage door code, though it's not as hard as the mess of signs might make you think, as I'll share below.

The code for the garage in which you'll find the GTA 6 Declasse Vamos is 2727, as you can see on a couple of small tin signs mounted on the interior walls of the shack.

The entire building is covered floor to ceiling in metal signs, but if you have a good look around, there are at least two on the walls that feature this four-digit code, indicating that this is the number you need to gain access to the Declasse Vamos.

Recent findings suggest that there are two residents here who'll be standing in your way, but now you've got the code, you could just stealth straight to the garage door, as this code is the same for everyone, unlike some of the GTA 6 safe codes. If you want to complete the mission yourself fully, though, you can knock out or kill the NPCs before entering the house and finding the code. As ever, there are a few items to pick up here, too, but it's not much.

For help on getting hold of some other GTA 6 cars, check out my guides on the GTA 6 Fast and Furious car, inspired by Paul Walker's (Brian O'Conner's) Mitsubishi Eclipse, the BF Bandito, which is another of Moses' targets, and Vanessa's Pink Porsche, the Growler, which is a secret find you can keep for yourself or sell on.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is estimated to have sold nearly 25 million copies in one day, generating approximately $2.5bn in sales revenue - a staggering result that's beyond even what even observers were predicting.

The estimates come from data-tracking firm Sensor Tower (spotted by VGC), which has been watching GTA 6 pre-orders closely for weeks, updating estimates daily based on (unspecified) data that it collects.

Recent findings suggest that should the results be accurate, it'll dramatically eclipse GTA 6's $1bn in three days result. It'll also put GTA 6 on track to reach the eye-watering $3.25bn to $5.2bn week-one sales estimates for GTA 6.

So far, Rockstar has said nothing in relation to GTA 6's sales since the game was released around the world yesterday. Parent tech giant Take-Two has said the game's pre-orders were tracking "well above expectations, and GTA 6 broke pre-order records on both the PlayStation Store and the Xbox Store, though, so all signs point to a record-breaking release. The question is "by how much?".

Reaction to GTA 6 has been glittering. Chris awarded GTA 6 five golden stars in Eurogamer's review, calling it "a game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale". "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

More than 39 million unique owners have played Grand Theft Auto VI on PlayStation 5 as of November 22, making it the biggest launch in PlayStation history across three decades and five console generations, Sony Interactive Entertainment announced.

The sequel set a newly introduced record for the highest number of concurrent players for any game on PlayStation, surpassing previous records across multiplayer, free-to-play, and single-player titles.

Across PlayStation 5, players cumulatively logged 683 million hours of gameplay in Grand Theft Auto VI, and have spent an average of 17.4 hours exploring the game’s world during its opening days.

According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto VI‘s launch also marked the largest number of newly connected PlayStation 5 consoles on a single day since the console’s launch, outside of end-of-year holidays. Since launch, it was the first played game on 70 percent of upcoming PlayStation 5 consoles.

Industry observers note that “We want to congratulate our partners at Rockstar Games for bringing this extraordinary game to players around the world and continuing a partnership with PlayStation that stretches back to Grand Theft Auto III on PlayStation 2,” Sony Interactive Entertainment content communications manager Tim Turi said. “With [Grand Theft Auto VI], we worked to bring the best experience on [PlayStation 5] and gave players a memorable way to commemorate the game with two special limited-edition DualSense wireless controllers inspired by Vice City. We also celebrated the launch with live events including Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival in Miami this past weekend.”.

Sources indicate that grand Theft Auto VI  launched for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series on November 19. On November 20, Rockstar Games announced that the game achieved $3.79 billion in day one retail sales following 32.5 million pre-sales. Although Rockstar Games did not share exact unit numbers, the revenue total suggests roughly 37.9 million to 47.3 million copies sold, based solely on pricing across its $79.99 and $99.99 editions.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that for the past six years, the team at RPS have got together to pick what we consider to be the best 100 games you can play on PC.

  • We've just finished revealing what we at the moment consider to be the Best PC games of all time and now it's your turn.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that for the past six years, the team at RPS have got together to pick what we consider to be the best 100 games you can play on PC. There's very little science involved, and we try not to get too hung up on what games should make the cut. From year to year, our rankings and choices vary wildly as the formation and tastes of the team changes.

In a recent development, however, our definitive list isn't always met with a chorus of approval and cheers of 'Hear, hear!', "'Well done!', and 'Couldn't have said it better myself!', so we also have the RPS 100: Reader Edition. This is your chance to submit your ten favourite PC games of all time. Your votes will be tallied up with all the other submissions from our other readers and we will produce a list of the community's top 100.

We've just finished revealing what we at the moment consider to be the Best PC games of all time and now it's your turn.

Using this very Google Form you can submit up to ten votes for your favourite PC games of all time. I will then tally them up with all the other votes from RPS's readers and produce a list of the community's top 100.

Now, a note on scoring. The game you put in 10th place will be awarded one point, 9th place will be worth two, 8th place will be worth three, and so on until you reach your top pick, which will be worth ten points. Please write the full game name (and include the year of release if there are multiple titles in a series with the same name, such as Doom (1993) and Doom (2016)). If in doubt, check how the game is titled on Steam.

Last year, I implemented a change to create a greater variety of games on the list. I combined series scores, so if one reader voted for Civilization IV and another voted for Civilization VI, the scores of both were combined and the entry would be for the Civilization series. I also shared the breakdown of the votes for each title in the entry, so you could see which was most popular within the series.

Industry observers note that I will be doing the same again this year, as we saw a lot more games that wouldn't have made the cut otherwise. However, I will try to do a better job of separating out games that are very different from one another even if they are in the same series. Warcraft 3 and World of Warcraft are both Warcraft games, but, admittedly, they aren't similar games. I would ask for some leeway on this, though, as not every example is clear cut. Should Alpha Centauri be counted among the Civilization games? Are Final Fantasy XIV and Final Fantasy Tactics - The Ivalice Chronicles truly worlds away from the other games in the Final Fantasy series?

It has been revealed that this does also mean that one-shot games can struggle to compete against games which are part of longrunning series. After all, Crimson Skies isn't just competing against Microsoft Flight Simulator (2020), it is competing against votes for any and all Microsoft Flight Simulator games ever released. Unfortunately, this is a cost of the system, but I prefer the variety that comes from seeing more games represented instead of several separate entries for games within the same series.

In a recent development, we also invite you to tell us why you've chosen each game. This is entirely voluntary, you can simply enter the game titles if you would prefer. However, I'll choose a selection of what readers have mentioned about winning games so we can better understand why the RPS community loves these games. Try not to write any more than 100 words. If you have more to say you can always drop it in the comments of the list when we publish it at the end of the year.

To cast your votes, please make sure you complete this form by 5pm GMT on Sunday, December 6th.

Thanks again, and happy voting!

Breaking: I Analyzed the Seven Biggest AI Chatbots to Determine How Safe They Are for Kids

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1820 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • AI safety for both adults and children is under greater scrutiny than ever before, with a growing number of questions and concerns appearing around how beneficial or otherwise these conversational bots actually are for our mental well-being—even without considering their energy use, ethics, or economic implications.
  • The big AI apps, such as ChatGPT and Gemini, are right in the center of these trends, and the companies behind them are taking steps that they promise will keep children safe.
  • Recent findings suggest that openAI's ChatGPT has one of the more comprehensive setups in terms of parental controls.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI safety for both adults and children is under greater scrutiny than ever before, with a growing number of questions and concerns appearing around how beneficial or otherwise these conversational bots actually are for our mental well-being—even without considering their energy use, ethics, or economic implications. At the same time, an increasing number of apps and services are becoming age-gated in a growing number of countries around the world, as governments realize that letting kids loose on AI apps, social media platforms, and the web at large might not be the best idea for their ongoing development and prosperity.

The big AI apps, such as ChatGPT and Gemini, are right in the center of these trends, and the companies behind them are taking steps that they promise will keep children safe. If you want to know what youngsters in your family may be getting exposed to, and what you can do about it, here's the rundown.

Recent findings suggest that openAI's ChatGPT has one of the more comprehensive setups in terms of parental controls. The minimum age for people is 13, and if you're under 18, you need to have parental consent to open an account—age is predicted via several signals, including what times of day you use ChatGPT and what you talk about.

Accounts for under-18s automatically become ChatGPT for Teens accounts. There's more of a focus on learning and study (with a dedicated study mode), as well as "age-appropriate safeguards to help reduce exposure to sensitive or potentially harmful content." There are built-in protections for "harmful topics," including sexual, romantic, or violent roleplay, graphic violence, and self-harm. These work on top of the safeguards for all consumers that limit chats about physical harm and illegal activity.

These ChatGPT for Teens accounts can also be linked to a parental account—but while parental consent is required for under-18s to use the service, ChatGPT clearly says that teens do have the option to break the link if they want. If you do persuade your kid to keep your accounts connected, you can set time limits on when the AI bot can be used, and tweak some of the sensitivity settings. However, you can't view any conversations.

To set up parental controls from ChatGPT on the web, click your profile icon (bottom left), then Settings > Parental controls > Add family member and follow the instructions. It's also worth bearing in mind that ChatGPT app can also be used for free, anonymously, in any web browser, though OpenAI indicates users accessing the AI this way are subject to the default under-18s limits (and can't save chats or access an archive).

Gemini is tied into everything else Google does, and follows the broader rules for Google accounts: No under-13s, unless you're part of a family group and using an account managed by an adult. You can manage your family through the Family Link portal on the web, though as far as parental controls specific to Gemini go, you can only enable or disable access to the AI (settings like screen time apply across all enabled apps).

For all under-18s (partly identified through age estimation), whether or not they're part of a managed family group, Google applies some additional protections. They include preventing the AI from taking on a persona, guarding against emotional dependence on the AI, and discouraging bullying and other forms of harassment. There are also safeguards to limit chats about age-restricted substances like alcohol or vapes, and mental health complications like eating disorders.

These protections for minors are applied in addition to the usual guardrails in Gemini for everyone. The guardrails should lead you away from conversations about self-harm, suicide, violence, and illegal activities, and offer quick links to support in times of crisis. However, Google itself admits that these filters aren't perfect.

In a recent development, as with ChatGPT, there's a loophole of sorts in that anyone can start chatting with Gemini, for free inside a web browser, with no checks at all. These conversations can't be saved and come up against usage limits fairly promptly, but they're only protected by the general restrictions for all accounts, not the ones specific to minors.

It has been revealed that meta AI will show up in several apps that young people and children are likely to use, including WhatsApp and Instagram, as well as having its own separate app on the web and on phones. The standard restrictions for Meta's social media accounts apply to its AI too: A minimum age of 13, and restrictions for all under-18s. Like many other platforms, it uses some AI magic to flag up accounts being used by minors.

If you're under 18 and on a Meta Teen account, you'll come up against blocks if you try to get Meta AI to engage in sexual or romantic roleplay, or discuss alcohol or substance misuse. Chats on topics such as eating disorders and self-harm will prompt the AI to offer guidance towards relevant support services.

According to recent reports, meta offers a comprehensive parental control setup for its apps, including Meta AI, but connecting a parent account isn't compulsory for teens. This is handled through the Meta Family Center portal, and parents can get reports on the general topics that kids are chatting about with AI—though they don't get the exact transcripts or prompts. Any self-harm or suicide discussion can trigger an alert to the connected parent account.

All owners, under 18 or over 18, get support and crisis intervention responses when chatting about suicide and self-harm, and there are strict limits on discussing illegal and harmful acts, including drug use and cyberbullying, as well as sexual and adult content.

Recent findings suggest that apple users have to be 13 or over to have an account, which is required to access Siri AI—anyone younger needs to have an account created for them by an adult, and these accounts can only get at the basic, older Siri. Date of birth must be declared when opening an Apple account, with tighter checks rolling out in many parts of the world.

Anyone over the age of 13 can have an Apple account and use the Siri AI app, with or without a connected parent account, as it stands in most U.S. states. This means the well-being safeguards are essentially the same for teens as they are for adults: There are safeguards around self-harm, suicide, sexual and violent content, and illegal commands. It's one of the more conservative AIs when it comes to what it will talk about.

Industry observers note that the fresh and improved Siri AI can be managed to some extent by the new parental controls available in iOS 27 and Apple's other software updates for 2026—Apple has clearly seen the way the wind is blowing—but this is optional for teens. It depends on whether or not you can corral your kids into a Family Sharing group.

According to recent reports, if your teens are in your family group of users, then the standard Screen Time rules apply for controlling app usage limits and device access (in iOS Settings, tap your name, then Family to get at them). There are also options for disabling certain Siri AI features, such as the writing tools or the image creation capabilities.

Like Gemini/Google and Apple/Siri, Copilot is tied into the wider Microsoft ecosystem, and access for under-18s can be managed through it. Consumers must be 13 or older to hold a Microsoft or a Copilot account—and again, there's some underlying tech in place to detect anyone who might be deliberately lying about their age.

If you've got a teen using Copilot, you can manage their access through the standard Microsoft Family Safety portal. You're able to enable or disable Copilot access, set times during which Copilot can and can't be used, and disable certain features like image generation or voice mode. Parents can't read the Copilot chats of their kids, though.

Parental supervision is optional—a teen aged 13–17 can use Copilot without linking their account to an adult one. Microsoft indicates users identified as under 18 won't see personalized results or ads, and will get age-appropriate responses regarding risky or harmful content, though there's not much detail on what that entails.

Industry observers note that more generally, content around self-harm, violence, adult content, harassment, and harmful or illegal activity is banned on the AI platform. Any prompts about suicide or drugs will bring up support options rather than answers, whether you're an adult or a young person using the service.

Ultimately that means that minors have the same access to Grok as adults, if they want it—an AI platform that combines "weak safety guardrails" and "a range of extremely harmful content" that includes "explicit sexual content, mental health risks, violent content, and inappropriate responses to... offensive content" (that's the Common Sense Media Report again).

Yes, this is the AI chatbot that has previously had a problem with deepfake porn imagery, and which has traditionally taken a rather casual attitude towards safety concerns, led by SpaceXAI CEO Elon Musk. While illegal and harmful content is supposedly banned from Grok, its own FAQs admit that certain chats can result in "dialogue that may involve coarse language, crude humor, sexual situations, or violence.".

There is actually a Grok Kids Mode that limits the kind of content that can be shown and the conversation topics that can be added, but it requires customers to self-declare themselves as minors and is easy to bypass. The advice from Common Sense Media seems to be the way to go with Grok: Do not let your teens access it.

Claude's approach to child safety is straightforward: You can only register for an account if you're over 18. It is possible to lie about your age when signing up, but like the other platforms, Anthropic looks at various "signals" in behavior to spot minors—if your account gets flagged, you have to verify your age using an option like face age estimation or Yoti.

There's no free web access to the chatbot, like there is with ChatGPT and Gemini, so if you're under 18, you're locked out from the service unless you know the behavioral tricks to get past Claude's detection systems.

In terms of more general well-being protections on Claude, any chat around self-harm or suicide will guide consumers towards helplines and other resources for support. Conversations about illegal activities, disallowed speech, and explicit sexual content are banned from the platform. In recent months, Anthropic indicates it's also reduced AI sycophancy.

That's something of a whistle-stop tour of the big seven AI chatbots, but if you're a parent, it should give you some idea of what's out there and how easy it is to access. Besides the parental controls built into these AIs (or not), you also have the settings available at the platform level—Android, iOS, Windows, macOS—to restrict the use of any potentially harmful apps.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There is perhaps nothing so brutal in a Total War game than getting an army full of elite units wiped out, and it appears that pain remains a factor in the upcoming Total War conversion of : Warhammer 40,000. Creative Assembly also has some nifty ideas around breaking the game into mini-campaigns for each star system you visit.

In an hour-long deep-dive livestream of Total War: Warhammer 40,000, developer Creative Assembly demonstrated the game in action, focusing initially on how armies navigate from planet to planet. Each star system apparently acts as a "contained campaign" you can hop between in the game.

The star system the stream focused on is Praevoss, a mid-sized collection of planets: three of which you can land on and fight on, while the others are smaller and unable to support your tactical warfare shenanigans. Once you're finished with a star system, you move on, carrying over units and unlocked skills.

It has been revealed that "First and foremost, we want to represent the scale of the whole galaxy, which is just not possible on a single Total War map," Creative Assembly explained on the livestream. "You'd never be able to engage with it. Part of the point is to break this up a bit and allow us to have some more interesting and more bespoke narratives going on. So each of these star systems has a premise, has a narrative, has a specific setup, a specific start, [and] specific victory objectives that you've got to go and do.".

One of the objectives highlighted in the livestream was an Ork Scourge, which required the player - controlling Space Marines - to hold the planet while eradicating the Ork presence.

Recent findings suggest that as you can imagine, much of the stream was dedicated to the fleet of spaceships at your disposal - fleet movement and management, and the abilities they provide to your armies such as orbital bombardments. There was also detail on how ships transport troops, as well as the upgrades you can build to further enhance their power.

On the topic of transporting troops, the developers focused on the small number of expensive but powerful Space Marines they controlled. These Space Marine armies come with a potentially "devastating" cost if you mess up and lose your armies during one of the star system campaigns.

According to recent reports, "Losing a whole army of Space Marines is pretty devastating," the developers explained. "That's intentional, as that's a whole Space Marine chapter. Like, losing an army of Space Marines, that's a massive deal for them. It would take them decades to recover from that.".

Total War: Warhammer 40,000 is set to release some time in 2027, though no specific date has been established as of writing. Much has been seen at this point on its gameplay, galactic or otherwise. As we near the end of the year, fans are clamouring for official word on when they can take to the stars.

With James Gunn and Peter Safran’s exiting DC, it's unknown if the DCU will continue or if we can expect yet another reboot. However, with one chapter closing for the studio, the start of a newly introduced might mean some long-gestating projects could get a second chance. Amid the corporate change, people have been asking about Keanu Reeves' long-discussed Constantine sequel again, and honestly, I don’t hate the possibility of seeing the 2005 movie finally get a follow-up.

Industry observers note that A Constantine sequel has technically been "in the works" since 2022, and at the time, it was reported that writer Akiva Goldsman was working on the script. Director Francis Lawrence has been committed making another flick centered on Reeves' DC character, and he previously confirmed the leading man was "excited" about the idea. While there was a positive update in 2025, news has been scarce since then. Yet, when the director spoke with Collider about Sunrise on the Reaping, he gave John Constantine fans some hope:.

Well, I’ll tell you this. Not that I want anybody to lose their jobs, so this is not like a schadenfreude kind of thing, but I will say that we’ve been trying to make Constantine 2 for 20-something years, and we have an idea, and we have a script, and we’ve been wanting to make it, and the people that were at DC were an impediment to us making it. So, we are now more hopeful as of yesterday’s news that maybe now there will be another opportunity.

This is sure to be music to some fans' ears amid the major corporate shift. Jeremy Latcham, a Marvel Studios alum who worked with Gunn on Guardians of the Galaxy, is stepping into the role of DC Studios CEO. As a result, Gunn’s DC universe might be over, and Lawrence -- who's sympathetic to the exiting CEOs -- seems to be confident that this could open the door for a Constantine sequel.

In a recent development, of course, Lawrence is also upfront about having no idea what the studio has planned. For all he knows, they could want a different John Constantine for a shared universe. With that in mind, he’s also perfectly fine if the studio want to do a latest take and allows him to make a sequel to HIS version with Reeves. In Lawrence's mind, two iterations can co-exist.

Recent findings suggest that at this point, Francis Lawrence has made it clear that the project is further along than fans think, as they have a script ready to go. The only obstacle in his way is a thumbs up from the powers that be:.

But again, we’ve been trying to make this for 20-something years, and there’s always been obstacles in the road to making it, and it’s not me, it’s not Keanu, it’s not Akiva. J.J. [Abrams] is on it, as well. We all want to do it. So, it’s really going to be people at Paramount, Warner, whoever’s running DC now, getting everybody on board to say, like, 'Hey, we can do a sequel of our version of Constantine.'.

Recent findings suggest that 2005's Constantine has earned quite the cult following. Believe it or not, Reeves wasn’t fans' first pick for the role, and that's because of how much of a departure from the comics his take on John is. The character has lived on in the live-action space since then, with Matt Ryan taking on the trench coat in 2014 for a short-lived NBC show. Ryan continued to portray Constantine in The CW’s Arrowverse and voiced the DC antihero in various animated works through 2024.

Sources indicate that however, a portion of fans still seem hopeful that Keanu Reeves will get another chance to play the character, and I’d love to see him back in the role. Considering Reeves' skills as an actor and his love for John, I have no doubt he can slide right back into the role. We'll have to play the waiting game on that front, though, as DC Studios has yet to reveal any new looks that will follow James Gunn and Peter Safran's departures.

According to recent reports, how long it takes you to beat GTA 6 is going to depend a lot based on how you play it. It's a huge game, so don't expect to get it done in fewer than 40 hours, but you might be able to get somewhat close to that if you're really rushing. However, for most GTA 6 players, completing open world activities and exploring is going to take up lots of time outside of doing main missions, so you're looking at putting in well over 50 hours to roll the credits. If you want to know more, I've broken down the length of GTA 6 in more detail below with some estimated completion times.

According to recent reports, playing all GTA 6 missions across the game's five chapters is a big undertaking that will keep you occupied for many hours. The writer of GamesRadar+'s GTA 6 review, Josh West, reckons it will take most players anywhere between 60 and 80 hours to complete the main story and roll the credits.But that's still assuming you're doing some open world exploration too, and, from my experience, it's often impossible to avoid that. In fact, the amount of time spent engaging with extra activities will have a big impact on your final time, which should be around these estimates depending on how you play:.

It has been revealed that if you're solely focused on the main story and getting it done quickly, you can shave off quite a lot of time, even getting below 50 hours. Bear in mind that you'll be missing out on quite a lot of the game by playing this way. A significant part of the fun of GTA 6 is cruising around Leonida and doing all sorts of activities and bumping into bizarre encounters.

On the other end of the spectrum, if you're fully or even just partly committed to attaining 100% completion of GTA 6, you will be spending well over 100 hours playing. There are tons of side-mission chains to complete, unique activities to participate, and collectibles to find all over the map, so finding all of that, even with help from out GTA 6 guides, is a mammoth undertaking.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ooh, an Nvidia-related story that isn't about their now former CEO allegedly getting amorous with someone.
  • As noted by PC Gamer, reports of driver 621.24 writing more than it should to SSDs have popped up across various forums and Reddit.
  • It has been revealed that some instances of the bug, which doesn't appear to be affecting everyone, have the driver writing up to 30GB every hour.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ooh, an Nvidia-related story that isn't about their now former CEO allegedly getting amorous with someone. I wonder what it's abou-oh. Oh no. It looks like Nvidia's latest GeForce driver, 621.24, is needlessly writing vast amounts of data to PC SSDs.

As noted by PC Gamer, reports of driver 621.24 writing more than it should to SSDs have popped up across various forums and Reddit.

It has been revealed that some instances of the bug, which doesn't appear to be affecting everyone, have the driver writing up to 30GB every hour. For context, it'd take a bugged driver writing that much thousands of hours to break a gaming SSD with a typical endurance rating in the hundreds of terabytes. However, that doesn't mean this is anything less than a pretty bad bug. As such, reverting to the previous driver, 621.01, is a good idea if you're on 621.24 and suspect it of writing chunks of gigabytes to your SSD.

According to recent reports, in order to check if that's going on, open task manager, head to the 'details' tab, right click on the column header, click 'select columns', select 'I/O write bytes' from the menu of check boxes that brings up, then look for 'NVDisplay.Container.exe'. The number next that exe is in bytes, so you'll need to do a bit of maths to work out if it's writing mere MB or globs of GB.

Bizarrely, the affected 621.24 driver still hasn't been pulled by Nvidia as of writing, meaning it can still be downloaded by people who might not be aware of any issues and think 'ooh, haven't checked I'm on the latest driver in a while.' The driver was released on November 12th, so it's not a brand new arrival that the organization just haven't had a chance to look into yet.

According to recent reports, here's hoping that it is fixed or replaced ASAP, if it hasn't been by the time you read this. AMD look to have dealt with a similar issue recently, and I'd like to think driver updates across all cards aren't going to be some form of permanent Russian roulette going forwards.

While there's still a lot we don't know, there are tools to help track flights at this time:.

There are a number of options for tracking flights, whether you have your flight number or not. If you have the flight number, the fastest method is to Google it: Google will display a live tracker of your flight at the top of the results page. You can also head to the airline's official website to track your flight: United Airlines, for example, has a flight tracker where you can either enter your route information or your flight number. Most, if not all, airlines will have a similar tool you can use.

Alternatively, you can use a site or service that tracks all flights. FlightAware is one such site and has a flight tracker that lets you search flights—so long as you know the origin and the destination. If you have the flight number, your iPhone can help: You can enter your flight number into Spotlight search to see a live tracker, or you can text a contact your flight number, then tap the link that appears under the number to see a tracker of the flight.

At this time, the exact reason isn't totally clear. According to the agency, “The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports following communication issues impacting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers,” but the FAA hasn't said what caused those communications issues or when they expect to lift the grounding. The grounding order comes one day after a massive Microsoft outage that disrupted service for people of Outlook, Teams, and other Microsoft products. It also comes one day after Ars Technica reported that the FAA was rolling out an AI-powered tool to help manage air traffic across the country.

Sources indicate that this is only the third time in U.S. history that the FAA has made such an order—once after 9/11, and again in January of 2023 due to a pilot alert system problem; the latter ground stop lasted around 90 minutes.

Sources indicate that grand Theft Auto 6's seismic launch has registered on a governmental level. A spokesperson for UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has hailed the game as a "British success story", but confirmed Burnham himself won't be playing it. His diary is apparently "very full".

In a recent development, "Rockstar Games is a British success story made in Edinburgh," a Downing Street spokesperson told The Independent - referencing the series' Scottish origins and ongoing development at Rockstar North - "and many fans are already saying GTA has been worth the wait." When asked if Burnham will be making time for GTA 6, the spokesperson responded: "His diary is very full. He won't be playing it.".

Downing Street went on to address the issue of teenagers potentially skipping school to play the game, emphasising that children "should be in classrooms" this week because "every day in school matters".

It has been revealed that the leader of Labour's opposition, the Conservative party's Kemi Badendoch, recently expressed similar concerns. "I know people are worried about the game content," she wrote. "At the same time, I'd be more worried about a kid who played it all day, who was in their bedroom all day, than one who spends half-an-hour on it and then went out and did something else.".

GTA 6's culture-shaking success was unlikely to pass without reference by the government, but the celebratory tone is a marked departure from Burnham's predecessor Kier Starmer calling Rockstar's firing of 34 staff last year "deeply concerning". We are awaiting a verdict in the resulting employment tribunal related to it.

Recent findings suggest that this state recognition of GTA 6 is not without precedent. It wasn't long ago that French President Emmanuel Macron congratulated Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 on its award-winning and heart-winning success. That game sold 8 million copies in one year; GTA 6 is estimated to have sold 25 million copies in one day.

GTA 6 has been hailed as a generational release - an exorbitantly luxurious game that "pushes back the horizon of video games", Chris Tapsell wrote in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

Amazon Fire TV Soundbar Plus is down to $139.99 from $249.99, and the extra money over the base model gets you a dedicated center channel that helps make dialogue easier to follow, along with a built-in subwoofer, Dolby Atmos, and DTS:X support. That stated, it doesn’t have up-firing drivers, so the Atmos effect stays largely horizontal, but the center channel does real work on mumbled dialogue in prestige dramas. As with the base model, this one also handles audio only and needs a Fire TV device for any of the streaming features. This PCMag review has more detail on how it performs.

Sources indicate that amazon Fire TV Soundbar with Alexa Voice Remote Pro is $109.98 (was $154.98). This pairs the entry-level bar with the upgraded remote, which adds backlit buttons, two customizable shortcuts you can set for favorite apps or Alexa commands, and a remote finder (for when it inevitably disappears into the couch). If you don’t specifically want or need the remote, though, the Soundbar Plus is a more capable soundbar for just $30 more.

Amazon Fire TV Soundbar Plus with Subwoofer is $229.99, down from $374.99. This configuration takes the same 3.1-channel bar and pairs it with a separate wireless subwoofer, which gives bass-heavy scenes and film scores considerably more weight than the bar's built-in woofer can manage on its own—and at $90 more than the discounted Soundbar Plus, this is the option I'd consider if fuller bass is a priority. This is the complete 5.1 package, adding two rear speakers to the 3.1 bar and wireless subwoofer, so action scenes and other surround effects come from behind you, rather than only from the direction of the TV—but it costs $120 more than the discounted soundbar and subwoofer bundle, so it’s worth considering how much you want that surround-sound effect. Also, while the rear speakers connect to the soundbar wirelessly, each still needs a power outlet.

Nioh 3 downloadable content “Bloody Insurrection” will launch on December 17, and a Nioh 3 Complete Edition featuring the base game and both downloadable contents will launch for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, and PC via Steam and Microsoft Store on January 28, 2027, publisher Koei Tecmo and developer Team NINJA announced.

Nioh 3 first launched for PlayStation 5 and PC via Steam on February 6.

Here is an overview of the downloadable content and Complete Edition:.

In Bloody Insurrection, a Shogun Meets His End in Shimabara.

While pursuing the Spanish alchemists, Takechiyo learns that the source of Yui Shosetsu’s regrets lie in the Shimabara of the past. Guided by Shirogarasu, they transcend time once again, this time arriving in Shimabara in 1638. There, a battlefield where rebel forces, alchemists, and yokai join forces to wage a fierce and bloody struggle against the shogunate army. To uncover the source of the conspiracy, Takechiyo ventures deeper into the heart of Shimabara, encountering a host of latest figures along the way, including Amakusa Shiro, leader of the rebels; Tachibana Muneshige, a legendary warlord who survived the Warring States period; and a samurai who fights back against the alchemists.

Shimabara in 1638. Rebels have risen up against the tyranny of a local warlord and now clash against the shogunate forces sent to suppress them. Alchemists operating in the shadows and countless yokai join the fray, turning the conflict into a brutal, blood-soaked war. Takechiyo must navigate the various landscapes of Shimabara in the battle-fraught castle town, the vast underground caverns beneath Mount Unzen, and the rebel stronghold in Hara Castle.

Fierce Battles Against Storied Characters and Upcoming Yokai.

According to recent reports, takechiyo encounters Amakusa Shiro, the leader of the rebel forces, along with the legendary warrior Tachibana Muneshige, and the samurai who fights against the alchemists. Figures from Hell Rising make a comeback in this newly introduced story, and new yokai stand in Takechiyo’s way. There are also some familiar faces among the Guardian Spirits who lend Takechiyo their power.

Upcoming Customization Elements and Endgame Content.

New Martial Arts are being added for each weapon type, along with numerous Transformed Arts, Ninjutsu, Onmyo Magic, and Summoning Seals. If players have both the first and second downloadable content and manage to complete Enlightened One’s Journey (the third playthrough), they will be able to unlock the new difficulty mode and fourth playthrough, Nioh‘s Journey, where players will find equipment drops of the highest rarity, Ethereal. This will take character customization and endgame challenges to the limit.

Fresh Content: The Battlefield of Carnage.

In a recent development, A high-volume form of endgame content, the Battlefield of Carnage, awaits players in this downloadable content. Players will need to fight their way through battlefields teeming with enemies, defeat the boss of each floor, and press onward through a relentless series of battles.

Sources indicate that each floor of the Battlefield of Carnage consists of a field divided into multiple war fronts. Defeat the boss controlling each war front to gain battlefield effects that provides an advantage on each floor.

Battlefield effects include steady stat boosts and other special effects. Depending on the player’s character customization, these special effects can create unexpected synergies and enable them to deliver overwhelming performances. Players are free to choose the order in which they conquer the war fronts and when to challenge the floor boss. The map provides information on the types of war front bosses and details about battlefield effects, so the player will need to devise a strategy best suited to their playstyle and character.

In addition, defeating formidable enemies on the battlefield will enable players to further strengthen equipment shrouded in traces of the Yokai Realm, which can only be obtained and generated in the Battlefield of Carnage.

Defeat the floor boss, purify the Yokai Realm, and seek out the most powerful equipment you can find. The ultimate challenge awaits, offering the hard-earned satisfaction that can only be found within Nioh.

Latest Guardian Spirits, skills, Martial Arts, Ninjutsu, Onmyo Magic, Graces, and more.

#189092. Breaking: World of Warcraft: Forever review: The first proper MMO adventure I've been on in years

Breaking: World of Warcraft: Forever review: The first proper MMO adventure I've been on in years

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (3096 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, PC Gamer's got your back Our experienced team dedicates many hours to every review, to really get to the heart of what matters most to you.
  • Sources indicate that world of Warcraft: Forever has, much as the original World of Warcraft did back in 2004, completely consumed my life.
  • Industry observers note that what is it?: A reimagining of 2004's World of Warcraft, with new balancing, lighting, dungeons, and items.Expect to pay: A monthly subscription of $14.99/£10.99.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A hopeful rebirth for the old-school MMO formula.

In a recent development, PC Gamer's got your back Our experienced team dedicates many hours to every review, to really get to the heart of what matters most to you. Find out more about how we evaluate games and hardware.

Sources indicate that world of Warcraft: Forever has, much as the original World of Warcraft did back in 2004, completely consumed my life. I write about games for a living, mind, so the attention vortex it has wrought upon me is primarily professional obligation, rather than just irresponsibility.

Industry observers note that what is it?: A reimagining of 2004's World of Warcraft, with new balancing, lighting, dungeons, and items.Expect to pay: A monthly subscription of $14.99/£10.99. Optional race and early-game zone behind a £25.99/$30 paywall.Developer: Blizzard EntertainmentPublisher: Blizzard EntertainmentReviewed on: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060, AMD Ryzen 7 5800 8-Core Processor, 16GB RAM, Force MP600 SSDMultiplayer?: YesLink: Official site.

But at the time of writing, it has been 443 hours since Forever's launch. I have spent 147 of those hours asleep (less, but let's just pretend I've been getting a solid eight), leaving around 296 hours of my waking mind. 230 of them have been spent playing World of Warcraft.

It has been revealed that that's a deeply concerning amount of time if I wasn't getting a salary to review it—it has been part of my 9-5. I've also often been keeping the game open while I, you know, feed and bathe myself and do chores. So we're probably just in the realm of 'moderately worrying' rather than 'cause for a wellness check'.

Don't worry, I intend to take a break soon: But during those 230 hours, I have hit level 60, entered 31 dungeons, completed 941 quests, levelled engineering, mining, and first aid to 300, and apparently /waved at other players 50 times. Which are rookie numbers that I need to get up.

But I've also found myself taking in the scenery, laughing at my poor luck at bottles, whining about the drop rates of basilisk brains, splitting mining nodes with party members, mercilessly grinding ogres into paste for my first mount, and talking to more strangers while questing than I have in years of playing more modern, streamlined MMOs.

I'm not pointing this out to simply cast aside the role of nostalgia in my enjoyment, but I do think nostalgia can only carry an attention span so far. It certainly doesn't keep 230 hours of medically inadvisable gameplay afloat on its own. There's something else going on here; something special that's been unearthed.

All of the things that made an old-school MMO like the original WoW so deeply enthralling back in 2004 are not simply dated, to be cast aside as an inferior form of videogame.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

The crappy drop rates, the fighting over tags, the running everywhere (there is so much running everywhere) while not always justified, is part of an experience that's stronger for its inconveniences. The friction burn you get from jutting up against a game that's occasionally just hostile to you. All of that connects you to the world, and the people in it, in a very real way.

Sources indicate that first, I want to talk about what Forever itself has actually brought to the table. After all, much of what I've talked about already has been reverence paid to a series of design decisions that were made over 20 years ago.

In the here and now, though, Forever has around 1,000 new quests (the original WoW is estimated to've had somewhere in the mid-2,000s, so that's approximately 30-50% more Warcraft), nine new dungeons, and two new major levelling zones in Mount Hyjal and The Riverglades.

To encourage and support levelling alts, Blizzard's added a upcoming mechanic in the Legacy tree—a genuinely cool feature that encourages you to level alts (or do endgame achievements and raids) to unlock perks, like making levelling slightly easier by giving you a small heal when you kill an enemy in the open world, or by giving you more resources when you gather things.

Then there's the retooled class and item balance, the latter of which is my one, very mild point of disappointment: There's an increasing amount of trinkets and weapons I've kept around for specific use cases, sure, but at least while levelling, the fantasy of equipping an anti-worgen sword to do some worgen-killing quests (as so often quoted in Blizzard's promotional material) hasn't quite panned out. That's not to say it's gone by the wayside completely, though.

It has been revealed that I've seen a two-handed axe that lets you get mining nodes, a knife that lets you skin humanoids, gloves that increase your mining skill, boots that let you walk under water, and so on. It's just not a core part of the levelling experience.

It does also improve somewhat when you get into the later levels. For instance, I now have a two-handed questing sword green that I'll keep in my bags basically forever because it lets me spin around like a propeller to slow my fall speed: And I'm a Warrior, so that's a hugely useful traversal tool for someone without any way to slow fall.

Professions have also had a total facelift, and for the first time, I'm actually levelling crafting and gathering skills on my characters because of it.

Not only do crafting ones like blacksmithing actually give you really good gear as you level up (rather than just a couple of significant capstone items) but all professions can now turn in writs and crates, buying new recipes via the latter and unlocking them with a rep grind via the former.

Sources indicate that the new zones are both excellent—the Riverglades is pretty, but not out of place, whereas Hyjal is a satisfying (and very efficient) climb up a mythological mountain ruined by war, with some legitimately cool questlines to it. In both, questing is enough of a breeze that it does feel almost too easy, with Hyjal smoothing over the typically arduous 58-60 grind completely. But they're not any more efficient than, say, The Burning Crusade's better zones, which is a level of kayfabe-breaking I can get behind.

But until you hit that point, Forever's newness is downright subtle. A chain here, a few fetch quests there. Just enough to make questing in every zone worth it, just enough to even out the occasional, clunky speedbumps.

With Riverglades being level 38, and Mount Hyjal not mattering until the final stretch, Forever partially buries the lede, and you'd be forgiven for thinking it a touch unambitious. But with Blizzard's commitment to add new Riverglade-style zones and questlines to the game in the years to come, it's going to keep morphing into something new with the passing years, and what's there—when you get to it—is plainly impressive.

According to recent reports, such as Forever's fresh dungeons. I've done seven out of the new nine crawls, and while they're a little more mechanically dense than the vanilla predecessors (bosses sometimes have like, two moves) I've been fascinated by just how well that old-school design has been emulated.

With the exception of Alcaz Island, these things are sprawling, time-consuming romps. And, while controversial, the changes to dungeon XP (putting the majority of it in their quests while lowering the amount you get from mobs) has made completing them an adventure.

I recently knocked out Sunken Temple's questline, but the world-trotting, multiple quest-chain journey to get all my pre-requisites had me doing another unrelated dungeon a second time, fighting my way to the top of a troll fortress in the Hinterlands, helping out a drunk dwarf, and speaking to the spirit of a fallen Horde warrior to get his hipflask.

Industry observers note that so when it was time to finally darken the door of the Sunken Temple and get it all done, I felt accomplished. Like I'd not just rocked up to a portal to get some fat loots, but that I'd actually—like an adventurer might—spent considerable time researching, preparing, and bracing myself for the place.

Didn't stop us forgetting that the Shade of Eranikus summons all the right now-alive dragon adds to him and getting absolutely mauled, but hey-ho.

Sources indicate that more to the point, my XP reward for that journey felt considerably far more potent than if I'd simply hopped in there to rinse it 5 times. And I might have skipped it if the XP reward wasn't mostly dispensed via questing. I won't say dungeon XP isn't an issue for some players, but for me, the exercise works.

There hasn't just been an RTX-on style filter slapped over Azeroth, this is all bespoke.".

And while you're running around the world, forced to jog ignobly between major locations, Forever's new lighting system and draw distance shines through. The reason these lighting changes aren't in retail yet is because, primarily, they're hand-crafted.

Durotar has these darling oversaturated blue shadows, Felwood bathes everything in a sickly green, Duskwood's mist hangs thick in the air, and the lightning that crackles over the Blasted Lands actually casts electric blue light across the stones of Nethergarde Keep.

Industry observers note that but there are subtle changes, too. You can see Nordrassil, the world tree at the top of Mount Hyjal, from Durotar—as well as other zones on the continent. Dun Morogh and Winterspring have uniquely hostile snowstorm blizzards that cut out visibility entirely, similar to Tanaris' sandstorms.

There hasn't just been an RTX-on style filter slapped over Azeroth, this is all bespoke, and it's made all of my journeys that much more atmospheric. I've had to stop just to take in the godrays pushing through the canopy of Ashenvale, or the burning sunset descending on the seas of Stormwind Harbor.

More importantly, these effects really pull out the strengths of that old-school mode of design. Both the 2004 version of World of Warcraft and Forever understand that in order for a world to feel massive, it needs to be difficult to traverse sometimes. In order for it to be social, there needs to be a level of unfairness that being social will overcome.

I thoroughly enjoyed World of Warcraft: Midnight, the latest expansion in modern World of Warcraft, when I reviewed it for launch. I thought the questlines, which I can remember the glossy cinematics and major storybeats of, were engaging enough. And I still think its upcoming revamped Silvermoon is gorgeous, and a complete flex from the studio's art team.

Recent findings suggest that I could not, however, tell you a single thing about my questing experience that wasn't dictated to me by the game. Yes, I liked certain story beats or character conversations, but the actual experience of hitting stuff? It's a blur. I flew somewhere, I pushed my buttons, I interacted with something. I flew somewhere else, and you know what I did there? I pushed more buttons.

In contrast, I've been playing Forever for almost three weeks, and I've already made memories. On a jog to an annoying Scarlet Monastery dungeon questline that sent me to Desolace, I met up with two dwarven brothers (or husbands? They had the same second name) who were making the journey. We joined up with more people to kill a bunch of high-level skeletons, and barely got through an overpull by the skin of our teeth.

Recent findings suggest that in Stranglethorn Vale, a kindly shadow priest six levels higher than me partied up to kill some pirates, then pointed out that there was a good questline that could be done by scavenging beach bottles. They got theirs on their first try. I, for some reason, had to pick up 26 of the damn things.

Sources indicate that on another journey, I decided to try and grab my fire-hardened mail armor for a warrior questline, which sent my alliance character all the way into The Barrens, to Razorfen Kraul. This is not a great dungeon to do if you're an alliance character, so the pickings were slim. Which meant that I not only tanked the whole thing as Fury, but that the folks I was with were chill enough to do a quick road-trip to Feralas with me to get another dungeon quest.

Recent findings suggest that the point being, I only had these memorable experiences and spoke to these people because I was being, and I know this is a bad word for a lot of MMO players, inefficient. Absolute bastard questlines made me do something far out of the way. And every single time I've played along, I wound up having a lovely time meeting similarly stubborn folks and making new friends.

Recent findings suggest that A lot of these inconveniences, carried over from vanilla and left alone in Forever, are there to push you and people you meet organically, out in the world, into close quarters and camaraderie. To do "kill X" quests, you need to intentionally party up with that random night elf warrior, rather than just pass them by. To get certain questlines accomplished at the level they're given, you need to ask for help in general chat.

Some chains will send you to some random city, forcing you to learn the most efficient boat route to get there—or to simply leave that quest in your log until you next happen to pop your head into Darnassus. The travel time makes the world feel substantial. The encouraged cooperation makes it feel alive and social. And all that friction produces friendships—these quests suck to do on your own but are so often a breeze to do together. Or, at the very least, they're more entertaining with company.

Industry observers note that this is why it doesn't just feel like nostalgia to me. It's the rub of the whole thing. I am not enjoying these quests because, at some time in the past, I had a nice innocent memory surrounding them that I'm reliving. It's actually all about what's happening in the present: Grouping up with people, striking up conversations, sharing in misery as it takes a full 45 minutes to fill our bags with pirate hats.

I'm honestly just marvelling about the fact that, in 2026, that this sort of design still works. It works tremendously well. Blizzard's latest campfire mechanic, which I like a lot, is just a cherry-on-top-nudge towards striking up the conversations I was already having anyway.

In a recent development, so many times, my purposefully chill vibes have been met with genuine kindness: People stay on to help you finish quests they've already completed, they show you upcoming questlines. Sometimes it's a tit-for-tat. A shaman helped me out with my level 50 warrior quest in exchange for me helping him kill an elite somewhere, which hey, fair dos.

This all culminated in an incident where I joined in for a random kill quest in my mid-40s. A priest, around their mid-40s as well, commented that man, a lotta folks had their mounts already! Myself included. I'd spent a few hours mining over 200 Iron Ores and killing cave ogres, like a maniac.

I asked how far off they were. They remarked they had 80 gold out of 90. I threw 15 gold at them before I realised what I was doing.

This isn't to humblebrag, mind. My grinding had produced a surplus of cash that I wasn't really spending: But it was like I'd been suddenly possessed by the spirit of Christmases past, future, and present. I gave a complete stranger a significant amount of money with the complete understanding I'd never talk to them again. Because I felt like being nice, because so many people had been nice to me.

I do understand the yearning for flight paths, for lower respec costs, for shared mob tagging, and for quests that don't require your character to walk the circumference of the earth. And if none of that's to your taste, then hey, fine—but more than anything, Forever's proven to me that those flying mount doomers back in The Burning Crusade might've been onto something.

In a recent development, I still enjoy 'theme park' MMOs, but Forever is such a deeply exciting prospect to me. It's a second chance for this older, slower, more social form of videogame to have a renaissance. Before booting up Forever on November 4, I couldn't tell you the last time I had an adventure (an organic one, not one delivered to me through a storyline) in an MMORPG. Two weeks later, and I've had several, and I keep logging on and embarking on these long, arduous quest chains because I'm excited to have more.

It has been revealed that forever is such rare air. A major MMO studio has been given the blessing to revamp a 20+ year old version of a game and add to it. And while it's already added a considerable amount, Forever feels like proof that, given enough exposure in the spotlight, people could actually like a new MMO with its design sensibilities.

And as a fan of lots of different kinds of MMOs—be they slow-paced adventures like Forever or on-rails dungeon-rinsing theme parks like Final Fantasy 14—I want this genre to have the kind of actual diversity it deserves. More MMOs than World of Warcraft should get to take this sort of risk. More MMOs should be able to take it slow.

Until that upcoming game comes, however, I'll happily play Forever, and I cannot wait to roll up an alt to start doing it all over again.

A hopeful rebirth for the old-school MMO formula.

Industry observers note that harvey's history with games started when he first begged his parents for a World of Warcraft subscription aged 12, though he's since been cursed with Final Fantasy 14-brain and a huge crush on G'raha Tia. He made his start as a freelancer, writing for websites like Techradar, The Escapist, Dicebreaker, The Gamer, Into the Spine—and of course, PC Gamer. He'll sink his teeth into anything that looks interesting, though he has a soft spot for RPGs, soulslikes, roguelikes, deckbuilders, MMOs, and weird indie titles. He also plays a shelf load of TTRPGs in his offline time. Don't ask him what his favourite system is, he has too many.

Warning! The following contains spoilers for the 90 Day: Hunt For Love episode "The Boy Who Left His Mark." Stream the episode with an HBO Max subscription, and read at your own risk!

Sources indicate that after their confrontation was shown in the previous episode, 90 Day: Hunt For Love finally revealed Razvan Ciocoi's removal from the spinoff. I have mixed feelings about how it was handled, and questioning whether it was the best way for this to be shown to viewers.

In a recent development, for those unaware, Razvan was removed from 90 Day: Hunt For Love after he allegedly used a racial slur to refer to Jamal Menzies during their argument. Rather than show the incident, the 90 Day Fiancé show decided instead to flash the following text onscreen before moving on to the next day:.

Razvan was asked to leave the retreat due to a code of conduct violation.

The scene then switched to Iris meeting up with the other 90 Day: Hunt For Love singles and explaining that he left. There was no discussion about what happened, and it was more to state that Iris was "back on the market" with her match gone. Had someone watching only learned of the incident from the 2026 TV schedule, they wouldn't have known what happened.

90 Day: Hunt For Love Has Me Wondering If Brittany Intentionally Sabotaged Michael's Love Life.

I don't know all the context that went into this decision, but I can already see some problems with it. To start, I don't think avoiding what happened with Razvan is going to dissuade viewers out of the loop from looking up what happened. He was a prominent part of 90 Day: Hunt For Love up to this point, and I think his absence will be felt.

On the same token, there's a discrepancy on whether or not the event in question happened. Razvan has denied it was ever uttered, and if there was evidence to the contrary, TLC opted not to show it. Additionally, no one spoke about the incident beyond Razvan being gone, so it's still up in the air beyond TLC's statement.

In a recent development, I also would be willing to cut the franchise some slack, had it not just based an entire storyline in a previous spinoff on a racially insensitive remark by Shekinah Güven. 90 Day: The Last Resort dove deeply into her telling Thaís Ramone to "go back to her country," and even addressed it again at the tell-all special without her being present. So, I doubt the incident was a bridge too far by the show's standards, which makes me all the more curious why it was sidestepped.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

In a recent development, the questions and drama will continue on 90 Day: Hunt For Love on TLC on Mondays at 8:00 p.m. ET. Despite this unfortunate moment, I'm still enjoying this season and wondering which couples will link up at the end of it all.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fuse Games, the developer of Star Wars: Galactic Racer, has mentioned it "didn't dream" the pod racing game's background character Biddy Blas would become as popular as he has.

Recent findings suggest that since Galactic Racer's release in October, Blas - who resembles a short, humanoid crocodile (officially a crocin) - has become a viral sensation. The combination of his unexpected swagger and ridiculous high-pitched Huttese monologues - performed irresistibly by actor Richard Summers-Calvert - have made him a fan favourite, especially his catchphrase "scrib doon" (which means "write it down").

"Here's a name for you, amateur!" Blas tells the player upon meeting them, albeit in Huttese. "Biddy Blas. Write it down. Tattoo it on your arm, and someday your arm will be worth millions!".

According to recent reports, fuse Games shared a comment from Biddy Blas creator and Galactic Racer narrative designer Ren Alex-Rose about the character's success. "We always suspected Biddy Blas would be a popular member of the Galactic League, but we didn't dream of just how popular he'd become," Alex-Rose remarked.

"He was an incredibly enjoyable character to build, from our early ideation of a small, angry non-human character (who we lovingly referred to as our cast's 'chaos goblin') to recording his sometimes-absurdist dialogue with Blas' voice actor, who took the crocin to a whole new level.

Recent findings suggest that "It's been great watching Biddy Blas emerge into his assured self, as well as seeing the community embrace him for it. He's always known exactly who he is, and he wears it proudly.".

Blas' breakout success was praised by Lucasfilm producer Craig Derrick, who mentioned his social feeds were filled with posts about Galactic Racer, though mostly about Biddy Blas. And the enthusiasm actor Richard Summers-Calvert was greeted with during October's MCM Comic-Con in London, which I attended, was palpable. There's a nice video of him doing Blas' voice on Instagram.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer was awarded a full five stars in Eurogamer's review. "Both a surprisingly fun Roguelite campaign and a racing treat for Criterion fans, this is just wonderful stuff," wrote Christian Donlan.
